$CEG KEY READ-THROUGHS FROM CONSTELLATION ENERGY’S Q3 2026 EARNINGS CALL

Constellation’s call strengthens the investment case for existing generation, nuclear refurbishment and integrated capacity solutions more than it supports an indiscriminate power-infrastructure spending boom. The central development is the ability to combine existing electricity production with targeted additions of capacity, storage or demand response, thereby monetizing assets without constructing an entirely new baseload plant for every new customer. This favors companies controlling operating generation, customer relationships and flexible demand. It creates a competitive hurdle for development-stage nuclear projects whose economics depend on customers having few alternatives. The most actionable read-throughs concern NRG’s demand-response platform, Vistra and Talen’s remaining contracting opportunities, and Siemens Energy’s verified nuclear-turbine exposure. Customer benefits are also tangible, but power procurement should not be confused with permission to energize data centers or immediate cloud revenue. Peer disclosures available through November 9 are incorporated below to distinguish incremental information from developments already reported.

MERCHANT POWER AND DEMAND FLEXIBILITY

NRG’S CUSTOMER AND DEMAND-RESPONSE PLATFORM BECOMES MORE STRATEGICALLY VALUABLE (READ-THROUGH 1)

Affected company: NRG Energy (NRG: United States).

Directional impact and magnitude: Positive. Potentially material to long-term commercial differentiation and contracted growth, but no directly quantifiable near-term EPS increase follows from Constellation’s announcement.

Call evidence: Constellation signed a 20-year, 270 MW Peak+ agreement combining existing nuclear output with new generation and demand response. Dominguez explained that its retail platform provides relationships with customers that can curtail, and that the solution can range “from zero capital all the way to the capital one would need to deploy for storage solutions.” He also highlighted the opportunity to replace short-duration demand-response incentives with payment streams lasting 5-10 years or longer.

Transmission mechanism: This validates the strategic value of NRG’s ownership of CPower, acquired with the LS Power generation portfolio in January 2026. CPower gives NRG an established commercial and industrial demand-response platform rather than merely an option to develop one. Multiyear commitments from large electricity consumers can support payments to existing customers for installing controls, changing operating procedures or making other investments that enable reliable curtailment. NRG can monetize the resulting flexibility through aggregation, optimization and integrated electricity supply, potentially reducing the capital required to serve incremental load.

The less obvious implication is that customer access and dispatchable demand can become valuable complements to generation ownership. Constellation’s willingness to evaluate returns across an entire customer solution indicates that an otherwise marginal capacity investment can be attractive if it unlocks a larger supply agreement. NRG has a comparable ability to combine customer relationships, generation and demand-side resources, although it does not automatically capture the clean-nuclear premium discussed by Constellation.

An important current-perimeter check strengthens this conclusion. NRG’s separately published November 9 results announced a $4 billion sale of 4.9 GW of generation but explicitly stated that the company retains the entire acquired PJM portfolio and CPower. The proposed divestiture therefore does not remove the assets most relevant to this read-through.

Timing and limitations: Near-term catalysts are additional integrated supply agreements and evidence that regulators accept the associated demand-response capacity. The fundamental benefit accrues over several years through contracted commercial margins and more capital-efficient load growth. Existing demand-response commitments cannot simply be relabeled as new capacity, and customer compensation, accreditation and performance penalties determine the retained margin. Constellation’s transaction is evidence that the commercial structure can work, not an award to NRG. NRG had already released Q3 results on November 9, so this is not a pre-earnings read-through.

EXISTING NUCLEAR OUTPUT CAN BE CONTRACTED WITHOUT EXHAUSTING THE UPRATE PIPELINE (READ-THROUGH 2)

Affected companies: Vistra (VST: United States) and Talen Energy (TLN: United States).

Directional impact and magnitude: Positive for long-duration contracting opportunities and earnings quality. Potentially material for assets that remain available for new agreements, but limited as an immediate 2026-2027 earnings catalyst.

Call evidence: Constellation added approximately 4,560 MW of agreements after its previous quarterly update, including nearly 3,500 MW from existing generation. Management rejected the proposition that contracting opportunities end when available uprates have been sold. Dominguez stated, “They were never the only pathway for contracting.” The company retained its illustrative $20-$50/MWh premium range above the PTC-floor reference.

Transmission mechanism: The Peak+ structure demonstrates that incremental capacity can be sourced separately from the existing clean generation being monetized. That expands the potential customer set for merchant nuclear owners. A generator does not necessarily need an additional reactor uprate for every new nuclear supply contract if storage, demand response or another qualifying resource can satisfy the customer’s capacity obligations.

Vistra has already demonstrated the core customer appetite through its Meta agreements covering 2,176 MW of existing output and 433 MW of uprates. Constellation’s additional contribution is evidence that other contracting structures can extend the opportunity beyond uprate-linked packages. For Talen, the opportunity is particularly identifiable: its November 3 call disclosed approximately 300 MW of uncontracted Susquehanna nuclear output alongside battery development and other new-capacity options. Constellation’s transaction validates a commercial approach directly relevant to that remaining inventory.

The magnitude must be calibrated to available output rather than total nuclear capacity. Talen’s approximately 300 MW opportunity is not its entire nuclear fleet, and contracted output cannot be sold again. Similarly, Vistra’s already-announced Meta economics should not be counted as new upside because a competitor has executed another agreement.

Timing and limitations: Near-term trading support comes from reduced concern that regulatory uncertainty or limited uprates prevent further transactions. The stronger fundamental effect is additional contracted earnings beginning later in the decade and reduced exposure beyond the current nuclear PTC period. Vistra reported on November 6 that approximately 98% of expected 2027 generation and 78% of 2028 generation were hedged. Those energy hedges constrain immediate exposure to changes in market prices, although they do not determine the treatment of capacity revenue.

There is also a competitive offset: Constellation’s approximately 113 million MWh of remaining marketable clean generation represents a substantial alternative supply pool for customers. The call supports the existence of premium contracting demand, not unlimited pricing power for every nuclear owner. Vistra and Talen had already reported Q3 results, making this corroboration of their longer-term opportunities rather than a new forecast of quarterly earnings.

NUCLEAR-OWNING UTILITIES

PSEG HAS ATTRIBUTABLE UPRATE UPSIDE, BUT THE OPERATING READ-THROUGH IS NOT UNIFORMLY POSITIVE (READ-THROUGH 3)

Affected company: Public Service Enterprise Group (PEG: United States).

Directional impact and magnitude: Positive for longer-term nuclear investment and contracting opportunities. The identified uprate is modest at the consolidated-company level, while the broader nuclear contracting opportunity is more consequential. Near-term operating risk remains adverse.

Call evidence: Constellation described nearly 1,200 MW of uprates, approximately $4.3 billion of investment and strong customer demand for existing and incremental nuclear output. Management emphasized that earlier public investment figures included both license-extension work and uprates, rather than uprates alone.

Transmission mechanism: PSEG is an actual co-owner of assets within the relevant regional nuclear investment opportunity, not merely a utility exposed to the same theme. Its November 2 presentation disclosed a planned approximately 200 MW Salem uprate, of which approximately 112 MW is attributable to PSEG. Successful development would increase PSEG’s saleable output and provide another potential basis for long-term customer agreements.

The attributable amount is approximately 3% of PSEG’s roughly 3,758 MW nuclear portfolio. It is therefore inappropriate to assign PSEG the entire Salem uprate or a proportional share of Constellation’s overall $4.3 billion program. The larger potential value lies in demonstrating that existing nuclear production can be contracted above the company’s reference economics while supporting continued operation and investment.

Constellation’s customer agreements also do not automatically transfer their pricing to PSEG. Co-ownership establishes an economic interest in plant output and investment obligations; it does not establish entitlement to another owner’s customer contract. PSEG must monetize its own output under its own commercial arrangements.

The critical negative qualification is operating performance. Constellation’s reported 97.2% quarterly nuclear capacity factor excludes Salem and South Texas Project. PSEG’s Q3 filing separately disclosed degradation of the thermal shield at Salem 1, with testing expected to extend the refueling outage. Consequently, Constellation’s strong summer reliability cannot be used to infer a similarly favorable PSEG Q4 outcome. Lost generation, additional inspection or repair costs, and replacement-power requirements can offset contracting optimism.

Timing and limitations: PSEG’s own uprate and outage disclosures were already public before this call. The immediate catalysts are clarification of the Salem 1 repair scope and restart timing, followed by PSEG-specific contracting announcements. The structural benefit requires investment, approvals and commissioning. With more than 95% of expected 2026 nuclear output hedged, the call does not justify a near-term merchant-price earnings upgrade.

NUCLEAR EQUIPMENT AND SERVICES

SIEMENS ENERGY IS A VERIFIED BENEFICIARY OF THE NUCLEAR REFURBISHMENT CYCLE (READ-THROUGH 4)

Affected company: Siemens Energy (ENR: Germany).

Directional impact and magnitude: Positive for nuclear-related equipment and service demand. Meaningful within the relevant business, but the incremental consolidated earnings contribution remains unquantified.

Call evidence: Constellation completed Byron Unit 2’s low-pressure turbine upgrade in late October after completing Unit 1 earlier in 2026. Management reported completion under budget, more than 1 week faster than the vendor’s prior record, and early output above expectations. The broader uprate program encompasses nearly 1,200 MW, with most capacity scheduled during 2029-2032.

Transmission mechanism: Siemens Energy has explicitly disclosed that it is providing 12 low-pressure steam turbines for Constellation’s Byron and Braidwood facilities, supporting approximately 135 MW of additional output across the plants. This establishes a direct supplier relationship. The read-through is therefore more defensible than assigning the nuclear investment cycle indiscriminately to equipment companies with only general sector exposure.

Successful delivery supports the commercial case for further conventional-island modernization: steam turbines, generators, associated controls and services can increase output without constructing a new reactor. Long-term customer contracts make the owner’s investment easier to underwrite, while favorable project financing can reduce the risk that technically viable upgrades are deferred for funding reasons. Repeat investment across the existing nuclear fleet can consequently support equipment and service demand before large-scale new reactor construction becomes a substantial revenue source.

The attractive feature is the sequence of monetization. Equipment engineering, procurement, installation and outage services occur before the generating assets reach their full contracted earnings run rate. Suppliers can therefore recognize activity earlier than the late-decade electricity delivery ramp, although actual revenue recognition depends on contract terms.

Timing and limitations: Byron’s completion is confirmation of execution on an existing relationship, not a newly announced Siemens Energy order. Some associated revenue may already have been recognized. The call does not identify the supplier allocation for the remaining uprate program, and Constellation’s $4.3 billion project budget is not Siemens Energy revenue. Near-term catalysts are disclosed follow-on awards and order intake; the longer-duration benefit is a multiyear refurbishment and service cycle. The preliminary excess output at Byron remains unquantified and should not be converted into additional supplier revenue.

ADVANCED NUCLEAR DEVELOPMENT

BROWNFIELD NUCLEAR AND FLEXIBLE CAPACITY RAISE THE COMPETITIVE HURDLE FOR DEVELOPMENT-STAGE REACTORS (READ-THROUGH 5)

Affected companies: Oklo (OKLO: United States) and NuScale Power (SMR: United States).

Directional impact and magnitude: Negative for scarcity-based pricing assumptions and the conversion of prospective projects into binding commercial commitments. Potentially material to long-duration valuation assumptions, but no specific near-term revenue reduction or project cancellation is established.

Call evidence: Constellation expects nearly 1,200 MW of uprates for approximately $4.3 billion, with most capacity available during 2029-2032. Management described these projects as substantially less expensive than new nuclear construction. It also argued that underutilized existing generation and flexibility could support additional demand for another 6-7 years, potentially toward 2035.

Transmission mechanism: Customers deciding how to obtain dependable power have more alternatives than a binary choice between constrained grid supply and a first-of-a-kind reactor. Existing nuclear contracts, uprates, restarts, storage and demand response can reduce the urgency to accept development risk or high initial costs. That can pressure the price, contractual protections and customer funding that advanced-reactor developers obtain when converting preliminary interest into binding agreements.

For Oklo, which plans to own and sell output from its plants, the transmission is through achievable power prices, customer funding commitments and the pace of deployment. For NuScale, which supplies reactor technology and modules, the transmission is through customers’ investment decisions and the timing of firm module orders. The business models differ, but both depend on projects remaining attractive against other reliable-power options.

The negative conclusion must remain narrower than “new nuclear is unnecessary.” Oklo already has a Meta-backed Ohio development arrangement targeting an initial phase as early as 2030 and expansion toward 1.2 GW by 2034. NuScale’s November 5 results disclosed a manufacturing agreement with Doosan Enerbility for the upper reactor coolant system of its first commercial module. Those developments show continuing customer support and industrial progress. Constellation’s statement that some new-build estimates are a decade later should not be applied universally to every developer’s published schedule.

The capital comparison also requires care. Constellation’s approximately $3,580/kW uprate figure leverages an existing plant and excludes some broader life-extension expenditure; it is not an all-in greenfield reactor cost. Nevertheless, the availability of contracted brownfield alternatives creates a real competitive hurdle for customers evaluating new projects.

Timing and limitations: The immediate effect is on relative valuation narratives and perceived urgency, not reported earnings. The longer-duration risk is slower conversion of development pipelines, tougher customer terms or lower achievable returns during 2028-2035. The decisive catalysts are binding power agreements, project financing, regulatory milestones and firm construction economics. This is a negative read-through to assumptions that customers lack alternatives, not evidence that existing funded programs have been displaced.

HYPERSCALERS AND CLOUD INFRASTRUCTURE

ALPHABET AND AMAZON IMPROVE POWER-PROCUREMENT VISIBILITY WITHOUT SOLVING EVERY DATA-CENTER BOTTLENECK (READ-THROUGH 6)

Affected companies: Alphabet (GOOGL: United States) and https://t.co/SpqvHNV5fi (AMZN: United States).

Directional impact and magnitude: Positive for regional infrastructure planning and long-term energy-cost visibility. Strategically meaningful in PJM, but a direct consolidated EPS benefit is not quantifiable from the disclosed terms.

Call evidence: Management identified Google and Amazon as counterparties to major long-term agreements supporting both existing nuclear plants and new capacity. Constellation also emphasized that its solutions can serve customers across PJM rather than requiring data centers to sit adjacent to a particular generating plant.

The related disclosures establish the scope. Google’s arrangements include approximately 890 MW of new nuclear capacity under a 20-year PPA and a separate 15-year financial energy agreement covering 2,700 MW. Amazon’s Calvert Cliffs agreement covers 690 MW for 20 years, including approximately 190 MW of new capacity expected during 2030-2032.

Transmission mechanism: These contracts reduce uncertainty around a major input to infrastructure planning and allow the customers to support incremental supply without directly undertaking full nuclear construction and operation. Combining existing generation with new capacity can help address affordability and reliability concerns more efficiently than requiring a completely new baseload facility for every increment of demand.

The geographic implication is important. Google’s arrangements span multiple nuclear sites in Illinois, Pennsylvania and New Jersey, while Amazon’s Calvert Cliffs supply supports operations across PJM rather than only Maryland. Regional contracting can provide greater flexibility in locating load, subject to transmission availability and local interconnection requirements.

However, the approximately 4,280 MW covered by these arrangements is not equivalent to 4,280 MW of newly energized data-center capacity. Only approximately 1,080 MW represents the identified nuclear additions, and Google’s 2,700 MW arrangement is financial. Neither a financial hedge nor a PPA automatically provides a completed substation, transmission upgrades or permission to energize a particular campus. These agreements therefore do not justify mechanical increases to near-term server, networking or cooling-equipment forecasts.

There is also a cost and commitment trade-off. Long-term agreements improve visibility but can leave customers paying above future market prices or carrying obligations if their regional development plans slow. The disclosed pricing is insufficient to establish an operating-margin benefit. Constellation’s $20-$50/MWh sensitivity is not the publicly disclosed price of either customer’s contract.

Timing and limitations: The Amazon and Google agreements were announced in September and October, respectively. The earnings call adds execution context and a clearer view of the investment program rather than wholly new customer commitments. Near-term significance is reduced uncertainty around procurement strategy. The fundamental benefit emerges as supply and customer facilities become operational from 2028 onward, with much of the additional nuclear generation arriving during 2029-2032.

MICROSOFT’S CRANE AGREEMENT GAINS EXECUTION CONFIDENCE, NOT ANOTHER YEAR OF SCHEDULE ACCELERATION (READ-THROUGH 7)

Affected company: Microsoft (MSFT: United States).

Directional impact and magnitude: Positive for the reliability of a specific long-term clean-power procurement plan. Modest at Microsoft’s consolidated earnings scale, but meaningful for the associated PJM energy strategy.

Call evidence: Constellation reported that the first fuel assemblies and transformers are on site at Crane, that the NRC issued a favorable final environmental assessment, and that the plant remains on track to restart in the 2nd half of 2027, under budget. Crane’s approximately 835 MW restart supports Microsoft’s existing long-term power purchase agreement.

Transmission mechanism: Physical equipment deliveries and progress through environmental review reduce identifiable risks to the project supplying Microsoft’s contracted clean energy. Successful restart would add operating nuclear generation to PJM and improve the availability of reliable, low-carbon energy supporting Microsoft’s regional procurement commitments. These are more substantive milestones than an unchanged aspirational development target.

The crucial timing distinction is that the 2nd-half 2027 restart target was already communicated on Constellation’s Q2 call. The description of the project being 1 year ahead of schedule refers to the original timetable, not a new acceleration announced in Q3. The incremental information is improved confidence in delivery against the existing accelerated schedule.

The contract also should not be treated as a dedicated physical connection that automatically energizes Microsoft computing capacity. Crane’s generation enters the regional system, while individual data centers retain their own transmission, distribution, commissioning and operating requirements. No conversion from the plant’s MW to Azure revenue or AI capacity is supported.

Timing and limitations: Near-term catalysts are remaining approvals, commissioning progress and confirmation that the restart remains within budget. The principal fundamental event is sustained commercial operation in the 2nd half of 2027. Fuel arrival and environmental progress are positive, but neither is equivalent to final authorization to operate or proof of post-restart availability. The appropriate read-through is reduced execution risk around an existing Microsoft commitment, not a new contract or an immediate cloud earnings upgrade.

First Lady Melania Trump Receives Thunderous Applause at LSU-Alabama Game as She Announces Fostering the Future Scholarships (VIDEO) | Cristina Laila, The Gateway Pundit

First Lady Melania Trump stole the show at LSU on Saturday as she announced ‘Fostering the Future’ scholarships for student.

“First Lady Melania Trump and Louisiana State University (LSU) have secured $7.2 Million to establish a permanent endowment fund supporting FOSTERING THE FUTURE scholarships for LSU students who experienced foster care,” the White House said.

“A great education does more than prepare someone for work life. It gives something no one can ever take away. There is nothing more powerful we can give a young person than a world-class education,” said First Lady Melania Trump.

According to the White House, “The $7.2 Million endowment advances First Lady Melania Trump’s FOSTERING THE FUTURE initiative which provides individuals from foster care with academic scholarships to prepare them to secure an entry-level job and become financially independent.”

“As adults, we have a moral obligation to our children, especially those in foster care. But, as you know, we must act to truly make a difference. The foster care community doesn’t need words,” Melania Trump said.

MMR Group committed $5 million to First Lady Melania Trump’s FOSTERING THE FUTURE, with contributions from additional LSU Foundation donors.

“Access is a top priority for LSU, because circumstances should not determine whether talent and ambition thrive. MMR Group’s visionary scholarship funding for First Lady Melania Trump’s FOSTERING THE FUTURE is transformative for youth from foster care who aspire to earn an LSU degree,” said LSU President Wade Rousse.

“Today, Louisiana State University is launching $7.2M Fostering the Future scholarship endowment,” Melania Trump said.

“To the Fostering the Future scholars here today, and throughout America: I see you. I believe in you. And I will keep working to create new opportunities with you,” she said.

“LSU defines excellence. Your high standards start in the classroom, amplifies on the football field, and shapes America’s future leaders,” Melania said.

The First Lady received a thunderous applause as she was introduced at the LSU-Alabama game.

text:
The Green Wave keeps rolling in the 2027 cycle.

While the current team battles through a challenging season, Tulane’s recruiting staff under Will Hall has continued stacking talent for the future. 

The class sits at roughly 26 commitments as of early November 2026, with the latest wave of additions giving the roster more size up front, speed in the secondary, and versatility at linebacker.

Caleb Unger set the tone in late October. 

The 6-2/6-3, ~300-pound interior offensive lineman from Madison-Ridgeland Academy in Madison, Mississippi, flipped from Mississippi State and became one of the highest-rated pledges in the class. 

A high-motor, technically sound lineman with good leverage and quickness, Unger held offers from Power Four programs including LSU, Colorado, Oregon, and others before choosing Tulane. 

He plans to enroll early and is viewed as a potential early contributor, especially as the program looks to solidify the offensive line. 

That momentum has continued. The two most recent additions are Trevor Caudle and Special Henry.

Trevor Caudle, a 6-0 corner from James Clemens High School in Madison, Alabama, brings elite track speed (10.55 in the 100m, 21.06 in the 200m). 

The Green Wave landed the track-athlete corner after a strong official visit. He projects as a lockdown outside corner with recovery speed, ball skills, and the willingness to tackle, exactly the kind of multi-phase defensive back the staff has targeted. 

Special Henry, a 6-3/195-pound linebacker from Melissa High School in Texas, flipped from Iowa State. 

With verified 4.44–4.50 speed, an 82–83-inch wingspan, and hybrid versatility (listed at times as OLB/CB), he offers sideline-to-sideline range, length in coverage, and the frame to add strength. 

He held a long list of Division I offers and chose Tulane for the fit and opportunity.

text:
$NRG Q3 2026 earnings: NRG sells $4B of plants, but 2027 profit barely grows

NRG Energy, the North American power and smart-home group, rebounding in Texas and selling six gas plants for $4 billion, still set a 2027 profit plan that barely moves. Third-quarter operating profit excluding one-offs rose 67% from a year ago to $2.0 billion, helped by power plants bought in January and a 26% recovery in Texas. Chief executive Robert Gaudette kept the 2026 plan unchanged, which by our math leaves fourth-quarter profit per share up 17%.

• Operating profit (Adjusted EBITDA): $𝟐,𝟎𝟏𝟑𝐌 (+67% from a year ago (+27% outside the East))
• Profit per share, excluding one-offs: $𝟒.𝟔𝟖 (+68% from a year ago)
• 2027 profit per share outlook: $𝟖.𝟎𝟓–$𝟏𝟎.𝟎𝟓 (middle of the range: +1.7% vs 2026 plan)
• Power plant sale to LS Power: $𝟒.𝟎𝐁 𝐜𝐚𝐬𝐡 (4.9 GW of gas plants; funds $3B buybacks & $3B debt cut)

⚖️ 𝐕𝐞𝐫𝐝𝐢𝐜𝐭: 🟢 Bullish

The story got better because the $4 billion plant sale back to LS Power fixes the balance sheet while Texas stopped shrinking. The sale funds $3 billion in debt cuts and $3 billion in buybacks across 2026 and 2027 while keeping the East Coast power fleet. One caution: the initial 2027 outlook puts profit per share at a $9.05 middle, up less than 2% from the 2026 plan as interest and plant upkeep climb, and the 1.2 GW data-center power project still lacks a final contract.

The question now is whether the extra $2 billion of buybacks and debt cuts from the plant sale will lift 2027 profit per share more than losing the six plants hurts it. If the sold plants earned modest cash flow, the share count drop will accelerate per-share growth toward management's 14% yearly goal; if they were major earners, 2027 stays slow. Management's updated 2027 plan after the sale closes in the second quarter of 2027 will settle it.

Full article with charts - link in bio

🐂 𝐁𝐮𝐥𝐥 𝐂𝐚𝐬𝐞

🟢🟢 $𝟒𝐁 𝐏𝐨𝐰𝐞𝐫 𝐏𝐥𝐚𝐧𝐭 𝐒𝐚𝐥𝐞 𝐅𝐮𝐧𝐝𝐬 𝐃𝐞𝐛𝐭 𝐂𝐮𝐭𝐬 𝐚𝐧𝐝 𝐁𝐮𝐲𝐛𝐚𝐜𝐤𝐬
NRG Energy, a North American electricity, natural gas and smart-home provider, doubled its power fleet in January by buying plants from LS Power. That deal pushed debt up and raised concerns about how the Houston group could fund new power plants while still buying back shares. Chief executive Robert Gaudette answered that concern today: "Today’s announcement is about returning more to our shareholders and supporting future growth investments."

The company signed an agreement "to sell six natural-gas fired generation assets totaling 4.9 GW to LS Power, for a purchase price of $4 billion in cash proceeds", closing in the second quarter of 2027. Crucially, the deal "retains the entire PJM portfolio and CPower acquired by the Company in January 2026", which are the East Coast plants and the commercial demand-response platform.

• Planned 2027 debt reduction: rises from $1 billion to $3 billion once the sale closes
• Share buybacks across 2026 and 2027: $3 billion in total, including $1 billion more starting in late 2026
• Unallocated sale cash: $1 billion left for contracted growth projects or extra debt paydown
• Annual common dividend: rising 8% to $2.05 per share in 2027

Selling 4.9 gigawatts (GW) of gas plants turns a stretched balance sheet into a source of cash, because the extra $2 billion debt payoff will "maintain the Company's current leverage profile" after those plants leave. What to watch: updated 2027 profit targets after the sale closes in the second quarter of 2027. Those numbers will show how much yearly cash flow the six sold plants were producing.

🟢🟢 𝐓𝐞𝐱𝐚𝐬 𝐏𝐫𝐨𝐟𝐢𝐭 𝐑𝐞𝐛𝐨𝐮𝐧𝐝𝐬 𝐀𝐟𝐭𝐞𝐫 𝐓𝐡𝐫𝐞𝐞 𝐐𝐮𝐚𝐫𝐭𝐞𝐫𝐬 𝐨𝐟 𝐃𝐞𝐜𝐥𝐢𝐧𝐞𝐬
Texas is NRG's largest market, and its operating profit there had fallen from a year earlier for three straight quarters as weak local power prices and mild winter weather hurt sales. In the third quarter, Texas Adjusted EBITDA — operating profit before interest, taxes, wear and tear, and one-off items — jumped 26.1% from a year ago to $1,018 million, driven by "increased retail margins and favorable weather in the third quarter".

That summer rebound erased the deficit from the first half of the year, leaving nine-month Texas Adjusted EBITDA nearly even with last year at $1,615 million versus $1,618 million. Across the whole company, lower fuel and operating costs lifted the operating margin by 6.0 percentage points to 11.5% of sales: cost of operations fell by 5.3 percentage points of revenue, and overhead and selling expenses dropped by 1.5 points.

One good summer softens the concern about Texas customer losses and cheap solar and battery power, but it does not settle it because hot weather helped carry the quarter. What to watch: Texas home customer counts and power volumes in the third-quarter filing. Steady customer numbers would show the rebound came from better pricing rather than temporary summer air-conditioning demand.

🟢 𝐄𝐚𝐬𝐭 𝐆𝐫𝐢𝐝 𝐂𝐚𝐩𝐚𝐜𝐢𝐭𝐲 𝐏𝐫𝐢𝐜𝐞𝐬 𝐚𝐧𝐝 𝐕𝐢𝐯𝐢𝐧𝐭 𝐋𝐢𝐟𝐭 𝐂𝐚𝐬𝐡 𝐅𝐥𝐨𝐰
Outside Texas, NRG relies on East Coast power plants and Vivint Smart Home, its home-security and automation subscription business, to bring in steady cash. Both businesses grew fast this quarter. East Adjusted EBITDA rose nearly sixfold from a year ago to $614 million from $107 million, helped by the plants bought in January and higher capacity prices — payments grid operators make to power plants just for standing ready to supply electricity.

Vivint Adjusted EBITDA climbed 14.0% to $317 million on "higher new customer adds and an increase in monthly recurring service margin per customer". Together with the Texas rebound, those gains pushed Free Cash Flow before Growth Investments — cash left after plant upkeep but before new builds — up 50.0% to $1,242 million. Even excluding the East acquisition jump, profit across the rest of the business rose 27.4% by our math.

What to watch: quarterly capacity revenue in the third-quarter filing. A figure at or above the second quarter's $392 million would confirm that higher East Coast grid payments are flowing into revenue on schedule.

🐻 𝐁𝐞𝐚𝐫 𝐂𝐚𝐬𝐞

🔴🔴 𝐈𝐧𝐢𝐭𝐢𝐚𝐥 𝟐𝟎𝟐𝟕 𝐏𝐫𝐨𝐟𝐢𝐭 𝐏𝐥𝐚𝐧 𝐓𝐫𝐚𝐢𝐥𝐬 𝐋𝐨𝐧𝐠-𝐓𝐞𝐫𝐦 𝐆𝐫𝐨𝐰𝐭𝐡 𝐓𝐚𝐫𝐠𝐞𝐭
"Our 17,000 employees delivered strong third quarter results that reflect the depth of NRG, with our eight million customers and a substantial generation business that produce steady earnings and cash flows," Gaudette said. The company also backed its long-term targets, which call for profit per share excluding one-offs to grow by at least 14% a year through 2030. Yet the first outlook for 2027 starts far below that pace.

• 2027 profit per share, excluding one-offs: $8.05 to $10.05, or $9.05 at the middle of the range (up 1.7% from the 2026 middle of $8.90 by our math)
• 2027 net profit, excluding one-offs: $1,665 million to $2,075 million, down 1.6% at the middle from 2026 by our math
• 2027 Adjusted EBITDA: $5,500 million to $6,000 million, up 3.1% at the middle from 2026 by our math
• 2027 cash flow before growth: $2,900 million to $3,400 million, up 3.3% at the middle from 2026 by our math

Net profit barely moves in 2027, so the small gain in profit per share comes entirely from share buybacks trimming the basic share count from 214 million to 207 million. These figures do not yet include the 4.9 GW plant sale or the extra $2 billion of buybacks it will fund. What to watch: the revised 2027 outlook after the plant sale closes in mid-2027, which must show whether buybacks outweigh the lost plant earnings.

🔴 𝐇𝐢𝐠𝐡𝐞𝐫 𝐈𝐧𝐭𝐞𝐫𝐞𝐬𝐭 𝐚𝐧𝐝 𝐏𝐥𝐚𝐧𝐭 𝐖𝐞𝐚𝐫 𝐄𝐚𝐭 𝐈𝐧𝐭𝐨 𝐍𝐞𝐭 𝐏𝐫𝐨𝐟𝐢𝐭
Buying the LS Power fleet gave NRG more power plants, but it also brought big financing bills, heavier plant upkeep, and old power contracts locked in at low prices. In the third quarter, the utility paid $172 million in cash to cancel some of those inherited contracts, equal to 15.7% of its operating cash flow by our math. Interest costs also rose 61.5% from a year ago to $302 million.

Those costs grow again in the 2027 plan before the asset sale. Compared with the 2026 plan, net interest expense rises by $105 million to $1,300 million, depreciation and amortization — the yearly charge for aging plants and customer contracts — climbs by $160 million to $2,115 million, and plant maintenance spending steps up by $120 million at the middle of the range to $585 million. That is why a $175 million rise in 2027 Adjusted EBITDA turns into a $30 million drop in net profit.

What to watch: management's breakdown on the conference call of how many below-market inherited power contracts remain for 2027 after this quarter's $172 million buyout. A remaining drag in 2027 would explain why next year's operating profit grows only 3.1% despite a full twelve months of the acquired fleet.

🔴 𝐃𝐚𝐭𝐚 𝐂𝐞𝐧𝐭𝐞𝐫 𝐏𝐨𝐰𝐞𝐫 𝐃𝐞𝐚𝐥 𝐒𝐭𝐢𝐥𝐥 𝐋𝐚𝐜𝐤𝐬 𝐚 𝐒𝐢𝐠𝐧𝐞𝐝 𝐂𝐨𝐧𝐭𝐫𝐚𝐜𝐭
A pillar of the bull case is NRG's Bring Your Own Power (BYOP) programme, which builds dedicated natural-gas power plants for technology companies running artificial-intelligence data centers. Last quarter, management outlined preliminary terms for a 1.2 GW Texas project costing $3.2 billion and committed $721 million for equipment in 2026, while bulls argued that a final contract was close.

This quarter's release gave no new milestone, stating only that the 1.2 GW project "remains on track" and "brings new, dispatchable generation alongside load growth to support reliability and affordability". Capital expenditures on the cash flow statement reached $1,181 million over the first nine months, up from $849 million a year earlier, as equipment buying continued ahead of a signed contract.

Spending money on turbines before a customer signs a binding contract leaves NRG carrying the financial risk if Texas grid rules or project permits cause a delay. What to watch: a signed final agreement and construction green light by the fourth-quarter release. Missing that year-end goal would leave hundreds of millions in equipment spending without guaranteed customer payments.

🔴 𝐑𝐢𝐬𝐤𝐬 𝐭𝐡𝐢𝐬 𝐪𝐮𝐚𝐫𝐭𝐞𝐫 𝐝𝐢𝐝𝐧'𝐭 𝐚𝐧𝐬𝐰𝐞𝐫
Several regulatory and market-design risks from prior quarters received no update in the third-quarter earnings release because policy decisions and detailed tables arrive in later filings.

• East Coast grid rules and carbon costs: PJM capacity price caps, backstop auction rules, and Virginia carbon-market charges were not quantified; updates arrive in the quarterly filing's regulatory note.
• Retail power price rules in Maryland and New York: potential state caps and retail margin pressure vs local utilities were not detailed; the filing's legal note will update them.
• Data-center customer credit and construction cost protection: the customer's name, credit terms, and cost-overrun rules remain undisclosed until a final contract is signed.

— • — • —

💲 𝐎𝐭𝐡𝐞𝐫 𝐊𝐏𝐈𝐬

𝐓𝐨𝐭𝐚𝐥 𝐝𝐞𝐛𝐭 (𝟐𝟔𝐐𝟑): $𝟐𝟐,𝟗𝟐𝟑 𝐦𝐢𝐥𝐥𝐢𝐨𝐧  ⇘ decelerating
Total debt — short-term and long-term borrowings plus finance leases — fell by $333 million from the second quarter's $23,256 million, though it remains up 39.4% from $16,443 million at the end of 2025 due to the January power plant purchase. Available corporate liquidity rose to $6,027 million from $5,280 million in June.

𝐓𝐨𝐭𝐚𝐥 𝐝𝐞𝐟𝐞𝐫𝐫𝐞𝐝 𝐫𝐞𝐯𝐞𝐧𝐮𝐞 (𝟐𝟔𝐐𝟑): $𝟏,𝟖𝟖𝟏 𝐦𝐢𝐥𝐥𝐢𝐨𝐧  ⇗ accelerating
Deferred revenue — cash collected from customers in advance for electricity and smart-home services not yet delivered — rose 3.3% from $1,821 million in the second quarter and is up 14.5% from $1,643 million at the end of 2025. The steady climb reflects growing multi-year Vivint smart-home subscriptions and acquired commercial contracts.

𝐁𝐚𝐬𝐢𝐜 𝐜𝐨𝐦𝐦𝐨𝐧 𝐬𝐡𝐚𝐫𝐞 𝐜𝐨𝐮𝐧𝐭 (𝟐𝟔𝐐𝟑): 𝟐𝟏𝟎 𝐦𝐢𝐥𝐥𝐢𝐨𝐧  ⇘ decelerating
The average number of basic common shares dipped by 1 million from the second quarter's 211 million as NRG completed $977 million of its $1.0 billion 2026 buyback plan through October. Shares remain 8.8% higher than a year ago because the energy group issued stock in January to help pay for the LS Power assets.

— • — • —

🔮 𝐆𝐮𝐢𝐝𝐚𝐧𝐜𝐞

𝟐𝟎𝟐𝟔 𝐀𝐝𝐣𝐮𝐬𝐭𝐞𝐝 𝐄𝐁𝐈𝐓𝐃𝐀: $𝟓,𝟑𝟐𝟓–$𝟓,𝟖𝟐𝟓 𝐦𝐢𝐥𝐥𝐢𝐨𝐧  ⇘ decelerating
🠆 unchanged from $5,325–$5,825 million
Unchanged. The full-year plan still points to $5,575 million at the middle of the range, up 36.4% from 2025 with eleven months of the acquired fleet. By our math, after $4,310 million in the first nine months, the middle of the range leaves $1,265 million for the fourth quarter, up 49.4% from a year ago.

𝟐𝟎𝟐𝟔 𝐀𝐝𝐣𝐮𝐬𝐭𝐞𝐝 𝐄𝐏𝐒: $𝟕.𝟗𝟎–$𝟗.𝟗𝟎  ⇘ decelerating
🠆 unchanged from $7.90–$9.90
Unchanged. Profit per share excluding one-offs is still planned at $8.90 at the middle of the range, up 8.0% from $8.24 in 2025 on 214 million basic shares. With $7.68 earned in the first nine months, by our math the plan leaves $1.22 for the fourth quarter, up 17.3% from last year's $1.04.

𝟐𝟎𝟐𝟔 𝐀𝐝𝐣𝐮𝐬𝐭𝐞𝐝 𝐍𝐞𝐭 𝐈𝐧𝐜𝐨𝐦𝐞: $𝟏,𝟔𝟖𝟓–$𝟐,𝟏𝟏𝟓 𝐦𝐢𝐥𝐥𝐢𝐨𝐧  ⇘ decelerating
🠆 unchanged from $1,685–$2,115 million
Unchanged. Net profit excluding one-offs remains at a middle of $1,900 million, or 18.3% above 2025. After $1,605 million through September, by our math the fourth-quarter remainder is $295 million at the middle, up 47.5% from $200 million in the fourth quarter of 2025.

𝟐𝟎𝟐𝟔 𝐅𝐫𝐞𝐞 𝐂𝐚𝐬𝐡 𝐅𝐥𝐨𝐰 𝐛𝐞𝐟𝐨𝐫𝐞 𝐆𝐫𝐨𝐰𝐭𝐡 𝐈𝐧𝐯𝐞𝐬𝐭𝐦𝐞𝐧𝐭𝐬: $𝟐,𝟖𝟎𝟎–$𝟑,𝟑𝟎𝟎 𝐦𝐢𝐥𝐥𝐢𝐨𝐧  ⇗ accelerating
🠆 unchanged from $2,800–$3,300 million
Unchanged. The cash-flow target stays at a $3,050 million middle, up 38.0% from 2025. With $2,201 million generated in the first nine months, by our math the fourth quarter needs $849 million to reach the middle, nearly five times last year's fourth-quarter level of $175 million.

𝟐𝟎𝟐𝟕 𝐀𝐝𝐣𝐮𝐬𝐭𝐞𝐝 𝐄𝐁𝐈𝐓𝐃𝐀: $𝟓,𝟓𝟎𝟎–$𝟔,𝟎𝟎𝟎 𝐦𝐢𝐥𝐥𝐢𝐨𝐧  ⇘ decelerating
New. The initial 2027 plan sets a middle of $5,750 million, which is 3.1% above the 2026 outlook middle by our math. The forecast includes a full twelve months of the fleet bought in January but does not yet subtract the 4.9 GW of gas plants being sold in mid-2027.

𝟐𝟎𝟐𝟕 𝐀𝐝𝐣𝐮𝐬𝐭𝐞𝐝 𝐄𝐏𝐒: $𝟖.𝟎𝟓–$𝟏𝟎.𝟎𝟓  ⇘ decelerating
New. The 2027 plan puts profit per share excluding one-offs at a $9.05 middle, up 1.7% from the 2026 outlook middle by our math. The gain comes from lowering the basic share count to 207 million via $1 billion of base buybacks, before counting the extra $2 billion of buybacks from the asset sale.

𝟐𝟎𝟐𝟕 𝐀𝐝𝐣𝐮𝐬𝐭𝐞𝐝 𝐍𝐞𝐭 𝐈𝐧𝐜𝐨𝐦𝐞: $𝟏,𝟔𝟔𝟓–$𝟐,𝟎𝟕𝟓 𝐦𝐢𝐥𝐥𝐢𝐨𝐧  ⇘ decelerating
New. The 2027 range centers on $1,870 million, down 1.6% from the 2026 middle of $1,900 million by our math. Higher operating profit is outweighed by $1,300 million of net interest and $2,115 million of depreciation and amortization before the planned $3 billion debt paydown takes effect.

𝟐𝟎𝟐𝟕 𝐅𝐫𝐞𝐞 𝐂𝐚𝐬𝐡 𝐅𝐥𝐨𝐰 𝐛𝐞𝐟𝐨𝐫𝐞 𝐆𝐫𝐨𝐰𝐭𝐡 𝐈𝐧𝐯𝐞𝐬𝐭𝐦𝐞𝐧𝐭𝐬: $𝟐,𝟗𝟎𝟎–$𝟑,𝟒𝟎𝟎 𝐦𝐢𝐥𝐥𝐢𝐨𝐧  ⇘ decelerating
New. The 2027 cash-flow plan centers on $3,150 million, up 3.3% from the 2026 middle by our math. Higher operating cash flow and a $235 million favorable swing in working capital cover a $135 million rise in cash interest payments and a $120 million increase in plant maintenance spending.

— • — • —

❓ 𝐊𝐞𝐲 𝐐𝐮𝐞𝐬𝐭𝐢𝐨𝐧𝐬

𝐇𝐨𝐰 𝐦𝐮𝐜𝐡 𝐨𝐩𝐞𝐫𝐚𝐭𝐢𝐧𝐠 𝐩𝐫𝐨𝐟𝐢𝐭 𝐝𝐨 𝐭𝐡𝐞 𝐬𝐨𝐥𝐝 𝐩𝐥𝐚𝐧𝐭𝐬 𝐩𝐫𝐨𝐝𝐮𝐜𝐞?
NRG is selling 4.9 GW of gas plants back to LS Power for $4 billion in mid-2027, but the initial 2027 outlook still includes them. Investors need the EBITDA and cash flow of those six plants to calculate 2027 profit per share after the sale.

𝐃𝐢𝐝 𝐭𝐡𝐞 $𝟏𝟕𝟐𝐌 𝐛𝐮𝐲𝐨𝐮𝐭 𝐜𝐥𝐞𝐚𝐫 𝐚𝐥𝐥 𝐛𝐞𝐥𝐨𝐰-𝐦𝐚𝐫𝐤𝐞𝐭 𝟐𝟎𝟐𝟕 𝐡𝐞𝐝𝐠𝐞𝐬?
The company paid $172 million in the third quarter to cancel inherited power hedges, after promising last quarter to detail how much of that drag extends into 2027. Whether any below-market contracts remain will show if 2028 gets an automatic earnings lift.

𝐖𝐡𝐞𝐧 𝐰𝐢𝐥𝐥 𝐭𝐡𝐞 𝟏.𝟐 𝐆𝐖 𝐝𝐚𝐭𝐚-𝐜𝐞𝐧𝐭𝐞𝐫 𝐝𝐞𝐚𝐥 𝐫𝐞𝐚𝐜𝐡 𝐟𝐢𝐧𝐚𝐥 𝐬𝐢𝐠𝐧𝐢𝐧𝐠?
Management said the 1.2 GW Bring Your Own Power project remains on track, but did not announce a binding contract or name the customer. With hundreds of millions already spent on equipment, the timing of a signed agreement is critical.

🚨 DEMOCRATS GAIN PATH TO TRANSFORM 2028 PRESIDENTIAL ELECTION — ELECTORAL COLLEGE FACES MAJOR LEGAL SHOWDOWN

One of the biggest consequences of Tuesday’s Democratic wave may have nothing to do with Congress.

Democrats now control the governorship and both legislative chambers in five additional states positioned to advance the National Popular Vote Interstate Compact.

The numbers:

▪️ 222 electoral votes already committed, including Maryland’s 10.

▪️ 270 needed to activate the agreement.

▪️ 61 additional electoral votes available from Pennsylvania, Michigan, Wisconsin, Arizona and Nevada.

▪️ 283 total if all five states join.

Under the compact, participating states would award their presidential electors to the NATIONAL popular-vote winner, even if another candidate won their own state.

The Electoral College would technically remain, but the traditional state-by-state winner-take-all system would be fundamentally altered.

Here’s the critical distinction: The compact has NOT reached 270. The five states must still pass legislation, and constitutional challenges could follow.

Supporters argue every presidential vote should carry equal weight. Critics question whether states can make such a sweeping change without congressional approval.

Maryland joined this effort back in 2007.

Now the 2026 midterms have opened a potential path to implementing it before 2028.

The next presidential election could involve a major constitutional battle over how America chooses its president.

FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE
Contact: Thomas Evenstad Campaign | @PrisonReform15
EVENSTAD ANNOUNCES REPUBLICAN CANDIDACY FOR U.S. SENATE
Survivor of nearly 30-year lawfare campaign enters 2027 special election for Klobuchar’s open seat
EDINA, MN — November 11, 2026 — Thomas Evenstad today formally announced his candidacy for the Republican nomination for the United States Senate seat being vacated by Amy Klobuchar. The special election primary is scheduled for August 10, 2027, with the general election on November 2, 2027.
Evenstad, a lifelong Edina resident and public-safety advocate, spent ten years in prison following his 1999 conviction for criminal sexual conduct in Hennepin County — a prosecution he has consistently maintained was a wrongful frame engineered by then-Hennepin County Attorney Amy Klobuchar’s office. His appeals were denied. He was released in 2009.
“Amy Klobuchar put me in prison for a crime I did not commit,” Evenstad said. “She built a political career on that case. Now she is leaving the Senate for the governor’s office, and I am running as a Republican to take the seat she leaves behind. This is not revenge. This is accountability.”
A Nearly 30-Year Fight for Public Safety
Evenstad’s public-safety advocacy began in January 2003 when he sent then-Governor Tim Pawlenty a detailed proposal for GPS ankle monitoring of high-risk sex offenders — months before the murder of Dru Sjodin. He has spent the decades since advancing the Violently Dangerous Persons Act (VDP Act / Mariah’s Law / Iryna’s Law), which independent modeling projects could cut violent crime 50–64 percent through expanded civil commitment, resource reallocation, and longer detention of the most dangerous repeat offenders.
In October 2026, a judge ruled in his favor after a 14-month legal battle against Minnesota GOP Chair Alex Plekach, finding no harassment.
“They tried to destroy me from the left and from the right,” Evenstad said. “I defeated both sides’ lawfare. I’m still standing. That tells you everything about who I am and what this campaign is.”
Platform Highlights for Minnesota Families
Evenstad is running as a Republican populist focused on results over party labels. His Contract with America / 10-point platform as a Minnesota Senator prioritizes concrete benefits for Minnesota voters:
Public Safety First — Enact the VDP Act / Mariah’s Law nationally to expand civil-commitment tools against violently dangerous repeat offenders and deliver the projected major reduction in overall violence. Minnesota families will no longer wait for the next preventable tragedy.
End Property Tax Oppression — Fight for elimination or radical reduction of property taxes that punish Minnesota homeowners and farmers, restoring economic freedom at the local level through public-safety savings.
Secure the Border and Enforce Immigration Law — Prioritize deportation of illegal aliens who threaten public safety and strain Minnesota communities, while protecting legal pathways and American workers.
Protect Children and Soft Targets — Harden schools, churches, and community spaces. Zero tolerance for policies that expose kids to predation or ideological capture.
Fiscal Discipline Without RINO Excuses — Cut waste, end corporate welfare for the connected, and restore accountability to federal spending that drives inflation and burdens Minnesota taxpayers.
America First, Minnesota First Trade and Agriculture — Defend Minnesota farmers and manufacturers from unfair foreign competition and bureaucratic overreach that destroys rural livelihoods.
Energy Independence and Affordable Power — Unleash American energy production so Minnesota families and businesses are not held hostage by high costs or unreliable supply.
Evenstad has also called for formation of a Bison Caucus within the Republican Party committed to strength, clarity, and results — “to stampede RINOs” and forge a true Lincoln Republican Party focused on the American people rather than internal warfare or personal branding.
“God doesn’t need a party,” Evenstad said. “He needs people willing to stand up. I’ve stood up for nearly thirty years. I’m not stopping now.”
Evenstad resides in Edina, Minnesota. He is a graduate of Edina High School, a born-again Christian, and a longtime activist focused on public safety and prison reform.

Edina, Minnesota

🏈 NFL Week 10 Matchup Review

Washington Commanders (2-5-1) at New York Giants (5-2-1) (-2)

Commanders:

+ Showcase elite ball security, leading the NFC with a +7 turnover differential and only 1 interception thrown all year.

- Passing efficiency is struggling, averaging a modest 6.7 yards per pass attempt.

Giants:

+ Field a premium defensive unit allowing just 301.4 total yards per game, ranking 5th in the NFL.

- The offensive line has given up 27 sacks through 8 games (3.38 per game).

Lean: Commanders (+ 2) 

Exploiting the Giants' Run Defense: The path to a cover relies entirely on Washington's ground efficiency. The Commanders rank 9th in the NFL in yards per rush attempt. They must relentlessly attack a Giants front four that ranks 27th in yards allowed per rush. If Jayden Daniels and the backfield can pick up 5+ yards on early downs, they will neutralize the Giants' pass rush. 

Weaponizing the Red-Zone Inefficiencies: Both teams field highly vulnerable red-zone defenses—the Giants rank 32nd (dead last) and the Commanders rank 29th in opponent red-zone touchdown conversion percentage. In this scenario, Washington maximizes their trips inside the 20, scoring touchdowns instead of field goals, and forces New York into a high-variance shootout. 

Capitalizing on the Giants' QB Uncertainty: The Giants are managing an injury-impacted quarterback room after Jaxson Dart's season-ending knee injury earlier this autumn, leaving J.J. McCarthy to play through a painful hip pointer on a short week. If the Commanders' defense can secure a crucial turnover against a limited McCarthy, their +7 turnover differential will allow them to control the game clock. 

New England Patriots (5-4) vs. Detroit Lions (6-2) (-3)

Patriots:

+ Feature a highly productive passing attack that has racked up 2,349 yards at 8.36 yards per attempt.

- Surrendered a massive 45 points to the Packers last week, raising serious defensive structural questions.

Lions:

+ Boast a top-tier balanced offense averaging 379.8 total yards per game (4th overall).

- The secondary frequently yields high-yardage games when the front four doesn't force immediate sacks.

Lean : Lions (- 3)

The Mismatch: Detroit's Multi-Option Engine vs. New England's Secondary: New England’s defense showed severe cracks in Week 9, surrendering 45 points to Green Bay. Detroit fields an offense that has already cracked over 2,000 yards passing and 1,000 yards rushing in only 8 games. The Patriots' secondary will be forced into a high-stress puzzle trying to simultaneously account for Jahmyr Gibbs out of the backfield, Amon-Ra St. Brown in the intermediate area, and Jameson Williams over the top. 

Turnover Margin Imbalance: Dan Campbell's team plays remarkably clean football, committing just 5 total turnovers all season—the second-fewest in the NFL. Meanwhile, Patriots quarterback Drake Maye has shown immense flash but is still vulnerable to rookie variance mistakes when pressured. In international games, self-inflicted mistakes are magnified due to travel fatigue.

Buffalo Bills (7-1) at New York Jets (2-7) (+7.5)

Bills:

+ Own the league's most lethal scoring unit, averaging a league-high 32.0 points per game.

- Pass protection has shown cracks, surrendering 17 sacks on only 236 dropbacks.

Jets:

+ Maintain a clean short-to-intermediate passing game, hitting a 67.5% completion rate.

- Suffer from poor pass-blocking execution, giving up 28 sacks and 236 lost yards.

Lean : Bills (- 7.5)

Historic Offensive Efficiency: Under the 37-year-old Brady (the youngest head coach in the NFL), the Bills' offense has hit a historic gear. His "Everybody Eats" philosophy has unlocked a league-high 32.0 points per game, keeping Josh Allen playing at an MVP-caliber level. 

The Locker Room "Juice": Players like right tackle Spencer Brown have openly detailed that Brady has injected a "whole new energy and juice" into the exact same roster. This makes Buffalo incredibly dangerous coming off a 23-6 Monday Night blowout of the Vikings, as they don't suffer from the tight, conservative mid-season ruts that sometimes plagued late-era McDermott teams. 

The Defensive Turnaround: The Bills' defense under coordinator Jim Leonhard has hit its stride, allowing just 16 total points over their last two games, which positions them perfectly to dominate a fragile Jets offensive line that has already conceded 28 sacks this season. Buffalo further weaponized its secondary at the trade deadline by acquiring safety Amani Hooker from the Titans for a 2027 second-round pick; Hooker, who currently ties for the NFL lead with five interceptions, will slot in next to rookie Cole Bishop to provide elite, ball-hawking stability that severely caps New York's passing game and reinforces the Bills -7.5 betting lean.

Carolina Panthers (3-5) at New Orleans Saints (3-5) (-2)

Panthers:

+ Run a top-5 high-volume passing offense averaging 261.1 yards per game.

- Suffer from a fragile defense that has let up a total of 219 points.

Saints:

+ Boast lethal, elite efficiency when cracking the opponent's territory, ranking 2nd in the NFL in red-zone touchdown percentage and executing a perfect 11-for-11 (100%) touchdown conversion rate on goal-to-go situations

- Have struggled significantly with home-field advantage, posting an inefficient 1-4 record in New Orleans.

Lean : Panthers (+ 2)

The Volatility Value: When two mathematically inconsistent teams face off, advanced models favor taking the points. The Saints are highly reliant on high-leverage efficiency (their 2nd-ranked red-zone conversion rate), which is prone to regression. If Carolina can simply force New Orleans to settle for a couple of field goals instead of touchdowns, the Panthers' 5th-ranked passing volume (261.1 YPG) will keep them close enough to cover.

The Dome Disadvantage: Home-field advantage is practically non-existent for New Orleans this year. The Saints are a miserable 1-4 straight up at home, showing severe defensive lapses and an inability to protect their own turf.

Kansas City Chiefs (6-2) at Atlanta Falcons (3-6) (+3.5)

Chiefs:

+ Ground game operates with rare efficiency, churning out 137.8 rushing yards per game to rank 4th in the NFL.

- While Patrick Mahomes protects the ball with a low 1.52% interception rate, the passing attack is uncharacteristically shallow, averaging an unusually low 5.74 Average Depth of Target (ADoT).

Falcons:

+ Field an aggressive, high-floor running attack that has piled up 1,235 total rushing yards.

- Pass offense is deeply broken due to decision-making variance, leading the NFL with a catastrophic 4.69% interception rate (12 INTs on 256 attempts).

Lean : Chiefs (- 3.5)

The Interception Avalanche: The defining metric of this matchup is Atlanta's league-worst 4.69% interception rate (12 interceptions on 256 attempts). The Falcons constantly sabotage their own drives with catastrophic aerial mistakes. Kansas City's disciplined secondary excels at baiting mistake-prone quarterbacks into turning the ball over when forced into obvious passing situations.

Early Down Domination: Kansas City sustains drives by suffocating defenses on early downs, executing an elite 51% overall success rate on 1st and 2nd downs. This allows Patrick Mahomes to stay completely ahead of the chains, drain the clock, and dictate the tempo of the game. Atlanta's defense, which struggles to get off the field, will likely face severe fatigue by the second half.

Squeezing the Volume: Atlanta likes to run a heavy downfield script (+4.9% Pass Rate Over Expected), but Kansas City’s balanced defense is designed to completely cap explosive chunk plays. By taking away the deep ball and leaning on their own 4th-ranked ground game (137.8 YPG), the Chiefs will force Atlanta into predictable dropbacks where their high-variance mistakes inevitably multiply.

Houston Texans (3-5) at Cleveland Browns (5-4) (+4.5)

Texans:

+ C.J. Stroud aggressively stretches boundaries, piloting the league with a vertical 9.44 yards Average Depth of Target (ADoT).

- The defense struggles to dictate terms, yielding an inefficient -0.04 defensive EPA/play baseline. 

Browns:

+ Excel at micro-level ball security, yielding a minuscule 1.06% interception rate through 9 weeks.

- Pass protection is fundamentally broken, surrendering a league-worst 38 sacks for 211 lost yards.

Lean : Browns (+ 4.5)

 The Game Spot (Flawless Home Record): The Browns (5-4) return home riding a painful two-game losing skid, creating an urgent, maximum-effort spot to save their season. Cleveland is a perfect 3-0 straight up and against the spread (ATS) at home this season. Conversely, the Texans (3-5) have been highly inefficient on the road, carrying a negative seasonal point differential (-4) primarily fueled by defensive collapses away from Houston.

Defensive Success Rate vs. Explosive Variance: Houston's offense depends entirely on high-variance vertical chunk plays via C.J. Stroud’s league-leading 9.44 Average Depth of Target (ADoT). However, the Browns' home defensive scheme specializes in taking away the deep third, forcing teams into short, methodical drives. Because Houston ranks poorly in rushing success rate on early downs, taking away their deep ball completely stalls their offensive engine.

Minnesota Vikings (6-2) at Green Bay Packers (6-3)(-3.5)

 Vikings:

+ Field a premier defensive front, choking opposing systems out to the tune of just 280.0 total yards allowed per game (2nd in NFL).

- The dropback passing unit hits severe lulls, registering a highly inefficient -0.11 EPA/pass baseline.

Packers:

+ Jordan Love commands a dynamic aerial engine that has piled up a massive, high-volume 2,618 passing yards and 19 touchdowns.

- Structural run-blocking concepts remain highly inefficient, grading out at a poor -0.24 EPA/rush. 

Lean : Packers (- 3.5)

The Brutal Quarterback Transition Spot: While the Minnesota Vikings (6-2) boast a legendary defense, their offensive architecture is in absolute chaos. Following a lopsided loss to the Bills on Monday Night Football, the front office frantically traded a 2027 third-round pick to the Raiders on Tuesday to bring back a familiar face in Kirk Cousins. Cousins is being thrust immediately into a short week of practice to learn a completely new structural terminology, creating an incredibly high-pressure road environment against a blossoming Green Bay defense that ranks 10th in the NFL in EPA per play. 

Jordan Love's Scorching Efficiency: Jordan Love enters Week 10 playing at an elite level, fresh off taking home NFL Player of the Week honors. In Week 9, Love tore apart a highly respected Patriots defense by throwing for 372 yards and 3 touchdowns with zero interceptions, posting a near-flawless 153.2 passer rating. Love commands a highly explosive, vertical engine that has already logged a massive 2,618 passing yards and 19 touchdowns through nine weeks. 

The 4th-Quarter Revenge Script: Minnesota comfortably handled Green Bay back in Week 1 (39-22), but the raw box score masks how the actual gameplay flowed. Love was actually systematically carving up the Vikings' secondary for the first two and a half quarters, dialing up massive chunk plays to Christian Watson (147 yards, 2 TDs) before a late-game fourth-quarter collapse skewed the final score. Now returning to a hostile, freezing outdoor Lambeau environment, the Packers' complete team structure—the only NFC North squad ranking in the top 10 in both offensive and defensive EPA—is perfectly optimized to choke out a discombobulated Minnesota offense. 

Jacksonville Jaguars (6-2) at Tennessee Titans (1-7) (+10.5)

Jaguars:

+ Match top-tier offensive output with elite ball security, generating an exceptional +9 turnover differential.

- The run defense shows high volatility, yielding a high 46% rushing success rate on first and second downs.

Titans:

+ Play with high defensive discipline upfront, limiting explosive over-the-top chunk plays to a minimal 4.1% rate.

- The dropback passing structure is completely stagnant, managing a non-viable -0.18 EPA/pass baseline.

Lean : Jaguars (- 10.5)

The Ultimate Point Differential Machine: Head coach Liam Coen has turned Jacksonville into the most ruthless point-margin squad in professional football. The Jaguars lead the NFL with a historic +108 seasonal point differential (+13.5 points per game). They do not let up when playing with a lead, as evidenced by consecutive double-digit blowouts over the last two weeks where they absolutely dismantled the Colts 42-7 and the Ravens 33-10. 

A Total Defensive Teardown in Tennessee: Whatever early-season structural success the Titans' defense had has officially evaporated due to roster liquidation. General Manager Mike Borgonzi has conceded the 2026 season. Over the last two weeks, the Titans traded away their two most foundational, high-level defenders: All-Pro defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons (to the Bears) and star safety Amani Hooker (to the Bills). 

The Secondary Mismatch: Trevor Lawrence enters Week 10 playing at an elite level, posting 1,932 yards, 18 touchdowns, and zero interceptions over his last two outings. He matches up against a hollowed-out Tennessee secondary that already ranks 31st in the NFL by allowing 258.3 passing yards per game. Without Hooker to patrol the deep third, Lawrence and breakout receiver Parker Washington (17.0 yards per catch, 5 TDs) are set to trigger massive chunk-play explosive variance over the top. 

The Ball Security Margin: Jacksonville leads the NFL with a +9 turnover differential. Conversely, the Titans are starting sophomore quarterback Cam Ward behind a leaky protection scheme. Ward must navigate a stagnant offense generating just 15.1 points per game against a Jaguars defense that has held five of its last six opponents under 20 points. 

Neutralized Rest Spot: While the Titans are returning from a Week 9 bye, any rest advantage is heavily minimized. Because Jacksonville played on Thursday Night Football in Week 9, they enter Nissan Stadium on a 10-day mini-bye schedule, giving their coaching staff ample time to scheme against a depleted division rival.

Miami Dolphins (1-7) at Indianapolis Colts (2-7) (-3.5)

Dolphins:
+ Coming off a good Week 9 performance where they held the NFL’s top-ranked Detroit Lions offense to a season-low 19 points and 270 total yards, choking out their ground attack to a stellar 3.8 yards per carry average and holding them to a 25% (3-for-12) conversion rate on third downs.

- Fail to stay ahead of schedule on dropbacks, landing at a highly inefficient -0.14 EPA/pass metric. 

Colts:

+ Execute a highly physical short-yardage rushing identity, pounding home 11 interior rushing touchdowns through 9 weeks.

- Their dropback passing game is deeply flawed, operating at an NFL-worst -0.25 EPA/pass. 

Lean: Colts (-3.5)

The Staggering Dolphins QB Emergency: The handicap of this game completely shifted on Tuesday when Miami officially placed starting quarterback Malik Willis on Injured Reserve with a severe groin tear. This forces rookie backup Kyle McCord to make his raw NFL debut on the road in a noisy domed environment. McCord is being thrown straight into the fire behind an offense that has already lost its top weapon, De'Von Achane, for the season. Forcing a rookie to navigate a highly complex defensive system in his first-ever snaps gives the Colts a massive mechanical edge. 

The Ground Identity Domination: Under head coach Shane Steichen, the Colts' entire organizing principle revolves around Jonathan Taylor. Taylor enters Week 10 with 656 rushing yards and 8 touchdowns, running with elite efficiency on gap-scheme concepts. Miami’s defense just lost its emotional and physical anchor, defensive tackle Zach Sieler, to a season-ending ruptured biceps. Without Sieler cloging the interior A-gaps, Taylor and a highly physical Colts offensive line are primed to completely dictate the line of scrimmage, sustain long drives, and bleed the game clock.

The Trade Deadline Roster Nuance: While the Colts made news by trading wideouts Keenan Allen and Josh Downs to acquire future draft capital, their remaining architecture remains functional. Daniel Jones still has dynamic tight end Tyler Warren (38 catches) and an athletic vertical piece in Adonai Mitchell to keep the defense honest. By utilizing multiple tight-end sets, Indy can shield Jones, lean heavily on their 156-yard baseline rushing chunk packages, and systematically squeeze a depleted Dolphins roster. 

Seattle Seahawks (5-4) at Las Vegas Raiders (4-5) (+6.5)

+ Anchor the entire league defensively, leading all 32 teams by allowing an elite, suffocating 244.2 total yards per game.

- The dropback passing game has fallen out of rhythm, generating a sluggish -0.09 team EPA/play baseline.

Raiders:
+ The intermediate passing script boasts significant volume, generating 2,401 total passing yards and 20 touchdowns. That being said, the Raiders are set to start rookie Fernando Mendoza, who will be making his first NFL start.

- The ground offense functions without a physical floor, bottoming out at an inefficient -0.17 EPA/rush.

Lean: Seahawks (- 6.5)

The Absolute Quarterback Nightmare Spot: The handicap of this game completely flipped at the trade deadline. The Raiders traded away starting quarterback Kirk Cousins to the Minnesota Vikings, completely plunging their offensive architecture into development mode. Las Vegas is officially starting rookie Fernando Mendoza—the No. 1 overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft—for his first career professional start. Forcing a rookie to make his debut against head coach Mike Macdonald’s highly complex defensive system is a historic recipe for a multi-score disaster. 

The Stingiest Yardage Prevention vs. Unidirectional Stagnation: Seattle enters Week 10 fielding a premier, top-4 scoring defense that holds opposing offenses to a suffocating 18.0 points allowed per game. Under Macdonald, they specialize in completely confusing young quarterbacks with disguised coverages. They match up against a completely unidirectional Raiders offense that ranks dead last in the league with a miserable 2.9 yards per rush attempt. Because Las Vegas cannot run the football, the Seahawks' front seven will relentlessly pin their ears back and force Mendoza into predictable, heavy-pressure third-and-long dropbacks. 

The Turnovers and Protection Disparity: Even with Sam Darnold sidelined, backup Drew Lock proved highly serviceable in a physical 17-3 dismantling of the Cardinals in Week 9, running a highly disciplined, low-risk approach behind an elite defense. The Raiders' offense under Klint Kubiak is inherently mistake-prone, surrendered by a defense that ranks dead last in the NFL by allowing an astronomical 29.8 points per game. Seattle's +5 turnover differential will allow them to secure short fields off rookie mistakes and dominate time of possession. 

Los Angeles Rams (5-4) at Arizona Cardinals (3-6) (-9.5)

Rams:+ Pilot a premier, balanced offensive engine that features an outstanding 53% success rate on dropbacks.

- Pass defense can be highly volatile, yielding an elevated 2.58% interception-to-attempt ratio on deep targets. 

Cardinals:

+ Special teams play acts as an elite field position weapon, grading out 3rd overall in analytics chart tracking.

- Plunged into an immediate offensive emergency following Gardner Minshew's season-ending injury, forcing rookie Carson Beck into a brutal debut against a top-tier pass rush.

Lean: Rams (- 9.5)

The Quarterback Catastrophe: The entire baseline handicap of this divisional matchup transformed after a brutal Week 9 slate. Arizona starter Gardner Minshew suffered a season-ending elbow injury against Seattle. This directly forces third-round rookie Carson Beck into making his raw NFL debut against a highly complex, premium pass rush. 

A Historically Terrifying Defensive Edge: Even with Puka Nacua and Davante Adams currently managing injuries in the wideout room, Sean McVay's squad can lean entirely on its upgraded, star-studded defense. The front office paired All-Pro anchor Aaron Donald with blockbuster trade deadline acquisition Myles Garrett (who recorded 3 sacks last week). Forcing a rookie quarterback in his very first professional start to process post-snap coverage disguises while Donald and Garrett collapse the pocket is a structural recipe for a multi-turnover disaster.

A Starless, Depleted Arizona Roster: The structural bleeding for the Cardinals doesn't stop under center. Head coach Mike LaFleur lost his undisputed No. 1 wide receiver, Michael Wilson, to a season-ending fractured neck. With top pick Marvin Harrison Jr. already traded away earlier this year, Arizona's entire offensive output rests completely on tight end Trey McBride. Jim Leonhard's secondary can bracket McBride on every single third down, forcing a limited Beck to look elsewhere. 

Offensive Floor Domination: Even if McVay operates a simplified passing script for Matthew Stafford, the Rams own a top-4 total offense generating a dominant 379.8 yards per game. Running back Kyren Williams (593 yards, 6 TDs) is perfectly optimized to chew up an Arizona defense that sits near the bottom of the league by allowing an astronomical 28.3 points per game.

San Francisco 49ers (7-1) at Dallas Cowboys (4-5) (+4)

49ers:

+ Set the absolute benchmark for modern offensive efficiency, leading the NFL with a historic 0.14 overall EPA/play and a 52.09% success rate.

- Red-zone situational defense occasionally bends, ranking 22nd in defensive success rate inside the 20.

Cowboys:

+ Lean heavily on a high-volume passing concept that has generated 2,381 yards and 16 aerial touchdowns.

- Field a fundamentally broken coverage unit that ranks 31st in the NFL by surrendering a massive 8.4 yards per pass attempt and allowing an inefficient +0.18 defensive EPA/pass baseline, leaving them completely exposed to explosive vertical concepts.

Lean: 49ers (- 4)

The Ultimate Analytical Mismatch: The 49ers  dominate the structural margins of this game, operating with a league-best 0.14 overall EPA/play and a 52.09% offensive success rate. Dallas fields a completely broken coverage unit that sits 31st in the NFL, giving up 8.4 yards per pass attempt and a highly inefficient +0.18 defensive EPA/pass baseline.

Red-Zone Inefficiency Exposure: When Dallas fails to sustain deep drives, their offense completely stalls. The 49ers lead the NFL with an astronomical 84.62% red-zone touchdown conversion rate (scoring touchdowns on 22 of their 26 trips inside the 20). Dallas, by comparison, relies on field goals far too often and cannot match the continuous seven-point output of Kyle Shanahan's offense. 

The Trade Deadline Masterstroke: To counter lingering injury concerns, John Lynch traded for 6-time Pro Bowl veteran Keenan Allen from the Colts on Tuesday. Allen immediately stabilizes Brock Purdy’s underneath passing concepts, matching up perfectly against a Dallas scheme that struggles to pass-cover condensed splits. 

One-Dimensional Structural Doom: The Cowboys are completely non-viable on the ground, struggling at a miserable -0.02 EPA/rush on an inefficient 38% rushing success rate. Because Dallas cannot lean on a run game to bleed the clock or keep Purdy off the field, the 49ers’ defense can aggressively pin their ears back, compress the pocket, and force Dak Prescott into heavy-pressure mistakes.
