text:
Fang Fang, Alice Huang, and the MSS Playbook: A Chinese Spy Network Bred Under Democrats, From Swalwell and Comey to Jensen Huang Under Biden-Harris. 

On November 8, 2026, Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang told his employees he had been unfaithful to his wife. He did not name the woman. The reporting already had: Alice Huang, no relation, a Chinese citizen and the face of Megaspeed, a Singapore company that bought billions of dollars in Nvidia chips. U.S. officials believe China's Ministry of State Security recruited her. Beijing calls that a smear, and she has not been charged. But the shape of this story is familiar. We saw it before, in California, with a Democratic congressman named Eric Swalwell. Both stories took root under Democrats, and the second is still unfolding. 

Start with the file we can read. In August 2026, the Trump White House declassified the FBI's records on Christine Fang, known as Fang Fang. The bureau classified both of her parents as known MSS intelligence officers. She ran straw donations through conduits into Swalwell's campaigns, steered interns into his offices, and raised money across Bay Area Democratic politics. Swalwell admitted to the FBI that he had sexual encounters with her. The case was code-named Freshman Fifteen. 

James Comey ran the FBI from September 2013 to May 2017. Freshman Fifteen, opened March 17, 2014, lived its whole life on his watch. In February 2017 the bureau dropped Swalwell as a subject. The closing memo on Fang is dated May 2, 2017. That memo lists what the bureau believed she had done: illegal foreign contributions, destroyed records, false statements, bulk cash smuggling, and acting as an unregistered foreign agent. Then came the verdict on all of it: prosecution was non-viable due to national security reasons, reached after consultation between the San Francisco Division's executive management and the U.S. Attorney's Office for the Northern District of California. The Public Integrity Section, then headed by Jack Smith, declined as well. Comey did not sign that call alone. But nothing in that case moved without his bureau. 

Fang did not wait for the paperwork. Around May 2015, agents searched her home, the FBI gave Swalwell a defensive briefing, and she vanished to China. The State Department barred her from coming back. No public record shows that John Brennan, James Comey, or Loretta Lynch ever tried to bring her back for questioning or arrest. They let her walk. Swalwell kept his seat for more than a decade afterward, sat on the House Intelligence Committee, and saw the House Ethics Committee close its review in 2023 with no action. The Democratic Party's golden boy from the East Bay stayed golden until his own staff scandal ended his career in April 2026. 

There is an objection, and it deserves a direct answer. The declassified files show the FBI tried to recruit Fang as an informant before it ever investigated her. An undercover employee first sat down with her in Las Vegas in May 2013. She signed a contract with a bureau front company on June 14, 2013, under the code name Rusty Thumbs. All of that predates Comey's directorship, though not his place in the national security world: he had served as George W. Bush's deputy attorney general before leaving for Lockheed Martin. So, the argument goes, the soft handling was spycraft, not protection. 

It cuts less than it appears. If Rusty Thumbs had been turned into a working American asset, eleven years is a long time for the bureau, the Justice Department, and every Democrat who has defended Swalwell to sit on the one fact that would vindicate them. And if she had been turned, Washington would have held a live window into the very network she came from, through the Obama-Biden years and into Biden-Harris. Then explain Alice Huang. A flipped Fang should have made the next woman harder to place, not easier...

Always a pleasure to meet with the Head of the EU Delegation in Albania, Ambassador Sofia Moreira de Sousa @EuAmbAL, and all the more so to receive a copy of the 2026 Progress Report for Albania, the most comprehensive, detailed and wide-ranging annual assessment of the country’s progress and its overall level of preparedness for European Union membership. 🇦🇱🇪🇺

The Report must be read as a whole. We should welcome the substantial and meaningful progress achieved, which confirms that we are on the right track and that Albania is able not only to make commitments, but also to deliver on them. At the same time, we must remain fully aware, clear-eyed and determined about the challenges that remain, and address them through inclusive processes, constructive engagement and genuine dialogue.

The Commission’s roadmap towards 2027 provides us with a clear direction. For the first time, our objective of concluding accession negotiations by the end of 2027 is reflected in an EU document as an ambitious but achievable goal. Reaching it will require sustained effort, high-quality reforms and, above all, effective and consistent implementation.

The Ministry for Europe and Foreign Affairs remains fully committed to further strengthening its institutional capacities and playing its full part in this decisive final stretch of the negotiations.

We are grateful to our partners in the European Commission, including the EU Delegation in Albania, and to all Member States for their continued support, understanding and partnership. We are equally grateful to our negotiating team for its dedication, professionalism and hard work.

Joining the European Union is out top national goal and project, and a whole-of-society endeavour, just as the benefits of membership will belong to society as a whole and It requires everyone’s contribution. 

--

Është gjithmonë kënaqësi të takohem me Shefen e Delegacionit të Bashkimit Evropian në Shqipëri, Ambasadoren Sofia Moreira de Sousa @EuAmbAL, dhe aq më tepër të marr prej saj një kopje të Raportit të Progresit 2026 për Shqipërinë, vlerësimit vjetor më gjithëpërfshirës, të detajuar dhe të gjerë mbi progresin e vendit dhe nivelin e përgjithshëm të përgatitjes së tij për anëtarësim në Bashkimin Evropian. 🇦🇱🇪🇺

Raporti duhet lexuar si një i tërë. Duhet të mirëpresim progresin thelbësor dhe domethënës të arritur, i cili konfirmon se jemi në rrugën e duhur dhe se Shqipëria është e aftë jo vetëm të marrë angazhime, por edhe t’i përmbushë ato. Në të njëjtën kohë, duhet të jemi plotësisht të vetëdijshëm, realistë dhe të vendosur përballë sfidave që mbeten, duke i adresuar ato përmes proceseve gjithëpërfshirëse, angazhimit konstruktiv dhe dialogut të mirëfilltë.

Udhërrëfyesi i Komisionit drejt vitit 2027 na jep një drejtim të qartë. Për herë të parë, objektivi ynë për përfundimin e negociatave të anëtarësimit deri në fund të vitit 2027 është pasqyruar në një dokument të Bashkimit Evropian si një objektiv ambicioz, por i arritshëm. Arritja e tij do të kërkojë përpjekje të vazhdueshme, reforma cilësore dhe, mbi të gjitha, zbatim efektiv dhe të qëndrueshëm.

Ministria për Evropën dhe Punët e Jashtme mbetet plotësisht e angazhuar për forcimin e mëtejshëm të kapaciteteve të saj institucionale dhe për të luajtur plotësisht rolin që i takon në këtë fazë përfundimtare dhe vendimtare të negociatave.

U jemi mirënjohës partnerëve tanë në Komisionin Evropian, përfshirë Delegacionin e BE-së në Shqipëri, si dhe të gjitha shteteve anëtare, për mbështetjen e vazhdueshme, mirëkuptimin dhe partneritetin e tyre. Po aq mirënjohës jemi edhe ndaj ekipit tonë negociator për përkushtimin, profesionalizmin dhe punën e palodhur.

Anëtarësimi në Bashkimin Evropian është objektivi dhe projekti ynë më i rëndësishëm kombëtar. Është një përpjekje e gjithë shoqërisë, ashtu siç përfitimet e anëtarësimit do t’i përkasin të gjithë shoqërisë. Për ta realizuar këtë projekt, nevojitet kontributi i të gjithëve.

text:
Gavin Newsom WANTS TO ERASE THE DEATH SENTENCES OF TWO CONVICTED COP K*LLERS, including one who BEAT AN OFFICER WITH A METAL PIPE, STOLE HIS GUN, AND SH*T HIM TWICE IN THE HEAD.

And the Riverside Police Chief is FURIOUS, saying Newsom's decision has reopened wounds for families who have already endured years of grief, trials, and appeals.

Riverside Police Chief Larry V. Gonzalez publicly condemned the California governor's sweeping November 5, 2026, announcement to commute all 548 death sentences in the state to life imprisonment without parole.

Among those facing commutation are Steve Woodruff and Earl Ellis Green, who were sentenced to death for m*rdering Riverside Detective Charles “Doug” Jacobs III and Officer Ryan Patrick Bonaminio in separate attacks.
The details of their m*rders are devastating.

On January 13, 2001, Detective Jacobs, 30, and Officer Ben Baker responded to a loud music complaint at a home on Lemon Street in Riverside.

Jacobs was a five-year veteran of the department and a husband and father.

During the call, Woodruff emerged from the residence and opened fire, striking Jacobs in the head and killing him.

Woodruff also fired at Baker, leading to a separate attempted m*rder conviction.

A Riverside County jury sentenced Woodruff to death in 2003.

After the California Supreme Court ordered a new penalty phase, a SECOND JURY reviewed the case in 2021 and again determined that Woodruff deserved the de*th penalty.

Jacobs left behind his wife, a 6-month-old daughter, and a 10-year-old stepson.

Nine years later, Riverside suffered another devastating loss.

On November 7, 2010, Officer Ryan Patrick Bonaminio was attempting to stop a stolen tractor-trailer connected to a hit-and-run when the driver fled into Fairmount Park.

Bonaminio pursued the suspect on foot.

The man, later identified as Earl Ellis Green, attacked the officer with a metal pipe, knocked him to the ground, and disarmed him.

Green then used Bonaminio's own service weapon to sho*t him twice in the head.

The officer was just 27 years old.

Bonaminio was also a U.S. Army veteran who had served two tours in Iraq as a military police officer before returning home to protect his community.

Green, who had a prior criminal record and was on parole at the time of the m*rder, was convicted and sentenced to de*th in 2012.

And now, 16 years after Bonaminio was killed, his family is being forced to confront another painful development.

Newsom announced his plan on November 5, just TWO DAYS before the anniversary of Bonaminio's murder.

Chief Gonzalez addressed that timing in a November 8 statement, expressing anger over the additional suffering caused to both officers' families.

“The decision to commute the death sentences of the killers of Fallen Riverside Police Detective Charles ‘Doug’ Jacobs III and Fallen Riverside Police Officer Ryan Patrick Bonaminio brings renewed pain to families who have endured unimaginable loss,” Gonzalez said.

He emphasized that the families had already endured multiple court proceedings and listened to the evidence surrounding their loved ones' deaths.

In Jacobs' case, two separate juries had reached the same conclusion about the appropriate punishment.

Gonzalez said families should not have to question whether their suffering or those judgments matter.

The chief also reaffirmed the department's commitment to supporting the surviving relatives and preserving the officers' legacies.

Newsom, meanwhile, has defended his statewide clemency plan by arguing that California cannot morally continue imposing capital punishment.

The Democratic governor previously halted executions in 2019, although California voters had upheld the death penalty in statewide elections in both 2012 and 2016.

Under his new proposal, every current death sentence would be converted to life imprisonment without the possibility of parole.

The prisoners would remain behind bars for life, but they would no longer face execution.

Because 382 of the condemned inmates have multiple felony convictions, California's Constitution requires a recommendation from at least four state Supreme Court justices before Newsom can finalize their commutations.

The governor has begun that process, but the proposed sentence changes have not yet taken effect.

Riverside County District Attorney Mike Hestrin has also criticized the decision and confirmed that prosecutors are exploring legal challenges, potentially involving the California Supreme Court.

Law enforcement unions throughout Riverside County have joined the opposition, arguing that blanket clemency disregards the individual circumstances of m*rders for which juries imposed death sentences.

The controversy comes as Newsom prepares to leave office in January, with speculation continuing about a possible presidential campaign in 2028.

For the families of Detective Jacobs and Officer Bonaminio, however, this is about the men they lost.

One was ambushed while responding to a routine noise complaint. The other was beaten and executed with his own firearm while pursuing a fleeing suspect.

Both were serving their communities when their lives were taken, and their families have spent years seeking justice through the courts.

Chief Gonzalez made clear that the Riverside Police Department will continue standing beside them.

“We will speak their names, honor their memories, and stand with the people they left behind.” We will, too.

#Riverside #BackTheBlue #California #DeathPenalty #Newsom #RPD

text:
Congress weighs tighter chip curbs. Can NVIDIA keep Washington at bay?👇
⠀
The board at NVIDIA ($NVDA) launched an investigation on Sunday to clarify media reports that CEO Jensen Huang became the target of a foreign intelligence operation.
⠀
In the same statement, the board said it had no reason to believe company secrets or national security were harmed and expressed confidence in Huang's leadership.
⠀
The chip designer's market cap hit $4.5 trillion on Nov. 6, 2026.
⠀
Huang held 3.6% as of late March 2026, worth more than $150 billion at recent prices.
⠀
Whether he stays or leaves also raises the risk of a leadership disruption; Seeking Alpha noted that's one of the issues the board probe has put on investors' radar.
⠀
-----
⠀
🔴 Follow me on X: @rich_compass
⠀
U.S. stock, crypto, and technical analysis
⠀
-----

▋ The board faces scrutiny for defending Jensen Huang on day one
⠀
The statement didn't name the person involved or describe the nature of Huang's relationship with that person.
⠀
A committee of independent directors oversees how the probe is run, with help from outside independent lawyers.
⠀
The board said the investigation will review 'all available information'; Huang fully supports it and has promised to cooperate.
⠀
The board also called U.S. national and economic security a priority and critical to NVIDIA and shareholder interests.
⠀
It also said it would provide updates in due course, but didn't announce a deadline for finishing the probe.
⠀
That creates some timing tension.
⠀
The board says it wants to get to the bottom of this, yet before the probe even started it said it had no reason to believe secrets or national security were harmed.
⠀
Harry Kraemer Jr., a former Baxter International CEO and management scholar now teaching at Northwestern's business school, called that stance 'inappropriate' and said, 'That's how you lose credibility.'
⠀
Some public company directors at The Wall Street Journal's board council meeting on Monday questioned whether NVIDIA's board was too quick to protect Huang or accepted his assurances about the relationship from the start, the paper reported.
⠀
The importance of succession planning also came up in the directors' discussion of the matter.
⠀
Heidrick & Struggles CEO Tom Monahan said every company should think about management depth, succession, and risk management.

▋ The intelligence probe into Alice Huang and Megaspeed chip sales
⠀
Alice Huang is a Chinese citizen, also known as Huang Le, and is not related to Jensen Huang.
⠀
She was a senior executive at Singapore data center company Megaspeed International at the time.
⠀
The Wall Street Journal reported earlier that U.S. officials concluded last year she shared information with the Chinese government while working with NVIDIA to build data centers in Asia.
⠀
Reuters, citing a New York Times report last month, said Huang and Alice Huang had a close relationship and that she was suspected of providing information directly to Beijing.
⠀
Reuters said it couldn't independently verify those allegations or Alice Huang's current role at Megaspeed, and couldn't determine her whereabouts.
⠀
Seeking Alpha, citing The New York Times and people familiar with the matter, reported that a highly classified memo warning senior officials about Huang's relationship with Alice Huang was drafted under Secretary of State Rubio's supervision.
⠀
Seeking Alpha's account said electronic surveillance was the basis for that warning, and U.S. officials concluded from it that Alice Huang had been recruited by China's Ministry of State Security.
⠀
ShareCast also reported that U.S. officials concluded Alice Huang was recruited by China's Ministry of State Security, an intelligence agency.
⠀
When authorities began surveilling her in late 2024, she disappeared in China for a while, the Wall Street Journal reported.
⠀
Her current whereabouts are unknown, as is whether she still holds a senior position at Megaspeed.
⠀
The company was spun off from a Chinese company in 2023, is based in Singapore, and builds data centers across Southeast Asia.
⠀
It's one of several companies that partnered with NVIDIA and promised to use its chips in data centers.
⠀
It rents out computing power to customers, a business under scrutiny for potentially moving chips to China and letting Chinese customers use the compute.
⠀
Reuters, citing Megaspeed's website, said the company is NVIDIA's cloud partner in Asia Pacific and offers GB200 NVL72 and HGX H100 chips.
⠀
In early 2025, Alice Huang and business partner Kang Wei pitched investors on a Southeast Asia data center project worth hundreds of millions of dollars, using access to NVIDIA chips as a selling point.
⠀
One investor told the Financial Times they assured backers there was 'no problem' getting chips and described Alibaba as a customer for the project.
⠀
Alibaba was a major customer of Megaspeed's Southeast Asia cloud services from the start and has remained its biggest customer.
⠀
Company documents say Alibaba lent money to Megaspeed in June 2024 through Singapore subsidiary Apex Enterprise Solutions.
⠀
The loan was arranged through Malaysian company Speedmatrix, which used the entire business as collateral.
⠀
Megaspeed's balance sheet ballooned from $33 million to $3 billion in 2024.
⠀
This is Live Mint's account of the Financial Times report, not a court finding that she illegally moved chips to China.
⠀
Megaspeed bought more than $4.8 billion of chips from NVIDIA over two years, Seeking Alpha reported, citing The New York Times.
⠀
Business Today put it differently: the company acquired at least $4.8 billion of AI equipment containing NVIDIA chips between June 2024 and February 2026; in November 2025 it also imported at least 17,544 GB300 chips worth about $787 million.
⠀
Seeking Alpha's account said that even after The New York Times disclosed the Commerce Department was investigating whether Megaspeed helped move restricted AI chips into China, NVIDIA kept selling to the company.
⠀
Opening an investigation is not itself a finding of wrongdoing, Seeking Alpha noted in its report.
⠀
The probe into Megaspeed and its potential ties to the Chinese government has lasted more than a year, with U.S. agencies including the Commerce Department and the Justice Department involved, people familiar with the matter told the Wall Street Journal.
⠀
Those people said Megaspeed came up in recent discussions about whether to add dozens of companies to the U.S. entity list, a debate that includes companies based in China or tied to Chinese firms.
⠀
For now, Megaspeed and other companies haven't been added, and agency officials have left the decision to senior officials involved in U.S. and China trade talks.
⠀
In August 2025, NVIDIA general counsel Tim Teter wrote to a Commerce Department Bureau of Industry and Security staffer, saying senior Commerce official Jeff Kessler had agreed they could reach out about the Megaspeed case.
⠀
The staffer declined to meet and forwarded the letter to Kessler.
⠀
Kessler replied that the case had to be handled strictly by the book.
⠀
The Justice Department later asked Commerce to pause, Commerce complied, and the probe shifted to a criminal investigation by Justice.
⠀
The Next Web reported that follow-up, citing The New York Times, and said it hadn't independently verified it.
⠀
Megaspeed couldn't immediately be reached for comment at the time, the Wall Street Journal reported.
⠀
The company had previously described itself as 'a company that follows the law and is legitimate.'
⠀
On Alice Huang's alleged ties to a Chinese intelligence agency, Singapore's Ministry of Home Affairs said it 'did not conduct any investigation.'
⠀
A Singapore Police Force representative said the investigation into Megaspeed is ongoing and didn't provide details.
⠀
China's embassy in Washington has previously denied the espionage allegations, saying China opposes hyping the narrative and that its technological development is based on 'independent innovation.'

▋ Jensen Huang apologizes for an affair but NVIDIA says business will not slow down
⠀
Jensen Huang sent an internal message to employees on Sunday apologizing for being unfaithful to his wife.
⠀
He said, 'I owe my family and all of you an apology,' and added that his actions hurt his wife and children, with 'no excuse.'
⠀
NVIDIA had first denied the relationship, and Huang later admitted it himself, the Wall Street Journal noted.
⠀
An NVIDIA spokesperson said 'today's news won't slow NVIDIA down' and added that Huang is committed to continuing as CEO without interruption.
⠀
He will stay CEO while the investigation proceeds, according to Seeking Alpha, citing The New York Times.
⠀
NVIDIA previously said that given business dealings, Huang's interactions with Alice Huang were 'not unusual or unexpected.'
⠀
On the operations front, Ryu Jemyung, vice minister of South Korea's Ministry of Science and ICT, told a National Assembly budget committee on Monday that the controversy affecting NVIDIA won't affect South Korea's already contracted GPU supply, and that previously contracted NVIDIA GPU deliveries are still on schedule.

▋ Shares fall over 4% and prediction markets price in leadership risk
⠀
After the board announced the investigation, NVIDIA shares fell 4% in Monday premarket trading.
⠀
Another Wall Street Journal report the same day put the latest premarket drop at 5.4%.
⠀
Yahoo Finance market data shows NVDA closed at $178.67 on Nov. 9, 2026, down 4.27% from the prior trading day's close of $186.64, a drop of $7.97.
⠀
That same day, a shareholder filed a civil class action.
⠀
TechCrunch wrote that New York law firm Rosen, representing investor Mark Kistenmacher, sued NVIDIA and Huang in the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of California.
⠀
The case docket page lists case number 5:26-cv-13448, filed Nov. 9, under securities law, as a class action.
⠀
TechCrunch wrote the proposed class period is Oct. 9, 2025 to Nov. 8, 2026; Kistenmacher made seven purchases this year totaling about $20,500.
⠀
The complaint points to three public statements: spokesperson John Rizzo said in late October that Huang's interactions with Alice Huang were 'not unusual or unexpected'; the company earlier said it found no evidence chips were transshipped; and Huang told Bloomberg on Oct. 30 that dealings with Megaspeed were 'normal and not unusual.'
⠀
The complaint claims those three statements were false or misleading because Huang and Alice Huang had a private relationship.
⠀
These are the complaint's allegations, and a court hasn't decided who is right or wrong.
⠀
TechCrunch wrote that the closing drop gives plaintiffs' lawyers a lot to work with.
⠀
TechCrunch also cautioned that a law firm's investigation notice, or this new lawsuit, doesn't mean the case has merit.
⠀
NVIDIA stock is roughly flat this year and about 22% below its October high, according to data in the Wall Street Journal's Monday premarket report.
⠀
Semiconductor stocks sold off last week, and Democratic midterm election wins intensified market anxiety about the AI trade that had been building for weeks, the Wall Street Journal reported.
⠀
Prediction markets also put odds on it.
⠀
Benzinga reported Polymarket priced a 35% chance Huang resigns or is removed by year end, and Kalshi priced a 35% chance he is removed before July 1, 2027.
⠀
Those prices reflect how market participants see the probability of an event.
⠀
NVIDIA's market cap rose from about $420 billion at the end of 2022 to $4.5 trillion on Nov. 6, 2026, according to data cited by Reuters.

▋ Analysts warn innovation could slow without a clear successor to Jensen Huang
⠀
Analysts cited by The Wall Street Journal said the investigation will at least trigger a congressional probe and pressure the stock.
⠀
Yorkville Ives analyst Dan Ives and others wrote that Huang will likely stay CEO near term without interruption, but the board probe's outcome creates a possibility he's removed.
⠀
They think this will add stock risk because Huang is so central to NVIDIA's global story and strategy, and it will increase U.S. scrutiny of chip sales to China.
⠀
Citrini Research's Jukan Choe thinks Huang's influence over NVIDIA is too large, and the company lacks an obvious successor.
⠀
Choe noted the company has kept a culture similar to a startup even as it scaled, largely driven by the cofounder; if Huang's leadership is weakened, there are concerns innovation could slow.
⠀
Bernstein analysts said there's no immediate clear successor if Huang is unwilling or unable to keep leading; they put it this way: 'NVIDIA is not a normal company, and Jensen is not a normal CEO; he is NVIDIA.'
⠀
Seeking Alpha noted that for investors, the probe raises questions about protecting NVIDIA's confidential information, oversight of customer relationships, and possible leadership disruption; those issues are especially important for a company whose chips power AI systems.

▋ Over sixty direct reports and no succession plan expose governance concerns
⠀
NVIDIA has no chairman and no succession plan, the Wall Street Journal noted.
⠀
Other famous tech founders often keep control through huge stakes or shares with super voting rights, the paper noted.
⠀
The board agenda is set jointly by Huang and lead independent director Stephen Neal, former Cooley CEO, and the two decide what information directors get and run meetings.
⠀
Only about 1% of Russell 3000 public companies have no chairman.
⠀
The Wall Street Journal reported that as of spring 2026, 3 of NVIDIA's 10 independent directors had served 25 years or more, and 2 more had served over 10 years.
⠀
The company's 2026 annual meeting proxy gives different numbers: the board had 10 people, 9 were nominated as independent directors, and Huang was the one company executive who wasn't independent.
⠀
On the proxy, Tench Coxe and Harvey C. Jones had served since 1993, A. Brooke Seawell since 1997, making all three over 25 years by spring 2026; Dawn Hudson had served since 2013 and Mark A. Stevens' current term dated to 2008, making both over 10 years.
⠀
John O. Dabiri, Melissa B. Lora, Stephen C. Neal, and Aarti Shah had served less than 10 years.
⠀
Those 3 and 2 counts still stand, except the independent directors are 9, not 10.
⠀
The Wall Street Journal also cited a comparison: directors at large U.S. companies serve less than 8 years on average, and only about 10% serve more than 10 years.
⠀
The proxy and NVIDIA's May 8 press release both say Suzanne Nora Johnson joined on July 13, 2026, taking the board from 10 to 11 members.
⠀
The spring count didn't include her.
⠀
Proxy adviser ISS gave NVIDIA's board structure its highest risk rating in spring 2026, citing multiple long serving directors, no chairman, and no board refreshment mechanism.
⠀
Over the past five years, NVIDIA added only two directors: former Taco Bell international president Melissa Lora in 2023 and former Goldman Sachs vice chairman Suzanne Nora Johnson this summer.
⠀
Some corporate governance experts say a lead independent director is usually enough.
⠀
In earlier years, boards often met rarely, or never without the CEO present; that's the Wall Street Journal's description of companies generally, not NVIDIA specifically.
⠀
A lead independent director can also act as a check on a CEO who is also chairman.
⠀
The paper also wrote that Stephen Neal schedules quarterly private meetings without Huang.
⠀
The company proxy says independent directors hold closed sessions with only independent directors present, and also meet with the CEO present; in fiscal 2026, both types met at four regular board meetings.
⠀
David Astorino, a senior partner at leadership advisory firm RHR International, said this kind of overlapping roles and a respectful, accommodating dynamic toward a founder is fairly common at companies of a certain size that are led by founders.
⠀
Doug Chia, former Johnson & Johnson corporate secretary and president of advisory firm Soundboard Governance, said that when you see Huang setting the agenda with the lead independent director, deciding what directors get and running meetings, 'it's pretty clear Jensen Huang is the chairman.'
⠀
There's no obvious No. 2 at the company.
⠀
More than 60 people report directly to Huang; he has said he runs the company with a fairly flat structure.
⠀
On NVIDIA's most recent earnings call, Huang answered analysts' questions almost entirely by himself, leaving only routine opening remarks to others, the Wall Street Journal reported.
⠀
The paper said that's normal for NVIDIA but unusual at other companies.
⠀
Huang is 63, cofounded NVIDIA in 1993 with Chris Malachowsky and Curtis Priem, and has led it ever since, making him one of the longest serving founder CEOs in Silicon Valley.
⠀
He was born in Taiwan, grew up in the U.S., and transformed NVIDIA from a gaming graphics chip maker into a leading supplier of AI processors.

▋ Trump backs Jensen Huang despite an FBI probe and mounting Congressional pressure
⠀
Trump told reporters at the White House Monday that he asked Huang earlier that day whether he knew the other person was a spy, and Huang answered 'absolutely not.'
⠀
Trump said 'I really believe him' and called him 'an amazing person' and 'a respected person.'
⠀
The FBI is investigating the matter, Trump also told reporters that day; he didn't give details.
⠀
Asked whether he had read the classified memo drafted under Secretary of State Rubio's supervision warning about Huang's relationship with Alice Huang, Trump said the memo 'didn't have much of an impact on me.'
⠀
He also said he didn't know the relevant intelligence existed when Huang traveled with him to China in May.
⠀
Asked Sunday whether Huang should remain CEO, Trump said 'I think so, of course,' and said he 'has done amazing things for our country.'
⠀
On his trip to China later this month, Trump doesn't plan to raise Huang with Xi Jinping on his own, but expects Xi will ask about him, he said.
⠀
In Congress, House Foreign Affairs Committee Chairman Brian Mast, Select Committee on China Chairman John Moolenaar, and Intelligence Committee Chairman Rick Crawford have sent a letter asking Huang for a closed joint briefing on his interactions with Alice Huang and how NVIDIA guards against foreign espionage.
⠀
A Foreign Affairs Committee press release says they asked him to brief on Nov. 18, 2026, and to accept that date by Nov. 11, or propose another meeting day.
⠀
The Verge wrote the letter was sent Nov. 4.
⠀
The press release is a request and doesn't say he has agreed to appear.
⠀
Texas Republican Senator John Cornyn wrote on X Sunday that Congress needs to investigate.
⠀
These pressures come as Huang lobbies the U.S. government and world leaders to let chips flow freely and tries to push back on concerns that doing so could endanger national security.
⠀
His role leading the world's largest chip design company has made him a global tech superstar and drawn criticism from opponents of NVIDIA's agenda inside and outside government.
⠀
NVIDIA sells hundreds of billions of dollars' worth of advanced AI processors and other hardware and provides financial support and guarantees across a wide swath of the AI industry.
⠀
Washington has restricted advanced AI chip exports to China since 2022, effectively shutting NVIDIA out of a lucrative China market, while Huang has long argued for more U.S. and China dialogue on AI development.
⠀
NVIDIA has won Trump's approval to export some older chips to China, and Trump has taken an approach friendly to the AI industry.
⠀
That policy has split the Trump administration, with officials who favor stricter export limits and more oversight frustrated by the influence of industry executives like Huang.
⠀
Seeking Alpha, citing The New York Times, reported that Huang's position is to allow exports of advanced AI chips a generation behind while keeping the newest technology in the U.S.
⠀
Whether export rules get tighter is now in Congress's hands.
⠀
CHOSUNBIZ wrote that Reuters, citing lawmakers and people involved, said this controversy makes bills tightening AI chip exports to China more likely to pass.
⠀
Three bills are being considered for the fiscal 2027 National Defense Authorization Act, but none has become law.
⠀
All three passed the House Foreign Affairs Committee earlier this year and are now candidates to be included in the NDAA in the Senate.
⠀
The AI Overwatch Act would give Congress more oversight of advanced chip exports.
⠀
The Chip Security Act would include measures like location tracking to prevent chip smuggling.
⠀
The MATCH Act would push allies to restrict exports of chipmaking equipment to China.
⠀
A joint statement from Democratic Senator Elizabeth Warren and Republican Senator Jim Banks argued that Huang's relationship with a suspected Chinese intelligence operative makes national security concerns more urgent, and called for provisions like the AI Overwatch Act to be put in the NDAA.
⠀
Democratic Representative Bill Foster also backed moving forward on X and pressed for the Chip Security Act to become law; he introduced it with Republican Representative Bill Huizenga, and it passed the Foreign Affairs Committee unanimously.
⠀
Reuters, citing a former congressional staffer who dealt directly with NVIDIA for months, said NVIDIA is seen as the main opponent of the Chip Security Act and AI Overwatch Act, CHOSUNBIZ reported.
⠀
The Information Technology Industry Council, which counts NVIDIA as a member, opposes the bills, saying they could weaken U.S. companies' competitiveness and make export controls more complicated.
⠀
The White House hasn't separately weighed in on the provisions.
⠀
CHOSUNBIZ wrote that whether they pass still depends on where the White House stands.
⠀
An NVIDIA press release on Oct. 28 said the company will hold its fiscal 2027 third quarter earnings call on Tuesday, Nov. 17, at 2 p.m.
⠀
Pacific time and 5 p.m.
⠀
Eastern time.
⠀
The quarter ended Oct. 25.
⠀
Earnings will be released around 1:20 p.m.
⠀
Pacific time.
⠀
5 p.m.
⠀
Eastern on Nov. 17 is 6 a.m.
⠀
Taiwan time on Nov. 18.

▋ Dan Ives sees Jensen Huang staying near term pending final probe results
⠀
Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesperson Guo Jiakun denied reports Monday that China planned to surveil Huang; he said the so-called Chinese spy narrative is 'completely based on unfounded speculation' and is 'slander and smearing.'
⠀
Bernstein gave NVIDIA an upbeat 'outperform' rating and a $400 price target, the Wall Street Journal reported; the paper also noted the stock closed at $186.64 on Nov. 6.
⠀
The $4.5 trillion market cap figure is from Nov. 6, before the board announced its investigation on Sunday.

Nithya Raman was elected mayor of Los Angeles and Janeese Lewis George was elected to lead Washington, D.C. in Tuesday’s elections, both mayor-elects are Democratic Socialists.

Democratic Socialists will now lead America’s two most populous cities and the nation’s capital, raising questions over the Democratic Socialist of America platform.

More than 14 million people will live under the leadership of Democratic Socialist mayors in a handful of American cities.

Upon being sworn in, Raman and Lewis George will join New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani and Seattle Mayor Katie Wilson in leading major metropolises, leading critics to be concerned about how their socialist agendas will impact the cities they lead.

A lot of eyes will likely be on LA, as the city is set to host the 2028 Summer Olympics, with thousands of people from around the world set to descend on the California city, plagued with a massive homeless problem.

President Donald Trump was asked about the latest round of socialist candidates leading the major cities in the Oval Office.

The president warned that “it’s going to be a disaster.” He added that the socialist policies “are very tough,” emphasizing, “they’re very tough on a city, a state or a country, that’s been proven over 1,000 years with different names.”

Based on the president’s comments and enthusiasm for the U.S. hosting the Summer Olympics for the first time since the 1996 Summer Olympics held in Atlanta, Ga., he could clash with Raman in the lead-up to the events.

The mayor-elect has already put herself at odds with the Los Angeles Police Department and its leadership; during Raman’s 2020 city council run, she called for the police to be defunded.

She also has a long voting history of voting to ban homeless encampments, particularly near schools, libraries and other public spaces. However, since her time on the council and her mayoral bid, she appears to have changed course on some of her controversial policies, including bans on homeless encampments and funding law enforcement.

A bit closer to home, Mayor-elect Lewis George is likely to clash with Trump if she follows through with some of her earlier statements regarding the district participating with Immigration and Customs Enforcement, youth curfews and National Guard members patrolling the district.

"Right now, using the curfew as a tool for our young people is dangerous. It is dangerous because we have federal troops who are in our city, masked ICE agents who are in our city, and these are the people enforcing this law and our young people, and these are not individuals who are trained in de-escalation, they are not accountable to D.C. residents,” the mayor-elect said during a mayoral debate.

The president has taken pride in his federal takeover of the district in August 2025, touting lower crime, the removal of homeless encampments, and the cleanup of the city. Trump’s move to deploy the National Guard was first met with anger by current D.C. Mayor Muriel Bowser, but soon softened to the idea as it appeared to help the district.

Trump has committed to keeping the National Guard deployed through the rest of his term.

While the president shared concern for his longtime home, New York City, Trump has met with Mamdani on different occasions, including inviting him to the Oval Office after his election.

“I deal with a very nice gentleman,” referring to Mamdani, “I get along with him,” the president told reporters. “We’ll see how that works out. I’d like to make sure New York does well. But it’s tough.”

While millions of Americans are governed or led by Democratic Socialists, A plurality of Americans don’t want to see their community move in the direction of the Democratic Socialist agenda, according to a recent poll from The Center Square.

Forty-four percent of American voters surveyed in The Center Square’s Voters’ Voice Poll say they would prefer to live in a city or community where Democratic Socialists have not gained influence.

Despite a plurality of Americans rejecting socialism, the cost of living appears to be the major factor behind the rise of the political ideology. New York City, Los Angeles and Washington, D.C. rank among the highest cost-of-living cities in the U.S., according to Kiplinger.

The Center Square’s Voters’ Voice Poll found 29% of Americans say the cost of living is the leading reason for the rise in popularity of some Democratic Socialist candidates in some cities and elections, followed by 15% who are frustrated with traditional Democratic politicians.

Not far behind, 13% of voters say it is because of younger Americans, and 12% say social media and online political organizing play a role in the rise of Democratic Socialists.

In an effort to combat the rise of socialism in the U.S., the White House released what it describes as the Real Cost of Socialism,” claiming the 10-year cost to American households is $355,000, while adding that the Democratic Socialist 2026 “Workers Deserve More” policies could add $49 trillion to the federal deficit over 10 years.

$NVDA $MU $SNDK $LITE HOW INVESTORS CAN SUE JENSEN HUANG, AND WHAT CAN ACTUALLY REACH HIM PERSONALLY

A full map of the legal routes, what each one can collect, and where his money is genuinely exposed. The short version: the class action can cost NVIDIA and its insurers a very large number and still leave his wallet mostly untouched. The routes that reach him personally run through Delaware and through his own board.

THE RECORD THE CASES ARE BUILT ON

• Four challenged statements, none in an SEC filing. The 10/09/25 compliance statement to the New York Times (Megaspeed "wholly owned and operated by a company based and headquartered outside China, with no China shareholders"; a site visit found "no evidence of diversion"; "a small commercial cloud"). The "field operations teams" explanation of the June 2024 Taipei bar appearance. The 10/29/26 "not unusual or unexpected" line. And Huang's own 10/30/26 remarks: dealings "normal and not unusual," and "We've studied all their deployments of our GPUs and counted every one"
• The theory is pure omission. No compliance fact in those statements is alleged to be false. They are said to be misleading because they omitted his relationship with the counterparty's executive, a woman US authorities assessed to be a Chinese intelligence asset, and the security and reputational risk that created
• The knowledge record cuts both ways. NVIDIA's general counsel Tim Teter called the Under Secretary of Commerce in late summer 2025 about the Megaspeed investigation and specifically about Singapore's detention of Alice Huang. The company, through its general counsel, knew of the investigation and the detention before the first challenged statement. Whether that knowledge reached Huang personally is a contested fact question
• For Huang: the reporting plaintiffs rely on says US officials initially did not believe he knew Alice Huang was gathering intelligence. But the falsity theory does not strictly require that. It requires the "normal dealings" statements to be misleading in light of the undisclosed relationship, and he obviously knew of his own relationship
• His trading record is much better than the headlines. A Rule 10b5-1 plan adopted 03/20/25, covering up to 6,000,000 shares. Exactly 6,000,000 shares sold for roughly $1.05B, from 06/20/25 to a final sale on 10/29/25, pre-scheduled and price-blind. Zero open-market sales in 2026. No Form 144s in 2026. His 2026 Form 4 activity is PSU vesting, tax withholding, and charitable gifts of 838,000 shares. A transfer of about 39.85 million shares to an independently managed LLC in December 2025 was a transfer, not a sale
• The tail is the problem. The plan kept selling for three weeks inside the proposed class period, and for months after his general counsel intervened with Commerce, before completing on 10/29/25. On an even-pace estimate that tail is roughly a million shares and a couple of hundred million dollars; an estimate from the plan totals, not a filed number. Note the date precisely: the final sale was a full year before the 10/29/26 intelligence-asset story. Any account tying the last sale to that story is conflating two October 29ths a year apart
• The plan's March 2025 adoption, months before the Teter call, plus a 90-day-plus cooling-off period before the first sale, gives him a strong Rule 10b5-1 affirmative defense. Attacking the tail requires pleading the plan was adopted or operated in bad faith, which the current record does not support
• His stake: 811,521,160 shares, about 3.4% of the company, held directly (about 70 million) and through trusts and LLCs. About $151B at the 11/06/26 close, about $145B at the 11/09/26 close. The 2026 proxy listed 870.6 million shares including about 58.7 million foundation shares, which are charitable assets, not his money

ROUTE 1: THE FEDERAL SECURITIES CLASS ACTION (ALREADY FILED)

• Kistenmacher v. NVIDIA, No. 5:26-cv-13448, Northern District of California, filed 11/09/26 minutes after the close. Count I: Section 10(b) and Rule 10b-5 against NVIDIA and Huang. Count II: Section 20(a) control-person liability against Huang personally
• Proposed class period 10/09/25 to 11/08/26. Corrective disclosure: the 11/08/26 board statement and the admission reporting. Loss pegged to 11/09/26: down $7.97, or 4.27%, to $178.67, roughly $190B of market value
• Anyone who bought NVIDIA securities in the class period, stock or listed options, is a presumptive class member. Retail investors do nothing now; they claim against a settlement fund later, through a claims administrator, on proof of transactions. The one live deadline belongs to institutions: under the PSLRA, the class member with the largest financial interest who moves by 01/08/27 is presumptively appointed lead plaintiff and picks lead counsel
• What plaintiffs must prove: a material omission that made affirmative statements misleading; scienter, pleaded with particularity to the Tellabs standard, an inference at least as compelling as the innocent one; reliance, presumed classwide under fraud-on-the-market (Basic), rebuttable at certification if there was no price impact (Halliburton II); and loss causation (Dura), a decline tied to revelation of the truth, not merely to bad news
• Strengths: the statements concern the very counterparty the relationship was with, which supplies the nexus courts demand before private conduct can make corporate speech misleading. Huang's own 10/30/26 statement is personally attributable and was made when the company had known of the investigation and the detention for over a year. The 11/09/26 decline came on a day the S&P 500 rose about 2%, which helps the firm-specific loss argument. The class period opens on a date when, on the Teter record, the company already knew more than it was saying
• Weaknesses: nothing challenged is alleged to be factually false, and courts are reluctant to convert a CEO's private life into securities fraud. The 10/29/26 article had already disclosed the intelligence assessment and the "close relationship," yet the complaint pleads no price reaction to it, handing defendants a truth-on-the-market and loss-causation attack: what the market learned on 11/08 was the affair confirmation and the board probe, and a drop on governance news is not automatically compensation for false statements about chip compliance. Scienter on the intelligence dimension is contested on plaintiffs' own sources. And the complaint is a first-filer product: 17 pages, no confidential witnesses, expressly on information and belief. Expect it to be replaced by a longer consolidated complaint in spring 2027
• Money mechanics: claimed damages are modeled as per-share inflation across a 13-month class period in one of the most heavily traded stocks on earth, so the plaintiffs' model will claim tens of billions. Almost no case collects claimed damages. Mega-cap cases that survive dismissal typically settle for a low single-digit percentage of the claim, which here still implies high hundreds of millions into the low billions, capped in practice by the size of NVIDIA's D&O tower, which is not public
• Timeline reality: lead plaintiff appointment runs weeks to months past the 01/08/27 deadline; the consolidated complaint lands roughly 60 days after appointment, so spring 2027; dismissal is briefed through 2027 and decided realistically in late 2027 or 2028. The PSLRA automatically stays discovery while dismissal is pending, so this case produces no depositions and no documents into the Megaspeed record until it survives. No class has been certified, and until certification nobody is represented by the filing firm unless they retain their own counsel

ROUTE 2: OPT-OUT DIRECT ACTIONS (INSTITUTIONS)

• A large holder can exclude itself from the class and sue individually on the same claims, adding state-law claims that SLUSA bars only as class claims. Opt-outs in major cases have historically recovered multiples of the class rate per dollar of loss, because a defendant pays a premium to extinguish a credible individual trial threat, and the institution controls its own timing
• The costs: the institution bears its own burden and loses class cost-sharing. The trap: under CalPERS v. ANZ Securities, a pending class action tolls the two-year limitations period but not the five-year statute of repose. On violations running from October 2025, repose is a 2030-31 problem, not a 2027 one, but it disciplines how long the opt-out option can sit unexercised
• The opt-out decision itself is made at certification or settlement notice, not now. What is decided now is lead plaintiff

ROUTE 3: DELAWARE DERIVATIVE LITIGATION (THE ROUTE THAT REACHES HIM)

• NVIDIA is a Delaware corporation. Claims that Huang and the board harmed the company belong in the Court of Chancery, brought derivatively: the shareholder sues in the company's name and any recovery is paid to NVIDIA, benefiting all holders pro rata
• Standing has a timing rule: under DGCL Section 327 the plaintiff must have owned stock when the challenged conduct occurred and must hold continuously. Anyone who bought only after the November 2026 disclosures cannot carry claims about 2025 conduct
• Step one is a Section 220 books and records demand. Investigating credible wrongdoing is the paradigmatic proper purpose and the threshold is the lowest in Delaware law, a credible basis to infer wrongdoing. A beneficial holder's demand must be under oath, with documentary evidence of ownership and a power of attorney or authorization from the record holder. A well-aimed demand seeks board and committee minutes on Megaspeed and China compliance, the materials on the Teter intervention, the committee's charter and materials, and the trading-plan adoption records
• The limits matter: production is anchored to records the board itself created or received. The crisis advisers' files and the committee's privileged investigation materials are not ordinary books and records; reaching them runs through the narrow Garner fiduciary exception under Wal-Mart v. IBEW. Courts do order emails and texts where the formal record is thin, but only after a fight
• The claims: (a) breach of fiduciary duty against Huang as officer and director, with concealment from his own board as the fact pattern Delaware treats most seriously, because it disables the corporation's own monitoring. (b) Caremark oversight claims against the board, and after the McDonald's derivative litigation, against officers within their spheres: export compliance is a mission-critical risk for this company, and the board's six-sentence November 8 statement, naming no committee members, no counsel, and no timeline, will be Exhibit A. Caremark requires bad faith and is famously the hardest claim in Delaware law, but the mission-critical framing from Marchand and the officer-duty holding from McDonald's are plaintiffs' best modern tools. (c) Brophy disgorgement: if an insider trades on material nonpublic information, the corporation recovers the profits without proving its own harm. On this record it is weak, for the plan reasons above. (d) Disgorgement of compensation for the period of disloyalty, quantified below
• The compensation scale, from the 2026 proxy: fiscal 2026 total reported compensation of $36,343,830, made up of $1,497,627 salary, $24,800,511 of PSU awards at grant-date value (he takes no RSUs or options), a $6,000,000 cash incentive, and $4,045,691 of other compensation, mostly security costs. Fiscal 2025 total: $49,866,251. The disgorgement arithmetic is $86.2M across the two most recent fiscal years and about $120M across three, of which actual cash is only about $7.5M a year
• Procedure decides control. A derivative plaintiff must demand the board sue its own CEO or plead demand futility director by director under the Zuckerberg three-part test. The November 8 committee is, on the public record, investigative; if the board hands it or a successor special litigation committee the derivative claims, it can move to dismiss under Zapata, where the court reviews independence and process and applies its own business judgment. The committee's unnamed membership is therefore not a detail; it decides who controls the claims against him
• Precedents for what this track produces: the Alphabet derivative settlement (2020), a $310M commitment plus sweeping governance reforms after the board's handling of executive misconduct; the CBS and Wynn Resorts settlements, eight-figure payments and governance changes; McDonald's, where Chancery established officer oversight duties. None of them touched a founder's core shareholding. All of them produced money to the company, structural reform, and governance pressure on the individual

ROUTE 4: CLAWBACK, ANSWERED PRECISELY

"Clawing back his shares" conflates five mechanisms. Two never trigger on these facts. One operates automatically if his service ends. One depends on what the board's investigation finds. And one, forfeiture of the founder shares themselves, does not exist in the law at all.

• Rule 10D-1 and NVIDIA's Compensation Recovery Policy: inapplicable. The policy, filed as Exhibit 97.1 and effective 10/02/23, requires recovery of erroneously awarded incentive compensation only in the event of an accounting restatement, regardless of fault. There is no restatement. Nobody alleges the financial statements are wrong; the allegations concern disclosure and conduct. The 2026 proxy describes the same restatement-only policy, maintained since 2009 and amended in 2023 for Nasdaq. The equity and cash plans reserve the board's power to write additional recoupment terms into award agreements, but that is reserved authority, not an operative misconduct clawback. Any claim that investors can claw back his pay under Dodd-Frank on these facts is wrong
• Sarbanes-Oxley Section 304: also inapplicable. It requires a restatement resulting from misconduct, and it is enforced by the SEC, not by private plaintiffs
• Forfeiture of unvested equity: applicable, automatic, and the largest sum the board controls without suing anyone. Under NVIDIA's standard award agreements, vesting ceases when continuous service ends, and units not vested on the termination date are forfeited and returned to the company at no cost. Cause is not the trigger; any end of service before a vesting date does it, resignation or removal, unless the board affirmatively deals value back in an exit negotiation. The proxy snapshot as of 01/25/26: 1,411,679 unvested RSUs and PSUs worth $264,929,798 at the price the proxy used, plus up to 465,761 unearned multi-year PSU shares payable only at stretch performance. The pool has moved since, in both directions: a 757,360-share multi-year PSU vested in full on 03/18/26, other awards kept vesting, and fiscal 2027 grants came after the snapshot. At recent prices it remains on the order of a quarter of a billion dollars. He is an at-will employee with no employment or severance agreement, so the board also owes him nothing on exit
• The Easterbrook route: the company sues, or settles on the way out. Steve Easterbrook was terminated in November 2019 characterized as without cause, which entitled him to a separation package, after disclosing one consensual relationship. McDonald's sued in Delaware Chancery in August 2020 when an investigation surfaced further relationships he had concealed, and evidence he had lied to investigators and deleted emails. In December 2021 he returned cash and equity valued at more than $105M. The theory was reliance: had the board known, he would have been fired for cause and forfeited the package. Transposed here, one difference helps NVIDIA and one helps Huang. Because he has no severance agreement, any exit value would be new consideration the board grants only in exchange for releases, cooperation, and give-backs it sets; the negotiation starts from zero. But there is as yet no public finding that he lied to the board or its investigators, which was the fact that made Easterbrook's package recoverable. A negotiated give-back priced into an exit remains the mechanism by which he personally writes the largest realistic check in this matter
• What cannot be clawed back: the 811.5 million shares. They are founder shares acquired over three decades, not incentive compensation and not proceeds of the challenged statements. No doctrine forfeits a shareholder's legitimately owned stake to other shareholders. Criminal forfeiture, the one regime that reaches personal assets, requires a conviction and property traceable to an offense, runs to the government, and no charge exists against him; the reported DOJ criminal investigation concerns the smuggling case, in which he is not, on current reporting, a target defendant. SEC enforcement, if it ever came, could seek disgorgement of ill-gotten gains, limited after Liu to net profits for victims, plus an officer-and-director bar; an SEC insider-trading theory faces the same plan wall, and an SEC disclosure theory would more likely land on the company

ROUTE 5: PROXY CLAIMS, AND THE ROUTES THAT GO NOWHERE

• Section 14(a) and Rule 14a-9: the 2026 proxy, filed in May 2026, solicited votes to re-elect directors and approve executive compensation at the June 2026 annual meeting. If by then the board or the company knew of the relationship, the investigation, or the detention, and the proxy's disclosures were materially misleading by omission, shareholders have a proxy claim. Damages are hard to quantify, so its practical use is as a derivative-side count and governance leverage. Its real value is evidentiary: it converts "the board knew by spring 2026" into a document-driven question the Section 220 process will test
• ERISA stock-drop claims by retirement plan participants follow a known template and face a demanding Supreme Court pleading standard. Expect investigation announcements; treat expected value as low
• Section 16(b) short-swing recovery: the one strict-liability disgorgement rule, no proof of actual inside information required, and it still yields nothing. His acquisitions were issuer awards exempt under Rule 16b-3, plus small ESPP purchases. There is no non-exempt purchase of any size to match against the 2025 sales
• Section 20A, the express claim for investors who traded contemporaneously with an insider trading on nonpublic information: a real route, capped at the insider's profit gained or loss avoided less any SEC disgorgement, but it inherits the insider-trading merits in full, and the plan defeats it on this record
• Securities Act Sections 11 and 12(a)(2) require a registered offering or prospectus. There was no relevant offering, so there is no strict-liability route and no underwriter to collect from. State-law fraud class claims tied to securities purchases are preempted by SLUSA. Short-side and seller theories do not fit a purchaser class

HOW COLLECTION ACTUALLY WORKS

• Class settlements are paid into a fund, overwhelmingly by the company and its D&O carriers, and distributed pro rata by a claims administrator against recognized losses from an inflation model. Three structures protect him personally: indemnification under the charter, bylaws, and his indemnification agreement, advancing his defense costs; D&O insurance, where Side C entity coverage funds the class settlement and Side A protects officers personally where indemnification is unavailable; and the conduct exclusion, which bites only after a final, non-appealable adjudication of deliberate fraud, which is precisely why these cases settle without admissions and why insurers pay
• Delaware law bars indemnification for amounts paid in settlement or judgment of derivative claims; expenses only. Amounts he is ordered to pay the company on a derivative judgment, trading profits or tainted compensation, fall on Side A insurance or on him. That technical rule is why the derivative track, which produces smaller headlines, is the one his personal counsel will take most seriously
• Defense costs are advanced and consumed from the same insurance tower, eroding the pool available for settlement over a long case. Settlement checks arrive years late, are taxable in complicated ways, and recognized-loss models systematically undercompensate hedged and options-based positions, whose legs get netted under plan-of-allocation rules that rarely mirror an options book's actual economics. Outright long holders collect best. Retail holders collect small checks per share

WHAT WOULD CHANGE THIS ANALYSIS

Six developments, in ascending order of force: (1) a confidential witness or internal document in the consolidated complaint showing the compliance statements were known to be incomplete when made. (2) Verification of the claim, reported by Bloomberg on 11/09/26 and not in the filed complaint, that NVIDIA's inventory reports omitted roughly 50,000 chips sold through hardware partners, which would give plaintiffs a conventional falsity leg against the "counted every one" assurance that does not depend on the affair. (3) Section 220 productions showing the board or Huang were told of the intelligence assessment itself, not merely the investigation, before the October 2025 statements, closing the scienter gap and reviving the trading-tail theories. (4) An adverse finding by the board's independent committee, which becomes the factual spine of every civil case and unlocks the Easterbrook route. (5) An SEC or DOJ action making factual findings, usable offensively by plaintiffs and fatal to settlement deniability. (6) An accounting restatement touching China revenue, the only event that switches on Rule 10D-1 and Section 304 and converts clawback from rhetoric into a mechanical recovery of three years of incentive pay

Absent one of those, this resolves the way these cases resolve: a large insurer-funded class settlement in 2027 or 2028, a derivative settlement heavy on governance reform, and his fate decided by the board and the government tracks rather than by any judgment.

THE PLAYBOOK

• Retail holders: keep trading records, file nothing now, submit the claim form if a settlement comes. The recovery per share will be a fraction of the $7.97 one-day decline
• Institutions: decide lead plaintiff by 01/08/27 if the losses matter; serve Section 220 demands now, while the probe record is fresh and before the committee's work hardens into privilege fights; preserve the opt-out decision for certification and settlement; and run the governance campaign, withhold votes and engagement letters, on the litigation calendar, because the board's cost-benefit on his tenure is the real decision forum
• Options holders: you are inside the class definition, but allocation will compress hedged structures. A calendar or vertical spread will not be compensated like an outright long. Model the plan of allocation before assuming the class case makes you whole. It will not

BOTTOM LINE

• His name is on the caption; his money mostly is not. The class action reaches NVIDIA's balance sheet and its insurers. It cannot claw back his shares and by itself it does not remove him
• The personal exposure is specific and finite: the disputed tail of $1.05B of plan sales, $86M to $120M of compensation for a tainted period at reported values, roughly a quarter of a billion dollars of unvested equity that vanishes if the board ends his service, and whatever give-back a negotiated exit extracts
• The real leverage investors hold is not asset seizure. It is the compounding cost, in discovery, personal defendant status, and board politics, that makes his continued tenure the expensive option

TYRANNICAL SOCIALISM COMMUNISM 

14 Million Americans Living Under Tyrannical Socialist Rule

Socialist mayors to lead LA, D.C., NYC, Seattle as Trump warns of ‘disaster’

Nov. 9, 2026 

Democratic Socialists will now lead America’s two most populous cities and the nation’s capital, raising questions over the Democratic Socialist of America platform.

More than 14 million people will live under the leadership of Democratic Socialist mayors in a handful of American cities.

Nithya Raman was elected mayor of Los Angeles and Janeese Lewis George was elected to lead Washington, D.C. in Tuesday’s elections, both mayor-elects are Democratic Socialists.

Upon being sworn in, Raman and Lewis George will join New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani and Seattle Mayor Katie Wilson in leading major metropolises, leading critics to be concerned about how their socialist agendas will impact the cities they lead.

A lot of eyes will likely be on L.A., as the city is set to host the 2028 Summer Olympics, with thousands of people from around the world set to descend on the California city, plagued with a massive homeless problem.

President Donald Trump was asked about the latest round of socialist candidates leading the major cities in the Oval Office.

The president warned that “it’s going to be a disaster.” He added that the socialist policies “are very tough,” emphasizing, “they’re very tough on a city, a state or a country, that’s been proven over 1,000 years with different names.”

Based on the president’s comments and enthusiasm for the U.S. hosting the Summer Olympics for the first time since the 1996 Summer Olympics held in Atlanta, Ga., he could clash with Raman in the lead-up to the events.

The mayor-elect has already put herself at odds with the Los Angeles Police Department and its leadership; during Raman’s 2020 city council run, she called for the police to be defunded.

She also has a long voting history of voting to ban homeless encampments, particularly near schools, libraries and other public spaces. However, since her time on the council and her mayoral bid, she appears to have changed course on some of her controversial policies, including bans on homeless encampments and funding law enforcement.

A bit closer to home, Mayor-elect Lewis George is likely to clash with Trump if she follows through with some of her earlier statements regarding the district participating with Immigration and Customs Enforcement, youth curfews and National Guard members patrolling the district.

"Right now, using the curfew as a tool for our young people is dangerous. It is dangerous because we have federal troops who are in our city, masked ICE agents who are in our city, and these are the people enforcing this law and our young people, and these are not individuals who are trained in de-escalation, they are not accountable to D.C. residents,” the mayor-elect said during a mayoral debate.

The president has taken pride in his federal takeover of the district in August 2025, touting lower crime, the removal of homeless encampments, and the cleanup of the city. Trump’s move to deploy the National Guard was first met with anger by current D.C. Mayor Muriel Bowser, but soon softened to the idea as it appeared to help the district.

Trump has committed to keeping the National Guard deployed through the rest of his term.

While the president shared concern for his longtime home, New York City, Trump has met with Mamdani on different occasions, including inviting him to the Oval Office after his election.
