$TNK Q2 2026 earnings: Teekay Tankers hits record profit, while ship prices slow renewal

Teekay Tankers, an operator of mid-sized crude oil ships, posted the highest quarterly profit in its history as Middle East conflict disrupted global shipping lanes. Revenue jumped 63% from a year ago and profit excluding one-offs rose 51% from last quarter to $194 million, pushing the debt-free company's cash pile past $1.2 billion. Chief executive Kenneth Hvid reported that third-quarter Suezmax bookings remain near record levels at $104,800 per day, though by our math unbooked Aframax days cooled to about $47,000 per day late in the second quarter.

• Revenue: $𝟑𝟕𝟗.𝟓𝐌 (+63% from a year ago)
• Profit per share, excluding one-offs: $𝟓.𝟓𝟔 (+51% from last quarter (record high))
• Cash and short-term investments: $𝟏.𝟐𝟐𝐁 (up $219M from last quarter, with zero debt)
• Q3 Suezmax spot bookings (44% fixed): $𝟏𝟎𝟒,𝟖𝟎𝟎/𝐝𝐚𝐲 (vs $109,171/day realized in Q2)

⚖️ 𝐕𝐞𝐫𝐝𝐢𝐜𝐭: 🟢 Bullish

The story got better because the collapse of the June peace agreement between the United States and Iran kept the Strait of Hormuz closed into July, extending the rate windfall into the normally quiet summer quarter. One caution: the brief two-week truce in June proved how fast spot rates drop when traffic resumes, and record prices for existing ships are preventing management from putting its cash pile to work on fast fleet renewal.

The question now is whether geopolitical chokepoints and eventual global oil restocking keep spot rates high long enough to outweigh a growing wave of new ship deliveries stretching into 2030. If conflict persists, cash builds toward $1.5 billion and forces a bigger shareholder payout; if Hormuz reopens, trapped tankers return and rates drop toward historical averages. Realized rates on the unbooked 56% of third-quarter spot days will tell.

[Model: Gemini 4 Argon. Full article with charts - link in bio]

🐂 𝐁𝐮𝐥𝐥 𝐂𝐚𝐬𝐞

🟢🟢 𝐒𝐡𝐢𝐩𝐩𝐢𝐧𝐠 𝐂𝐡𝐨𝐤𝐞𝐩𝐨𝐢𝐧𝐭𝐬 𝐃𝐫𝐨𝐯𝐞 𝐑𝐞𝐜𝐨𝐫𝐝 𝐏𝐫𝐨𝐟𝐢𝐭 𝐚𝐧𝐝 𝐂𝐚𝐬𝐡
Teekay Tankers operates mid-sized crude oil ships, mainly Suezmax and Aframax tankers, and keeps most of them on the spot market for single voyages. When conflict between the United States and Iran closed the Strait of Hormuz in late February, Asian refiners had to buy replacement oil from the Atlantic Basin. Those longer voyages tied up global shipping capacity and pushed daily hire rates to all-time highs.

• Profit excluding one-offs: $193.6 million ($5.56 per share), up 51% from last quarter and the "highest quarterly adjusted net income in the Company's history"
• Suezmax spot rate: $109,171 per day, up 76% from last quarter and more than triple a year ago
• Aframax and LR2 spot rate: $74,149 per day, up 24% from last quarter
• Third-quarter bookings so far: $104,800 per day for Suezmax and $59,900 per day for Aframax across 44% of spot days

Chief executive Kenneth Hvid noted that vessel attacks are now occurring in three vital oil regions at once: the Strait of Hormuz, the Red Sea and the Black Sea. Because Teekay refuses to sail into unsafe ports, these disruptions force ships onto longer routes and keep third-quarter bookings near record levels during what is normally the weakest season of the year.

What to watch: the final realized spot rates for the remaining 56% of third-quarter days in the November release. Holding Suezmax rates near $100,000 per day through the summer would confirm that long-haul Atlantic trade is absorbing the lost Middle East volume.

🟢 𝐅𝐢𝐱𝐞𝐝 𝐒𝐡𝐢𝐩 𝐂𝐨𝐬𝐭𝐬 𝐓𝐮𝐫𝐧𝐞𝐝 𝐑𝐚𝐭𝐞𝐬 𝐈𝐧𝐭𝐨 𝐏𝐫𝐨𝐟𝐢𝐭
Running a spot tanker fleet carries largely fixed daily crew and maintenance bills, so almost every extra dollar of daily hire rates flows straight to profit. Over the next 12 months, Teekay needs average spot rates of only about $9,700 per day to cover all operating costs and maintenance, Hvid said. With realized rates averaging over $91,000 per day in the second quarter, operating margin expanded by 34.9 percentage points from a year ago to 58.5%.

By our math, voyage expenses—fuel and port charges paid to move cargo—fell by 13.4 percentage points of revenue from a year ago to 20.4%. Vessel operating expenses, which cover crew wages, insurance and ship repairs, dropped by 8.2 percentage points of revenue to 17.7% even though total dollar spending rose slightly for Australian crew activities.

What to watch: third-quarter operating expenses and overhead, which finance chief Brody Speers expects to fall by about $3 million from the second quarter. Keeping daily ship costs flat while 260 days are lost to scheduled maintenance will test how much of the third-quarter rate windfall reaches the bottom line.

🟢 𝐂𝐚𝐬𝐡 𝐏𝐚𝐬𝐬𝐞𝐝 $𝟏.𝟐 𝐁𝐢𝐥𝐥𝐢𝐨𝐧 𝐖𝐢𝐭𝐡 𝐙𝐞𝐫𝐨 𝐃𝐞𝐛𝐭
Teekay Tankers has no bank debt, so its record operating cash flow is piling up on the balance sheet alongside cash from selling older ships. During the second quarter, the company generated $243.7 million of free cash flow by our math from the cash flow statement (or about $200 million using management's operational definition) and collected $53.5 million from selling a 2009-built Suezmax tanker.

Even after paying $1.25 per share in regular and special dividends and putting down $33.4 million on two new ships, total cash and short-term investments rose by $219.1 million during the quarter to $1.22 billion. In early July, the company closed the sale of its 2013-built VLCC (very large crude carrier) for another $84.5 million in cash.

What to watch: board decisions on excess cash ahead of the annual special dividend review next spring. Hvid called the cash pile a "high-class problem to have, but we have generated a lot of excess cash here", yet stopped short of committing to a higher regular quarterly payout.

🐻 𝐁𝐞𝐚𝐫 𝐂𝐚𝐬𝐞

🔴🔴 𝐀 𝐁𝐫𝐢𝐞𝐟 𝐏𝐞𝐚𝐜𝐞 𝐃𝐞𝐚𝐥 𝐒𝐡𝐨𝐰𝐞𝐝 𝐑𝐚𝐭𝐞 𝐅𝐫𝐚𝐠𝐢𝐥𝐢𝐭𝐲
Management emphasized that second-quarter spot rates beat the 2023 record by 50%, "primarily due to the effective closure of the Strait of Hormuz which disrupted oil and tanker markets". Yet the quarter also proved how quickly those rates drop when ships stop waiting at chokepoints or when diplomatic talks advance.

In May, Teekay had already booked 60% of its second-quarter Suezmax days at $121,800 per day and 53% of its Aframax days at $98,000 per day. Full-quarter realized rates finished lower at $109,171 and $74,149 per day. By our math, the remaining unbooked days earned about $90,200 per day for Suezmaxes and $47,300 per day for Aframaxes as trade flows adjusted and a June 17 peace framework between the U. S. and Iran briefly reopened Hormuz traffic before collapsing in early July.

What to watch: transit volumes through the Strait of Hormuz and Chinese crude imports, which hit a 10-year low in June. A lasting peace deal would release trapped and idle tankers back into the fleet and bring daily spot rates down toward historical averages.

🔴 𝐑𝐞𝐜𝐨𝐫𝐝 𝐒𝐡𝐢𝐩 𝐏𝐫𝐢𝐜𝐞𝐬 𝐒𝐥𝐨𝐰 𝐅𝐥𝐞𝐞𝐭 𝐑𝐞𝐧𝐞𝐰𝐚𝐥
Teekay is trying to replace its older tankers by selling ships built between 2007 and 2013 and buying newer vessels. Over the past 12 months, it sold nine older tankers for $369.5 million and committed $427 million to seven modern ships, including $190 million in June for two South Korean Suezmax tankers under construction for 2027 delivery ($95 million each). While bulls view this paired buying and selling as disciplined fleet renewal, buying during a rate boom locks in expensive capital.

Hvid admitted that Teekay entered 2026 expecting faster fleet renewal, but two quarters of record freight rates have pushed prices for existing ships to the "highest premiums of--for on-the-water tankers that we have seen in probably ever". That leaves $1.22 billion sitting in cash and government bills while the regular dividend stays at $0.25 per share.

What to watch: any new ship purchase prices versus the $156.6 million of remaining construction payments on the Korean Suezmaxes. Paying peak prices for secondhand ships right before the orderbook delivers would erode the cash pile's return.

🔴 𝐓𝐚𝐧𝐤𝐞𝐫 𝐎𝐫𝐝𝐞𝐫𝐛𝐨𝐨𝐤 𝐍𝐨𝐰 𝐒𝐭𝐫𝐞𝐭𝐜𝐡𝐞𝐬 𝐈𝐧𝐭𝐨 𝟐𝟎𝟑𝟎
High freight rates are encouraging rival shipowners to order new tankers while keeping their oldest ships in service instead of selling them for scrap metal. Teekay noted that a "high level of new tanker orders in 2026 has expanded the orderbook, which now stretches into 2030", while global ship scrapping remains limited.

Supply pressure showed up inside the second quarter in the mid-sized segment. Aframax spot rates fell much faster than large crude tanker rates late in the quarter due to "an influx of newbuildings and LR2s switching from clean to dirty trades"—meaning coated product tankers shifted into hauling unrefined crude oil. Management argues that the mid-sized fleet is "now the oldest in over 30 years" and that tougher sanctions scrutiny on the shadow fleet will eventually force older tankers out, but those exits are not happening while rates are near $100,000 per day.

What to watch: quarterly Aframax spot rates relative to Suezmax rates. In the third quarter to date, Aframax bookings of $59,900 per day trail Suezmax bookings of $104,800 per day by 43%, testing whether July's Atlantic rebound holds against new ship deliveries.

🔴 𝐑𝐢𝐬𝐤𝐬 𝐓𝐡𝐢𝐬 𝐐𝐮𝐚𝐫𝐭𝐞𝐫 𝐃𝐢𝐝𝐧'𝐭 𝐀𝐧𝐬𝐰𝐞𝐫
Three standing concerns around fleet scale, non-tanker profitability and capital return saw no resolution in the second-quarter materials.

• Fleet scale: following the July VLCC sale, Teekay owns 32 operating tankers plus two newbuildings and three chartered-in tankers, keeping the active fleet near management's historical minimum scale.
• Marine Services profitability: operating profit in Marine Services and Other jumped to $8.4 million, but that included a $5.6 million one-time recovery of prior-period Australian crewing costs; by our math, underlying profit was $2.8 million.
• Minority shareholder payouts: parent Teekay Corporation controls the company, and the board kept the base dividend at $0.25 per share with no share buybacks despite holding $1.22 billion in cash.

— • — • —

💲 𝐎𝐭𝐡𝐞𝐫 𝐊𝐏𝐈𝐬

𝐓𝐚𝐧𝐤𝐞𝐫𝐬 𝐬𝐞𝐠𝐦𝐞𝐧𝐭 𝐧𝐞𝐭 𝐫𝐞𝐯𝐞𝐧𝐮𝐞𝐬 (𝟐𝟔𝐐𝟐): $𝟐𝟓𝟖.𝟑 𝐦𝐢𝐥𝐥𝐢𝐨𝐧  ⇗ accelerating
Tankers net revenues—shipping revenue minus fuel and port voyage costs—climbed 31.6% from last quarter and more than doubled from $117.0 million a year ago. This non-GAAP measure tracks actual earnings across different charter types and rose for a third consecutive quarter on record spot rates.

𝐓𝐨𝐭𝐚𝐥 𝐟𝐥𝐞𝐞𝐭 𝐫𝐞𝐯𝐞𝐧𝐮𝐞 𝐝𝐚𝐲𝐬 (𝟐𝟔𝐐𝟐): 𝟑,𝟏𝟕𝟒 𝐝𝐚𝐲𝐬  ⇘ decelerating
Available earning days across the tanker fleet fell 4.5% from 3,324 days last quarter and 8.0% from 3,450 days a year ago by our math, as ten ship sales over the past year outweighed six acquisitions. Spot market days made up 77.5% of total days, down from 84.0% in the first quarter after Teekay placed more ships on fixed-rate time charters.

𝐃𝐢𝐥𝐮𝐭𝐞𝐝 𝐬𝐡𝐚𝐫𝐞 𝐜𝐨𝐮𝐧𝐭 (𝟐𝟔𝐐𝟐): 𝟑𝟒.𝟗𝟏 𝐦𝐢𝐥𝐥𝐢𝐨𝐧  ⇒ stable
Weighted-average diluted shares edged up 0.5% from 34.74 million a year ago and were virtually unchanged from 34.91 million in the first quarter. The shipping group did not repurchase any shares during the first half of 2026, issuing small amounts for employee stock options and stock-based pay.

— • — • —

🔮 𝐆𝐮𝐢𝐝𝐚𝐧𝐜𝐞

𝐐𝟑 𝐒𝐮𝐞𝐳𝐦𝐚𝐱 𝐬𝐩𝐨𝐭 𝐫𝐚𝐭𝐞 (𝟒𝟒% 𝐛𝐨𝐨𝐤𝐞𝐝): $𝟏𝟎𝟒,𝟖𝟎𝟎 𝐩𝐞𝐫 𝐝𝐚𝐲  ⇒ stable
New. Teekay has locked in 44% of its third-quarter Suezmax spot days at an average of $104,800 per day, just 4% below the second quarter's all-time high and more than triple the $33,404 per day earned in the third quarter of 2025. Across the last four quarters in our records, final realized Suezmax rates finished an average of 3.2% below the early quarter-to-date booking figure.

𝐐𝟑 𝐀𝐟𝐫𝐚𝐦𝐚𝐱 / 𝐋𝐑𝟐 𝐬𝐩𝐨𝐭 𝐫𝐚𝐭𝐞 (𝟒𝟒% 𝐛𝐨𝐨𝐤𝐞𝐝): $𝟓𝟗,𝟗𝟎𝟎 𝐩𝐞𝐫 𝐝𝐚𝐲  ⇘ decelerating
New. The mid-sized Aframax and LR2 fleet has booked 44% of its third-quarter spot days at $59,900 per day, down 19% from the second quarter's $74,149 per day after an Atlantic ship glut weighed on fixtures in June. However, chief executive Kenneth Hvid said Atlantic Aframax rates rebounded above $100,000 per day in July, which will support the remaining 56% of unbooked days.

𝐐𝟑 𝐃𝐫𝐲-𝐝𝐨𝐜𝐤 𝐨𝐟𝐟-𝐡𝐢𝐫𝐞 𝐝𝐚𝐲𝐬: 𝟐𝟔𝟎 𝐝𝐚𝐲𝐬  ⇗ accelerating
🠅 raised from 199 days
Raised. Finance chief Brody Speers projected 260 off-hire days for scheduled ship maintenance in the third quarter, up from the 199 third-quarter days outlined in the initial 2026 schedule. Management pushed dry-dockings out of the second quarter into the third quarter to keep ships trading during the spring rate spike, and Hvid said these mandatory inspections cannot be delayed further.

𝐐𝟑 𝐎𝐩𝐞𝐫𝐚𝐭𝐢𝐧𝐠 𝐚𝐧𝐝 𝐨𝐯𝐞𝐫𝐡𝐞𝐚𝐝 𝐞𝐱𝐩𝐞𝐧𝐬𝐞𝐬 (𝐎𝐩𝐄𝐱 𝐚𝐧𝐝 𝐆&𝐀): ~$𝟕𝟗.𝟔 𝐦𝐢𝐥𝐥𝐢𝐨𝐧 (-$𝟑.𝟎𝐌 𝐯𝐬 𝐐𝟐)  ⇘ decelerating
New. Speers expects combined vessel operating expenses and general and administrative overhead to decline by about $3 million in the third quarter from the second quarter's $82.6 million total, alongside slightly lower tax expense. The drop follows the second quarter's annual recognition of employee stock-based compensation in overhead and timing shifts in Australian marine maintenance.

𝐐𝟑 𝐆𝐚𝐢𝐧 𝐨𝐧 𝐕𝐋𝐂𝐂 𝐯𝐞𝐬𝐬𝐞𝐥 𝐬𝐚𝐥𝐞: $𝟐𝟐.𝟗 𝐦𝐢𝐥𝐥𝐢𝐨𝐧  ⇘ decelerating
🠅 raised from $22.5 million (originally expected in Q2)
Raised and shifted from Q2. Teekay completed the $84.5 million sale of its 2013-built VLCC in early July rather than June, moving the expected accounting gain into the third quarter and raising the estimate slightly from $22.5 million to $22.9 million.

— • — • —

❓ 𝐊𝐞𝐲 𝐐𝐮𝐞𝐬𝐭𝐢𝐨𝐧𝐬

𝐖𝐡𝐚𝐭 𝐰𝐢𝐥𝐥 𝐟𝐨𝐫𝐜𝐞 𝐚 𝐝𝐞𝐜𝐢𝐬𝐢𝐨𝐧 𝐨𝐧 𝐭𝐡𝐞 $𝟏.𝟐 𝐛𝐢𝐥𝐥𝐢𝐨𝐧 𝐜𝐚𝐬𝐡 𝐩𝐢𝐥𝐞?
Cash and short-term investments reached $1.22 billion with zero debt, and July's VLCC sale added $84.5 million. With secondhand ship prices at record highs slowing fleet purchases, investors need to know what cash threshold triggers a higher base dividend or share buybacks.

𝐖𝐢𝐥𝐥 𝐓𝐞𝐞𝐤𝐚𝐲 𝐥𝐨𝐜𝐤 𝐢𝐧 𝐦𝐨𝐫𝐞 𝐟𝐢𝐱𝐞𝐝 𝐜𝐡𝐚𝐫𝐭𝐞𝐫𝐬 𝐚𝐭 𝐜𝐮𝐫𝐫𝐞𝐧𝐭 𝐫𝐚𝐭𝐞𝐬?
Fixed-rate time-charter days rose from 289 in the first quarter to 490 in the second quarter across six tankers. With spot rates near $100,000 per day and peace talks an ongoing risk, why not lock in more multi-year charters now?

𝐖𝐡𝐚𝐭 𝐢𝐬 𝐭𝐡𝐞 𝐧𝐨𝐫𝐦𝐚𝐥 𝐩𝐫𝐨𝐟𝐢𝐭 𝐫𝐮𝐧-𝐫𝐚𝐭𝐞 𝐟𝐨𝐫 𝐀𝐮𝐬𝐭𝐫𝐚𝐥𝐢𝐚𝐧 𝐌𝐚𝐫𝐢𝐧𝐞 𝐒𝐞𝐫𝐯𝐢𝐜𝐞𝐬?
Marine Services and Other reported $8.4 million in operating profit, but $5.6 million came from recovering prior-period crewing costs. Without that one-off credit, profit was $2.8 million on $38.3 million of revenue; management has not stated the steady-state margin target.

𝐇𝐨𝐰 𝐦𝐚𝐧𝐲 𝐐𝟑 𝐝𝐚𝐲𝐬 𝐚𝐫𝐞 𝐥𝐨𝐬𝐭 𝐭𝐨 𝐞𝐦𝐩𝐭𝐲 𝐛𝐚𝐥𝐥𝐚𝐬𝐭 𝐫𝐞𝐩𝐨𝐬𝐢𝐭𝐢𝐨𝐧𝐢𝐧𝐠?
When the U. S.-Iran framework collapsed in early July, Asian refiners had to look back to the Atlantic Basin for crude. How many unpaid ballast days are built into the remaining 56% of third-quarter spot days as ships sail empty toward the Atlantic?

Alphabet’s stake in Anthropic expands

The value of Alphabet’s stake in the artificial intelligence start-up Anthropic has soared to around $US124 billion ($178 billion), making it one of the most lucrative bets in the company’s history.The Google parent disclosed in a filing on Thursday (Friday AEST) that the value of its investments in unidentified private companies totalled roughly $US124.3 billion as of June 30. Google has emerged as one of Anthropic’s biggest backers over the past several years. The technology giant first invested $US3 billion in the start-up starting in 2023. Earlier this year, it agreed to invest as much as $US40 billion more, consisting of $US10 billion upfront and a potential $US30 billion in additional funding tied to operational and financial milestones through 2030.Alphabet’s filing on Thursday showed the remaining commitment has fallen to $US20 billion as of June 30 from $US30 billion at the end of the first quarter, suggesting that Google invested another $US10 billion in the start-up last quarter. Rio Tinto dodges merger bullet

Rio Tinto has dodged two 'bullets' due to Glencore's rejection of a merger proposal: a possible BHP takeover bid and a dangerous acquisition. BHP looked closely at whether to bid for Rio Tinto if the latter announced a merger with Glencore. The two companies would make excellent merger partners; amongst others things, their staff and senior people have similar cultures, they are co-operating on future Australian iron ore projects and they are copper joint venture partners in Chile and the US. Meanwhile, there are significance cultural differences between Rio Tinto and Glencore; there is little doubt that Rio Tinto's CEO Simon Trott would have had doubts about a merger once he understood these cultural differences. (RMS)

News/Snapshot

Australian Mining

Global Commodity Rankings

Australia holds some of the world's largest reserves and is a leading producer of several key minerals.

#1 Producer: Iron Ore, Bauxite, Lithium, Rutile, and Zircon.

#1 Reserves: Iron Ore, Gold, Lead, Nickel, Rutile, Uranium, and Zinc.

#2 Producer: Gold, Alumina, and Manganese.

Key Mining Hubs & Major Projects

Western Australia: The nation's "engine room," producing 98% of Australia's iron ore and 60% of its gold. Major sites include the Pilbara (iron ore) and the Super Pit in Kalgoorlie (gold).

Queensland: A global leader in metallurgical coal (Bowen Basin) and silver/lead production (Cannington mine).

South Australia: Home to Olympic Dam, which contains the world's largest single uranium deposit and significant copper and gold reserves.

Major Players

The sector is dominated by several multinational giants and significant domestic players:

BHP: Often ranked as Australia's most valuable company; major interests in iron ore, copper, and coal.

Rio Tinto: A world leader in iron ore (Pilbara) and aluminum.

Fortescue (FMG): Primarily focused on iron ore and rapidly expanding into green energy.

Hancock Prospecting: Australia's largest private mining company, led by Gina Rinehart, the nation's wealthiest person.

South32: Spun out of BHP; manages a diversified portfolio including manganese, silver, and nickel.

2026 Trends & Developments

Critical Minerals Push: The government has introduced a $23 billion package to support domestic processing and manufacturing of critical minerals to reduce global reliance on single-country supply chains.

Uranium Rally: Prices exceeding US$100/lb have sparked renewed interest in Australian prospects like the Kalkaroo project.

M&A Activity: Major merger talks continue between giants like Rio Tinto and Glencore as they seek to consolidate copper exposure for the EV market.

Workforce Challenges: The Minerals Council of Australia is currently calling for migration reforms to address a significant "skills crunch" in the sector.

Australian Mining

Global Commodity Rankings

Australia holds some of the world's largest reserves and is a leading producer of several key minerals.

#1 Producer: Iron Ore, Bauxite, Lithium, Rutile, and Zircon.

#1 Reserves: Iron Ore, Gold, Lead, Nickel, Rutile, Uranium, and Zinc.

#2 Producer: Gold, Alumina, and Manganese.

Key Mining Hubs & Major Projects

Western Australia: The nation's "engine room," producing 98% of Australia's iron ore and 60% of its gold. Major sites include the Pilbara (iron ore) and the Super Pit in Kalgoorlie (gold).

Queensland: A global leader in metallurgical coal (Bowen Basin) and silver/lead production (Cannington mine).

South Australia: Home to Olympic Dam, which contains the world's largest single uranium deposit and significant copper and gold reserves.

Major Players

The sector is dominated by several multinational giants and significant domestic players:

BHP: Often ranked as Australia's most valuable company; major interests in iron ore, copper, and coal.

Rio Tinto: A world leader in iron ore (Pilbara) and aluminum.

Fortescue (FMG): Primarily focused on iron ore and rapidly expanding into green energy.

Hancock Prospecting: Australia's largest private mining company, led by Gina Rinehart, the nation's wealthiest person.

South32: Spun out of BHP; manages a diversified portfolio including manganese, silver, and nickel.

2026 Trends & Developments

Critical Minerals Push: The government has introduced a $23 billion package to support domestic processing and manufacturing of critical minerals to reduce global reliance on single-country supply chains.

Uranium Rally: Prices exceeding US$100/lb have sparked renewed interest in Australian prospects like the Kalkaroo project.

M&A Activity: Major merger talks continue between giants like Rio Tinto and Glencore as they seek to consolidate copper exposure for the EV market.

$NRGV Q3 2026 earnings: Energy Vault forecasts 2027 sales doubling, but equity turns negative

Energy Vault, which builds battery storage and power systems for grids and data centers, saw sales drop while customer prepayments swelled. Third-quarter revenue fell 61% to $13 million, though $246 million in customer deposits and $264 million in supplier advances show equipment is moving for a fourth-quarter delivery wave. Chief executive Robert Piconi tightened the 2026 revenue plan and set a preliminary 2027 forecast of $600 million to $700 million.

• Revenue: $𝟏𝟑.𝟏𝐌 (-61% from a year ago)
• Gross margin, excluding tariff refunds: 𝟑𝟕.𝟗% (27.0% a year ago (71.0% reported))
• Contract backlog: $𝟐.𝟑𝐁 (+15% from August; +147% from a year ago)
• 2027 preliminary revenue outlook: $𝟔𝟎𝟎–𝟕𝟎𝟎𝐌 (2026 outlook narrowed to $290–310M)

⚖️ 𝐕𝐞𝐫𝐝𝐢𝐜𝐭: ⚪ Neutral

The story is unchanged because massive order growth and upfront customer cash still collide with heavy debt and fourth-quarter delivery risk. The good news is that customers are funding the Texas AI equipment ramp upfront, and the 2027 plan points to positive cash earnings. The bad news: by our math, 83% of this year's revenue must land in the fourth quarter at a 17.6% gross margin, while total debt hit $281 million and shareholder equity turned negative.

The question now is whether the equipment surge can generate enough cash to outrun a debt-heavy balance sheet. Bulls point to the $800 million build-and-sell backlog and customer deposits covering near-term working capital; skeptics point to the negative equity, rising overhead, and unclosed SOSA project financing. Fourth-quarter deliveries and the quarterly filing's debt footnotes will settle it.

Full article with charts - link in bio

🐂 𝐁𝐮𝐥𝐥 𝐂𝐚𝐬𝐞

🟢🟢 𝐂𝐮𝐬𝐭𝐨𝐦𝐞𝐫 𝐃𝐞𝐩𝐨𝐬𝐢𝐭𝐬 𝐅𝐮𝐧𝐝 𝐭𝐡𝐞 𝐅𝐨𝐮𝐫𝐭𝐡-𝐐𝐮𝐚𝐫𝐭𝐞𝐫 𝐀𝐈 𝐑𝐚𝐦𝐩
Energy Vault builds battery storage and power systems for electric grids and artificial intelligence data centers. Total backlog — the estimated value of signed and option contracts — rose 15% from August to $2.3 billion, including $800 million from projects it builds and sells to customers.

“During the fourth quarter, we began deliveries to the recently announced 1.25GW hybrid generation and energy storage project supporting AI compute infrastructure in Texas,” chief executive Robert Piconi said. Balance sheet deposits prove that equipment is moving before fourth-quarter revenue is recorded.

• Contract liabilities (upfront cash from customers): $245.5 million, up from $29.7 million in Q2
• Advances to suppliers (current and long-term): $264.0 million, up from $6.3 million at year-end
• Preliminary 2027 outlook: $600 million to $700 million in revenue and $40 million to $50 million in adjusted EBITDA (earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortization, excluding one-offs)

This matters because customers are funding the working capital for the equipment build rather than forcing the company to use its own cash. What to watch: how much of the $245.5 million in customer deposits turns into revenue in the fourth-quarter report.

🟢 𝐏𝐢𝐩𝐞𝐥𝐢𝐧𝐞 𝐆𝐫𝐨𝐰𝐬 𝐖𝐢𝐭𝐡 𝐑𝐞𝐚𝐝𝐲-𝐭𝐨-𝐁𝐮𝐢𝐥𝐝 𝐏𝐫𝐨𝐣𝐞𝐜𝐭𝐬 𝐚𝐧𝐝 𝐓𝐚𝐱 𝐂𝐫𝐞𝐝𝐢𝐭𝐬
Through its Asset Vault subsidiary, the power infrastructure group builds and operates its own battery and generation sites to earn recurring revenue. In the third quarter, it bought 2.3 gigawatts of US battery projects from Goshe Energy Storage, including 350 megawatts ready to build, and paid the entire cash price.

The company also received grid connection approval for its 125-megawatt Stoney Creek battery project in Australia and started building its Snyder modular data center in Texas. Alongside project financing for 275 megawatts of Rolls-Royce gas engines and a $40 million credit commitment from S2G Investments, the company collected $39.7 million from selling investment tax credits over the first nine months, meeting its ~$40 million full-year target.

What to watch: total megawatts under operation, construction, and ready-to-build in the quarterly filing. A jump above 1.1 gigawatts will show how much of the Goshe portfolio enters the active build schedule.

🐻 𝐁𝐞𝐚𝐫 𝐂𝐚𝐬𝐞

🔴🔴 𝐎𝐧𝐞 𝐐𝐮𝐚𝐫𝐭𝐞𝐫 𝐌𝐮𝐬𝐭 𝐂𝐚𝐫𝐫𝐲 𝐅𝐢𝐯𝐞-𝐒𝐢𝐱𝐭𝐡𝐬 𝐨𝐟 𝐭𝐡𝐞 𝐘𝐞𝐚𝐫
Energy Vault recognizes most of its equipment revenue when batteries and generators arrive at customer sites. Third-quarter sales dropped 61% from a year ago to $13.1 million, leaving nine-month revenue at just $52.3 million.

Because management tightened its full-year revenue forecast to $290 million to $310 million, the fourth quarter must deliver $247.7 million at the middle of the range by our math. That single period represents 83% of the entire year's sales, up from 75% in the fourth quarter of 2025.

Furthermore, the company lowered the top end of its full-year gross margin plan from 25% to 22%. By our math, that leaves a 17.6% gross margin for the fourth quarter, down from 37.9% excluding tariff refunds in the third quarter, because early hardware deliveries carry much lower margins.

What to watch: fourth-quarter revenue and gross margin in the full-year report. Any customs delay on imported batteries would push sales into 2027 and cause a miss against the annual plan.

🔴🔴 𝐃𝐞𝐛𝐭 𝐂𝐥𝐢𝐦𝐛𝐬 𝐚𝐧𝐝 𝐒𝐡𝐚𝐫𝐞𝐡𝐨𝐥𝐝𝐞𝐫 𝐄𝐪𝐮𝐢𝐭𝐲 𝐓𝐮𝐫𝐧𝐬 𝐍𝐞𝐠𝐚𝐭𝐢𝐯𝐞
“Our third quarter financial performance reflects our previously discussed timing of deliveries and continued strengthening of our balance sheet and liquidity,” Piconi said. While cash grew and corporate recourse debt fell by $12 million from last quarter, total balance sheet leverage moved the other way.

• Total debt (short-term and long-term): $280.5 million, up from $243.0 million in Q2 and $94.6 million at year-end
• Stockholders' equity: a deficit of -$12.4 million, down from positive $6.9 million in Q2 and $67.5 million at year-end
• Nine-month interest expense: $12.7 million, more than double the $5.4 million a year ago

Meanwhile, project financing for the SOSA battery site in Texas — originally expected in the second quarter — has still not closed, with the footnote calling it “inclusive of SOSA, which is expected to reach financial close imminently”. What to watch: the debt footnote in the quarterly filing to see if convertible bond repayments are diluting shareholders while the parent company sits in an equity deficit.

🔴 𝐎𝐯𝐞𝐫𝐡𝐞𝐚𝐝 𝐆𝐫𝐨𝐰𝐬 𝐖𝐡𝐢𝐥𝐞 𝐁𝐚𝐜𝐤𝐥𝐨𝐠 𝐌𝐢𝐱𝐞𝐬 𝐈𝐧 𝐔𝐧𝐜𝐨𝐧𝐭𝐫𝐚𝐜𝐭𝐞𝐝 𝐏𝐨𝐰𝐞𝐫
Building an owned-asset business requires hiring and project development before the power plants generate cash. Operating expenses excluding one-offs rose 56% from a year ago to $25.2 million, driven by general and administrative costs (corporate overhead and legal fees) rising from $19.8 million to $25.5 million. As a result, the adjusted EBITDA loss widened to $14.7 million from $6.0 million a year ago.

At the same time, $1.5 billion of the $2.3 billion backlog sits in owned projects that pay out over many years. The company's backlog definition includes unexercised purchase options and variable power sales where management uses third-party computer models and counts “low-end simulation results to be probable”. What to watch: binding remaining performance obligations in the quarterly filing, which stood at $362 million last quarter.

🔴 𝐑𝐢𝐬𝐤𝐬 𝐭𝐡𝐢𝐬 𝐪𝐮𝐚𝐫𝐭𝐞𝐫 𝐝𝐢𝐝𝐧'𝐭 𝐚𝐧𝐬𝐰𝐞𝐫
The earnings release did not include the footnote tables needed to check five standing risks from prior quarters.

• Owned-asset debt covenants: whether the Cross Trails battery site in Texas passed its third-quarter debt-service coverage test after two waivers.
• Recurring power revenue: quarterly tolling and power-purchase revenue from the two operating battery sites, which requires the revenue breakdown note.
• New Mexico data center land: how the company will pay the $57.4 million land closing due in December 2026.
• Customer concentration: what share of revenue and receivables came from the top three customers.
• Foreign supply rules: whether Chinese-sourced battery cells qualify for tax credits under new federal foreign-entity rules.

👓 𝐎𝐭𝐡𝐞𝐫 𝐓𝐡𝐞𝐦𝐞𝐬

𝐓𝐚𝐫𝐢𝐟𝐟 𝐑𝐞𝐟𝐮𝐧𝐝𝐬 𝐋𝐢𝐟𝐭𝐞𝐝 𝐓𝐡𝐢𝐫𝐝-𝐐𝐮𝐚𝐫𝐭𝐞𝐫 𝐆𝐫𝐨𝐬𝐬 𝐌𝐚𝐫𝐠𝐢𝐧
US customs refunded $4.3 million of previously paid import tariffs during the third quarter after earlier emergency tariff rules were struck down. Because quarterly revenue was only $13.1 million, that one-time refund pushed reported gross margin to 71.0%, compared with 37.9% without the refund, and lifted gross margin excluding depreciation to 81.1% versus 48.0% on an underlying basis.

— • — • —

💲 𝐎𝐭𝐡𝐞𝐫 𝐊𝐏𝐈𝐬

𝐓𝐨𝐭𝐚𝐥 𝐜𝐚𝐬𝐡 𝐚𝐧𝐝 𝐫𝐞𝐬𝐭𝐫𝐢𝐜𝐭𝐞𝐝 𝐜𝐚𝐬𝐡 (𝟐𝟔𝐐𝟑): $𝟐𝟑𝟔.𝟐 𝐦𝐢𝐥𝐥𝐢𝐨𝐧  ⇗ accelerating
Total cash rose 59% from last quarter and nearly quadrupled from $61.9 million a year ago. The increase came from customer equipment prepayments, $262.4 million in nine-month debt proceeds, and $39.7 million in tax credit sales, leaving $180.5 million in unrestricted cash and $55.7 million in restricted project accounts.

18 ASOG, 818 OSS, 14 ASOS, 15 ASOS, 19 ASOS, 20 ASOS
Pope Field, NC --  
POPE ARMY AIRFIELD, NC – Twenty-four Airmen completed the 2019 Dragon Challenge at Pope Army Airfield Nov. 5-7. The annual THREE day competition is designed to prepare Airmen for the stress of combat includes a battlefield fitness test, shooting, casualty care, land navigation, obstacle course, knowledge test and combatives.

“This DRAGON CHALLENGE marks our third annual 18 ASOG combat field skills competition since we resurrected the event in 2017,” Col. Dane Crawford, commander of the 18th Air Support Operations Group, said. “We compete across our Group to hone our field craft, determine top individual and team performers, but most importantly to simulate the rigor of combat. Pitting our Airmen in competition from each of our squadrons adds a psychological dimension to the already physically and technically demanding challenge. The psychological factor is what best simulates combat stress and why competition is so important. Keys to success for our competitors are maximum individual effort, team work, and a positive attitude.”

Airmen from the 14th Air Support Operations Squadron (Pope AAF), 15th Air Support Operations Squadron (Fort Stewart, GA), 19th Air Support Operations Squadron (Fort Campbell, KY) and 20th Air Support Operations Squadron (Fort Drum, NY) competed individually and as a team. The Dragon Challenge was hosted by the 18th Air Support Operations Group with the support of the 818th Operations Support Squadron at Pope. The competition began in 1999 as a means to push the best Airmen from each squadron to compete, improve and bring new skills back to their units.

$PSKY Q3 2026 earnings: Skydance streaming sales grow fast, but Warner films hurt profit

Skydance, the film, television and streaming giant formed by merging Paramount and Warner Bros. Discovery, posted solid standalone growth before taking on a massive debt load and an immediate box office warning. Standalone third-quarter revenue rose 5% to $7.0 billion as Paramount+ streaming sales jumped 21% on higher prices. Chief executive David Ellison and co-chief executive Ynon Kreiz closed the Warner Bros. buyout in October — lifting gross debt to $87 billion — and warned that weak Warner Bros. movie results will cut fourth-quarter profit by up to $200 million against prior plans.

• Standalone Q3 revenue: $𝟕.𝟎𝟑𝐁 (+5% from a year ago)
• Paramount+ streaming revenue: $𝟐.𝟏𝟑𝐁 (+21% from a year ago)
• Gross debt after Warner Bros. close: $𝟖𝟕𝐁 (up from $15B at Q3 end)
• Standalone 2026 EBITDA outlook: 𝐑𝐚𝐢𝐬𝐞𝐝 𝐭𝐨 𝐡𝐢𝐠𝐡 𝐞𝐧𝐝 ($3.9B target; up to $200M Q4 hit at Warner film unit)

⚖️ 𝐕𝐞𝐫𝐝𝐢𝐜𝐭: ⚪ Neutral

The story is unchanged because closing the Warner Bros. deal eight months early removes the lawsuit risk and creates a 203-million-subscriber streaming giant, but replaces it with $72 billion of additional debt and immediate studio trouble. On the positive side, standalone Paramount beat its flat subscriber plan and raised its own cost-saving target above $3 billion. The bad news: streaming profit margins fell 11 percentage points on higher sports costs, and management will stop reporting quarterly subscriber numbers and quarterly financial plans starting next quarter.

The question now is whether combining Paramount+ and HBO Max can generate enough cash to pay down $87 billion of debt while cable television shrinks. Either the $6 billion cost-cutting plan and early-2027 streaming bundle lift cash flow toward the $10 billion 2030 goal, or Upfront restructuring bills of $4 billion and cord-cutting eat up the savings. The full-year 2027 financial outlook arriving with fourth-quarter results will give the first combined test.

Full article with charts - link in bio

🐂 𝐁𝐮𝐥𝐥 𝐂𝐚𝐬𝐞

🟢🟢 𝐏𝐚𝐫𝐚𝐦𝐨𝐮𝐧𝐭+ 𝐆𝐫𝐨𝐰𝐭𝐡 𝐀𝐜𝐜𝐞𝐥𝐞𝐫𝐚𝐭𝐞𝐬 𝐨𝐧 𝐇𝐢𝐠𝐡𝐞𝐫 𝐏𝐫𝐢𝐜𝐞𝐬 𝐚𝐧𝐝 𝐀𝐝𝐬
Direct-to-Consumer (DTC), the streaming division housing Paramount+ and free ad-supported service Pluto TV, is the company's main growth engine. Chief executive David Ellison and co-chief executive Ynon Kreiz plan to launch a single bundle combining Paramount+ and HBO Max in early 2027, and they aim to unite the backend technology of both services within a year.

Paramount+ revenue rose 21% from a year ago to $2.13 billion, its fastest growth this year. The service added 600,000 subscribers in the quarter to reach 82.2 million, beating management's forecast for flat numbers. Average revenue per user grew about 14% on earlier price increases and rising ad sales. Engineers also "largely completed phase one of the tech convergence, moving Pluto TV onto the unified Paramount+ platform across all major devices".

Total DTC revenue grew 11% to $2.51 billion, or 17% by our math when excluding a 6-point drag from folding BET+ into Paramount+ and cable declines at Showtime. Because the Paramount+ result beat what the flat subscriber forecast pointed to, the standalone streaming business enters the Warner Bros. merger with strong pricing power.

What to watch: pro forma combined DTC revenue growth in the fourth quarter, after it grew 15% in the third quarter. Acceleration above 15% will show that HBO Max is adding momentum ahead of the early-2027 bundle launch.

🟢 𝐂𝐨𝐬𝐭 𝐂𝐮𝐭𝐬 𝐚𝐧𝐝 𝐋𝐢𝐯𝐞 𝐒𝐩𝐨𝐫𝐭𝐬 𝐋𝐢𝐟𝐭 𝐓𝐫𝐚𝐝𝐢𝐭𝐢𝐨𝐧𝐚𝐥 𝐓𝐕 𝐌𝐚𝐫𝐠𝐢𝐧𝐬
Skydance TV runs the CBS broadcast network and cable channels such as MTV, Nickelodeon, CNN and TNT. Management relies on this division to generate the cash flow needed to fund streaming and pay down debt. To protect profits as audiences move online, Ellison and Kreiz placed the TV and streaming groups under one commercial leadership team to sell ads and distribution together.

While standalone TV Media revenue fell 7% from a year ago to $3.02 billion, its Adjusted EBITDA (earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, amortization and one-offs) rose to $1.03 billion. That lifted the division's profit margin by 7.9 percentage points to 34.0% by our math, because content costs dropped by 6.6 percentage points of revenue. CBS led fall broadcast ratings, NFL viewership on CBS rose 5% to a record 19.6 million average viewers, and sports advertising commitments for upcoming seasons rose over 20%. Management also raised its standalone Paramount cost-saving target from $2.7 billion to over $3 billion.

What to watch: combined Skydance TV Adjusted EBITDA margin in the fourth quarter. Holding margins above 30% after adding Warner Bros. cable networks like TNT and CNN will prove that cost cuts and live sports can offset shrinking cable subscriptions.

🟢 𝐒𝐭𝐮𝐝𝐢𝐨𝐬 𝐑𝐞𝐯𝐞𝐧𝐮𝐞 𝐑𝐢𝐬𝐞𝐬 𝟐𝟑% 𝐁𝐞𝐟𝐨𝐫𝐞 𝐖𝐚𝐫𝐧𝐞𝐫 𝐒𝐥𝐚𝐭𝐞 𝐒𝐭𝐮𝐦𝐛𝐥𝐞𝐬
The Studios division produces movies and television shows for the company's own platforms and outside buyers. Under Ellison, Paramount Pictures aimed to double its theatrical output to 15 films in 2026 and improve returns by testing movies earlier and matching marketing budgets to real-time audience data.

Standalone Studios revenue rose 23% from a year ago to $1.50 billion in the third quarter, driven by TV licensing and third-party production, while theatrical revenue stayed even at $112 million. Segment Adjusted EBITDA reached $129 million, or 8.6% of sales, up from $19 million a year ago by our math as content costs fell by 2.2 percentage points of revenue. Ellison and Kreiz said Paramount's 2026 film slate will generate over $500 million more in lifetime profit than last year's lineup.

What to watch: box office and licensing revenue from the six fourth-quarter theatrical releases, including Dune: Part Three on December 18. Strong ticket sales will show whether Paramount's marketing playbook can quickly fix the newly acquired Warner Bros. film unit.

🐻 𝐁𝐞𝐚𝐫 𝐂𝐚𝐬𝐞

🔴🔴 𝐖𝐚𝐫𝐧𝐞𝐫 𝐁𝐫𝐨𝐬. 𝐃𝐞𝐚𝐥 𝐂𝐥𝐨𝐬𝐞𝐬 𝐄𝐚𝐫𝐥𝐲, 𝐀𝐝𝐝𝐢𝐧𝐠 $𝟕𝟐 𝐁𝐢𝐥𝐥𝐢𝐨𝐧 𝐢𝐧 𝐃𝐞𝐛𝐭
Skydance "completed the acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery on October 6, 2026", resolving the regulatory lawsuit that had threatened to delay the deal until mid-2027. While bulls view the merger as the only way to reach global streaming scale — lifting combined subscribers to 203 million across Paramount+ and HBO Max — the transaction transforms the balance sheet and multiplies financial risk.

• Gross debt after closing: $87 billion, up $72 billion from $15.0 billion at the end of September
• Deal funding: $57 billion in new secured debt and $47 billion in new equity
• Cash after closing: about $10 billion, partly already committed to employee equity payouts and debt securitization paydowns
• Investment-grade credit target: pushed back to the end of 2029 (3.0x net debt to EBITDA), compared with standalone Paramount's earlier 2027 goal

The early close removes the risk of a $7 billion breakup fee, so management can start cutting duplicate costs immediately. However, carrying $87 billion of debt while traditional television shrinks leaves little room for integration delays or box office misses.

What to watch: year-end net debt and cash balance in the fourth-quarter report, after the company pays off Warner Bros. Discovery's securitization program and employee equity awards. A slower debt paydown than planned would keep interest costs high and pressure credit ratings.

🔴🔴 𝐖𝐚𝐫𝐧𝐞𝐫 𝐁𝐫𝐨𝐬. 𝐅𝐢𝐥𝐦 𝐅𝐥𝐨𝐩𝐬 𝐚𝐧𝐝 𝐒𝐭𝐫𝐞𝐚𝐦𝐢𝐧𝐠 𝐂𝐨𝐬𝐭𝐬 𝐇𝐢𝐭 𝐏𝐫𝐨𝐟𝐢𝐭
Ellison and Kreiz say they are building the premier global content engine and expanding streaming profit margins. Yet the first quarter as a combined company begins with an immediate earnings warning from the studio lot and a sharp drop in standalone streaming margins.

In the fourth quarter, management expects "improved Paramount film slate results to be more than offset by underperformance of the Warner Bros. film slate". That weak box office run will slow studio revenue growth and cause "a profit impact of up to $200 million vs. prior expectations for Q4". Meanwhile, in the third quarter, standalone DTC Adjusted EBITDA fell from $446 million a year ago to $225 million by our math. The streaming profit margin dropped 10.7 percentage points to 9.0% because content costs for UFC fights and original series jumped 9.6 percentage points of revenue.

This cuts against the narrative of smooth profit expansion, because higher sports and original programming bills are squeezing streaming margins just as inherited Warner Bros. movies miss targets.

What to watch: fourth-quarter combined Studios Adjusted EBITDA. A studio loss alongside the $200 million Warner Bros. film hit would show that fixing the combined theatrical pipeline will drag on 2027 profits.

🔴 𝐓𝐫𝐚𝐝𝐢𝐭𝐢𝐨𝐧𝐚𝐥 𝐓𝐕 𝐑𝐞𝐯𝐞𝐧𝐮𝐞 𝐊𝐞𝐞𝐩𝐬 𝐒𝐡𝐫𝐢𝐧𝐤𝐢𝐧𝐠 𝐃𝐞𝐬𝐩𝐢𝐭𝐞 𝐒𝐥𝐨𝐰𝐞𝐫 𝐂𝐨𝐫𝐝-𝐂𝐮𝐭𝐭𝐢𝐧𝐠
Traditional broadcast and cable networks still provide most of the company's segment profit, making the pace of cord-cutting a central risk. Ellison and Kreiz noted that US pay-TV subscriber losses slowed from the second quarter as "genre-based packages gained traction with the start of the NFL season".

Even with that moderation, standalone TV Media revenue fell 7% from a year ago to $3.02 billion. Subscription and affiliate fees from cable providers dropped 5% to $1.55 billion on subscriber losses. Advertising revenue fell 8% to $1.34 billion; excluding the sales of Latin American broadcasters Telefe and Chilevisión, underlying TV ad sales still fell 5% by our math despite a boost from US midterm political ads.

Adding Warner Bros. cable channels such as CNN, TNT, TBS and Discovery greatly enlarges Skydance's exposure to shrinking cable bundles just as major distributor contracts come up for renewal.

What to watch: fourth-quarter combined Skydance TV affiliate revenue trends. If affiliate revenue declines worsen past 5% once the Warner Bros. cable channels are included, cost cuts alone will struggle to keep TV cash flow steady.

🔴 𝐒𝐤𝐲𝐝𝐚𝐧𝐜𝐞 𝐃𝐫𝐨𝐩𝐬 𝐒𝐮𝐛𝐬𝐜𝐫𝐢𝐛𝐞𝐫 𝐑𝐞𝐩𝐨𝐫𝐭𝐢𝐧𝐠 𝐚𝐧𝐝 𝐐𝐮𝐚𝐫𝐭𝐞𝐫𝐥𝐲 𝐎𝐮𝐭𝐥𝐨𝐨𝐤𝐬
Just as investors take on an $87 billion debt load and a massive streaming integration, management is pulling back on transparency, while several standing accounting and governance questions got no new numbers in the release.

• Streaming subscriber counts: Ellison and Kreiz said that "beginning with Q4’26 results and in line with other leading DTC players in the industry, we will no longer provide quarterly subscriber disclosures".
• Quarterly financial plans: stopped; management will only issue annual outlooks starting with 2027 targets next quarter.
• Accounting boost to profit: the release did not quantify how much merger pushdown write-downs lowered content costs in the third quarter, ahead of next year's scheduled step-down.
• Related-party deals and cable renewals: no update in the release on controlling-stockholder contracts or the 18-month cable distributor renewal schedule; the quarterly 10-Q filing will carry any legal and related-party updates.

What to watch: the 2027 annual outlook format in the fourth-quarter release. Without quarterly subscriber counts or quarterly profit ranges, investors will rely on segment free cash flow and revenue disclosures to track whether the HBO Max bundle is losing overlapping customers.

👓 𝐎𝐭𝐡𝐞𝐫 𝐓𝐡𝐞𝐦𝐞𝐬

𝐒𝐢𝐱-𝐁𝐢𝐥𝐥𝐢𝐨𝐧-𝐃𝐨𝐥𝐥𝐚𝐫 𝐂𝐨𝐬𝐭-𝐒𝐚𝐯𝐢𝐧𝐠 𝐏𝐥𝐚𝐧 𝐂𝐚𝐫𝐫𝐢𝐞𝐬 𝐚 𝐅𝐨𝐮𝐫-𝐁𝐢𝐥𝐥𝐢𝐨𝐧-𝐃𝐨𝐥𝐥𝐚𝐫 𝐂𝐚𝐬𝐡 𝐁𝐢𝐥𝐥
Following the Warner Bros. close, Ellison and Kreiz launched a transformation program "targeting at least $6 billion of annualized run-rate synergies within three years" across a combined expense base of over $50 billion. They plan to cut $2.2 billion from corporate overhead and real estate, $1.4 billion from technology, $1.4 billion from vendor purchasing, and $1.0 billion from marketing, realizing 30% in year one. Achieving those savings will cost roughly $4 billion in one-time cash charges, including $1.5 billion to $2.0 billion in 2027.

— • — • —

💲 𝐎𝐭𝐡𝐞𝐫 𝐊𝐏𝐈𝐬

𝐅𝐫𝐞𝐞 𝐜𝐚𝐬𝐡 𝐟𝐥𝐨𝐰 (𝟐𝟔𝐐𝟑): $𝟑𝟏 𝐦𝐢𝐥𝐥𝐢𝐨𝐧  ⇘ decelerating
Free cash flow — operating cash flow minus capital spending — dropped from $258 million last quarter to $31 million, or 0.4% of sales. That figure includes $174 million of cash spent on severances, merger fees and system upgrades, which came in below the $200 million forecast. Before those one-off cash costs, free cash flow was $205 million by our math.

𝐏𝐫𝐨𝐠𝐫𝐚𝐦𝐦𝐢𝐧𝐠 𝐚𝐧𝐝 𝐨𝐭𝐡𝐞𝐫 𝐢𝐧𝐯𝐞𝐧𝐭𝐨𝐫𝐲 (𝟐𝟔𝐐𝟑): $𝟏𝟕.𝟗𝟏 𝐛𝐢𝐥𝐥𝐢𝐨𝐧  ⇗ accelerating
Total programming inventory — the capitalized cost of films, series and sports rights on the balance sheet — rose 8.6% from the end of 2025 ($16.49 billion) by our math, outpacing 5% revenue growth. The buildup reflects standalone Paramount doubling its annual theatrical slate to 15 films and investing in UFC and original streaming shows.

𝐍𝐞𝐭 𝐫𝐞𝐜𝐞𝐢𝐯𝐚𝐛𝐥𝐞𝐬 (𝟐𝟔𝐐𝟑): $𝟔.𝟏𝟎 𝐛𝐢𝐥𝐥𝐢𝐨𝐧  ⇘ decelerating
Money owed by customers and distributors fell 7.8% from $6.62 billion at the end of 2025, moving down while third-quarter revenue grew 5%. Even with lower receivables, working capital outflows pulled nine-month operating cash flow down to $627 million as the studio funded new film and television production.

— • — • —

🔮 𝐆𝐮𝐢𝐝𝐚𝐧𝐜𝐞

𝐒𝐭𝐚𝐧𝐝𝐚𝐥𝐨𝐧𝐞 𝐅𝐘𝟐𝟔 𝐀𝐝𝐣𝐮𝐬𝐭𝐞𝐝 𝐄𝐁𝐈𝐓𝐃𝐀: $𝟑.𝟗 𝐛𝐢𝐥𝐥𝐢𝐨𝐧  ⇘ decelerating
🠅 raised from $3.8–3.9 billion
Raised to the top of the prior range. Standalone Paramount Skydance remains on track for $3.9 billion, though fourth-quarter reports will now combine Warner Bros. Discovery. By our math, $3.9 billion leaves $640 million for standalone Q4, down 5% from $674 million a year ago. It is the third raise since late 2025: +$300M (on a basis change), +$50M, and +$50M to the high end.

𝐐𝟒 𝐂𝐨𝐦𝐛𝐢𝐧𝐞𝐝 𝐒𝐭𝐮𝐝𝐢𝐨𝐬 𝐏𝐫𝐨𝐟𝐢𝐭 𝐈𝐦𝐩𝐚𝐜𝐭: 𝐔𝐩 𝐭𝐨 -$𝟐𝟎𝟎 𝐦𝐢𝐥𝐥𝐢𝐨𝐧 𝐯𝐬 𝐩𝐫𝐢𝐨𝐫 𝐩𝐥𝐚𝐧  ⇘ decelerating
New. Management warned that weak box office results from the inherited Warner Bros. fourth-quarter film slate will more than offset gains at Paramount Pictures. That shortfall will slow studio revenue growth and reduce fourth-quarter profit by up to $200 million compared with earlier internal forecasts.

𝟐𝟎𝟑𝟎 𝐌𝐞𝐝𝐢𝐮𝐦-𝐓𝐞𝐫𝐦 𝐅𝐢𝐧𝐚𝐧𝐜𝐢𝐚𝐥 𝐎𝐮𝐭𝐥𝐨𝐨𝐤: 𝐌𝐢𝐝-𝐬𝐢𝐧𝐠𝐥𝐞-𝐝𝐢𝐠𝐢𝐭 𝐫𝐞𝐯𝐞𝐧𝐮𝐞 𝐠𝐫𝐨𝐰𝐭𝐡, 𝐦𝐢𝐝-𝟐𝟎% 𝐀𝐝𝐣𝐮𝐬𝐭𝐞𝐝 𝐄𝐁𝐈𝐓𝐃𝐀 𝐦𝐚𝐫𝐠𝐢𝐧, >$𝟏𝟎𝐁 𝐅𝐂𝐅  ⇗ accelerating
New. For the combined company, Ellison and Kreiz target about 5% annual revenue growth, Adjusted EBITDA margins around 25% (up from standalone Paramount's 14.2% in Q3), and over $10 billion in annual free cash flow by 2030. That cash ramp is required to bring net debt down to 3.0 times EBITDA by the end of 2029.

— • — • —

❓ 𝐊𝐞𝐲 𝐐𝐮𝐞𝐬𝐭𝐢𝐨𝐧𝐬

𝐇𝐨𝐰 𝐰𝐢𝐥𝐥 𝐢𝐧𝐯𝐞𝐬𝐭𝐨𝐫𝐬 𝐭𝐫𝐚𝐜𝐤 𝐛𝐮𝐧𝐝𝐥𝐞 𝐜𝐡𝐮𝐫𝐧 𝐰𝐢𝐭𝐡𝐨𝐮𝐭 𝐬𝐮𝐛𝐬𝐜𝐫𝐢𝐛𝐞𝐫 𝐜𝐨𝐮𝐧𝐭𝐬?
Management is ending quarterly subscriber disclosures in Q4 right before launching the Paramount+ and HBO Max bundle in early 2027. Without subscriber numbers or overlap figures for the 203 million combined accounts, how can outsiders verify whether the bundle is keeping customers?

𝐃𝐢𝐝 𝐏𝐥𝐮𝐭𝐨 𝐓𝐕 𝐚𝐧𝐝 𝐨𝐯𝐞𝐫𝐚𝐥𝐥 𝐚𝐝 𝐫𝐞𝐯𝐞𝐧𝐮𝐞 𝐫𝐞𝐭𝐮𝐫𝐧 𝐭𝐨 𝐠𝐫𝐨𝐰𝐭𝐡?
Last quarter, management said Pluto TV and company-wide advertising revenue would return to growth in the second half of 2026. Total standalone ad revenue fell 3% in Q3 and Pluto revenue was not disclosed; what are the fourth-quarter growth rates for both?

𝐇𝐨𝐰 𝐥𝐚𝐫𝐠𝐞 𝐢𝐬 𝐧𝐞𝐱𝐭 𝐲𝐞𝐚𝐫'𝐬 𝐚𝐜𝐜𝐨𝐮𝐧𝐭𝐢𝐧𝐠 𝐬𝐭𝐞𝐩-𝐝𝐨𝐰𝐧 𝐢𝐧 𝐜𝐨𝐧𝐭𝐞𝐧𝐭 𝐜𝐨𝐬𝐭𝐬?
Merger accounting write-downs lowered programming amortization in 2026, boosting Adjusted EBITDA, and management previously said this benefit steps down in 2027. How many millions of dollars of accounting relief will roll off next year, and will Warner Bros. assets receive similar write-downs?

𝐖𝐡𝐲 𝐝𝐢𝐝 𝐬𝐭𝐚𝐧𝐝𝐚𝐥𝐨𝐧𝐞 𝐐𝟒 𝐢𝐦𝐩𝐥𝐢𝐞𝐝 𝐫𝐞𝐯𝐞𝐧𝐮𝐞 𝐚𝐧𝐝 𝐩𝐫𝐨𝐟𝐢𝐭 𝐝𝐢𝐯𝐞𝐫𝐠𝐞?
By our math, standalone Paramount's prior $30 billion revenue target and $3.9 billion profit target imply Q4 revenue rising 7% while Adjusted EBITDA falls 5%. How much of that Q4 margin squeeze comes from UFC and original content amortization versus film marketing?

🏈 MNF Small Game Parlay 🏈

Since there is no soccer today, here is a SGP for tonight’s game between the Buffalo Bills and Minnesota Vikings

5 legs for +295 odds

1️⃣ BILLS +7.5 1st HALF: Buffalo has covered this halftime cushion in 7/7 games, leading at halftime five times and being tied twice. Minnesota’s opponents have covered +7.5 in the first half in 6/7 games. The only miss was Miami trailing Minnesota 9-0.

Football wise, Minnesota’s struggles on early downs make it difficult to consistently build a large lead. Buffalo’s established rushing attack and use of multiple tight ends give Allen options against Minnesota’s pressure. The +7.5 cushion allows Buffalo time to adjust while still protecting against a seven point halftime deficit.

2️⃣ VIKINGS o14.5 TEAM POINTS: Minnesota has scored at least 15 points in 6/7 games, while Buffalo has allowed at least 15 in 6/7 games. Minnesota’s scores have been 39, 9, 23, 15, 23, 16 and 15.

The passing matchup provides a realistic path to this number. Jefferson averaged 6.4 catches and 89.1 receiving yards across Wentz’s seven Minnesota appearances spanning this season and last. Buffalo has also allowed 10 of its 15 passing touchdowns after halftime, giving Minnesota an opportunity to recover from a slow start.

3️⃣ VIKINGS +10.5 FULL GAME: Minnesota has covered +10.5 in 7/7 games. Buffalo’s opponents have covered this cushion in 6/7 games, with Baltimore the only exception. The extra half point above ten matters: Buffalo’s 10 point win over Detroit would still satisfy this leg.

Minnesota’s defense provides the football foundation. It has produced 25 sacks and allowed touchdowns on only 25% of opponents’ red zone possessions. Pressure can stall drives, while red zone stops turn potential touchdowns into field goals. Those are valuable ways to keep a defeat within ten points, even if Buffalo moves the ball effectively.

4️⃣ JAMES COOK 16+ CARRIES: Cook has reached 16 carries in 5/7 games. His attempts have been 13, 21, 24, 12, 25, 22 and 21. He averages 19.7 carries overall and 22.7 across his last three games.

This is a workload based selection. Indianapolis and Detroit gave their running backs 29 and 34 combined carries against Minnesota, showing that opponents can maintain a substantial rushing commitment. Buffalo already prefers that approach. Cook does not need exceptional yards per carry; he needs sustained possessions and a competitive score that allows Buffalo to keep handing him the ball.

5️⃣ KHALIL SHAKIR 25+ RECEIVING YDS: Shakir has cleared 25 receiving yards in 6/7 games, including his last four. His totals have been 50, 38, 6, 82, 80, 34 and 64 yards, averaging 50.6 per game.

Minnesota’s aggressive pressure creates a reason for Allen to use quick throws, and Shakir’s ability after the catch fits that approach. Against the Rams, 63 of his 80 yards came after the catch. A few short completions can therefore be enough to reach 25. His main limitation is opportunity as Buffalo’s heavier formations can reduce his routes, making this modest yardage requirement preferable to relying on a high volume receiving performance.

text:
$CEG Q3 2026 earnings: Constellation raises its profit outlook and signs Google and Amazon

Constellation Energy locked in multi-decade nuclear contracts with technology giants while summer heat and its Calpine gas fleet lifted profit. Profit per share excluding one-offs rose 66% to $5.06, and chief executive Joe Dominguez announced deals with Google and Amazon that fund over 1,000 megawatts of nuclear expansions. Finance chief Shane Smith raised the full-year outlook, but by our math the plan leaves fourth-quarter profit per share at $2.30, unchanged from a year ago.

• Power volume from businesses owned a year ago: -𝟑.𝟐% (total volume +53.8% with Calpine)
• Profit per share, excluding one-offs: $𝟓.𝟎𝟔 (+66% from a year ago)
• Long-term clean power signed since March: 𝟒𝟑𝐌 𝐌𝐖𝐡 (45% of 2032 clean fleet contracted)
• Full-year profit per share outlook: 𝐑𝐚𝐢𝐬𝐞𝐝 $𝟎.𝟔𝟓 (middle of the range: $12.65 (+35%))

⚖️ 𝐕𝐞𝐫𝐝𝐢𝐜𝐭: 🟢 Bullish

The story got better because Google and Amazon agreed to back $7.3 billion of nuclear upgrades and the Energy Department committed up to $5 billion in low-cost loans. In addition, $2.5 billion of third-quarter free cash flow paid for $1 billion of buybacks and cut short-term debt. One caution: the new nuclear contracts do not start until 2028 to 2032, and the company models lower above-baseline trading margins for 2027.

The question now is whether 2027 profit can keep growing before the new data center contracts start paying in 2028. Bulls point to power prices above baseline assumptions and continued share buybacks; skeptics point to capped Mid-Atlantic capacity prices, weak Texas gas margins and a $900 million drop in modeled 2027 trading margins. Next quarter's first formal 2027 profit outlook will settle it.

Full article with charts - link in bio

🐂 𝐁𝐮𝐥𝐥 𝐂𝐚𝐬𝐞

🟢🟢 𝐆𝐨𝐨𝐠𝐥𝐞 𝐚𝐧𝐝 𝐀𝐦𝐚𝐳𝐨𝐧 𝐅𝐮𝐧𝐝 𝐎𝐧𝐞 𝐆𝐢𝐠𝐚𝐰𝐚𝐭𝐭 𝐨𝐟 𝐍𝐞𝐰 𝐍𝐮𝐜𝐥𝐞𝐚𝐫 𝐏𝐨𝐰𝐞𝐫
Constellation wants technology companies to pay for long-term nuclear power and fund plant upgrades. Chief executive Joe Dominguez said this quarter's deals help with "powering a growing economy while protecting existing customers" and bring new power "coming online with no costs being borne by existing customers".

The power producer signed contracts for about 4,560 megawatts across three customers this quarter. Since March, long-term deals cover 43 million megawatt-hours of annual power by 2032, lifting the contracted share of its clean baseload fleet to 45%.

• Google: a 20-year agreement enabling $4.3 billion of investment across 11 nuclear units to add 890 megawatts, plus a 15-year, 2,700-megawatt power supply deal
• Amazon: a 20-year, 690-megawatt agreement enabling over $3 billion of investment at Calvert Cliffs, adding 190 megawatts
• Peak+: a first 20-year, 270-megawatt contract for "an integrated solution that brings together new capacity, including new generation and demand response, with energy products to help large customers meet their evolving needs"
• Federal loan: a conditional commitment from the Department of Energy for up to $5 billion at 0.375 percentage points above US Treasury rates, saving about $40 million a year before taxes

These agreements matter because hyperscale data centers are paying to expand existing nuclear plants rather than waiting for new gas turbines. What to watch: the remaining 113 million megawatt-hours of uncontracted 2032 nuclear output. More deals under the Peak+ structure would show that pending grid rules do not slow customer signing.

🟢🟢 𝐒𝐮𝐦𝐦𝐞𝐫 𝐇𝐞𝐚𝐭, 𝐂𝐚𝐥𝐩𝐢𝐧𝐞 𝐚𝐧𝐝 𝐋𝐨𝐰𝐞𝐫 𝐅𝐮𝐞𝐥 𝐂𝐨𝐬𝐭𝐬 𝐋𝐢𝐟𝐭𝐞𝐝 𝐏𝐫𝐨𝐟𝐢𝐭
Constellation added natural gas power plants by acquiring Calpine in January and benefited from higher grid capacity prices in the Mid-Atlantic and Midwest. Operating profit per share excluding one-offs jumped 66% from a year ago to $5.06. "This strong performance allowed us to raise the midpoint of our adjusted operating earnings guidance range for the second time this year," finance chief Shane Smith said.

Operating margin rose 9.6 percentage points to 26.1% of revenue. Purchased power and fuel — the cost of buying electricity and gas to run plants and serve customers — fell by 8.2 percentage points of revenue to 46.1%, and operating and maintenance costs fell by 2.2 points to 20.8%.

Reference power prices in PJM West rose 50% from a year ago to $69.97 per megawatt-hour while natural gas prices fell, widening profit margins despite $175 million in extra employee bonus costs for the year. What to watch: fourth-quarter commercial margins, because a second quarter of wide spreads would lift the starting base for 2027.

🟢 𝐎𝐧𝐞 𝐁𝐢𝐥𝐥𝐢𝐨𝐧 𝐃𝐨𝐥𝐥𝐚𝐫𝐬 𝐨𝐟 𝐁𝐮𝐲𝐛𝐚𝐜𝐤𝐬 𝐏𝐚𝐢𝐝 𝐃𝐨𝐰𝐧 𝐃𝐞𝐛𝐭 𝐓𝐨𝐨
During the first half of the year, Constellation spent $2.0 billion buying back its own stock while free cash flow was negative, funding the purchases with short-term debt. In the third quarter, the utility group spent another $1.03 billion on buybacks, bringing the nine-month total to $3.0 billion and leaving $2.0 billion under its authorization.

Unlike in the first half, third-quarter operations generated $2.49 billion of free cash flow by our math. That cash covered the stock purchases and allowed Smith to cut short-term borrowings by $1.24 billion to $3.99 billion, lowering total debt net of cash to $22.38 billion.

What to watch: the closing of the required power plant sales by year-end, represented by $5.66 billion of assets held for sale on the balance sheet. Collecting that cash will show whether Constellation retires the remaining short-term debt.

🐻 𝐁𝐞𝐚𝐫 𝐂𝐚𝐬𝐞

🔴🔴 𝐍𝐞𝐰 𝐓𝐞𝐜𝐡 𝐂𝐨𝐧𝐭𝐫𝐚𝐜𝐭𝐬 𝐃𝐨 𝐍𝐨𝐭 𝐋𝐢𝐟𝐭 𝐏𝐫𝐨𝐟𝐢𝐭 𝐔𝐧𝐭𝐢𝐥 𝟐𝟎𝟐𝟖
Dominguez highlighted over 1,000 megawatts of new clean power deals alongside the raised 2026 profit outlook. However, the Google nuclear upgrades begin in 2028, the Peak+ contract starts in 2028, and the Amazon expansion at Calvert Cliffs comes online between 2030 and 2032. None of the agreements signed in 2026 are even included in the company's contracted clean power table through 2030.

• Fourth-quarter profit per share implied by the full-year outlook: $2.30 at the middle of the range, unchanged from $2.30 a year ago by our math
• PJM capacity price growth: slowed to 22% from a year ago ($329.17 per megawatt-day), down from 165% growth last quarter, because auctions hit the price cap
• 2027 enhanced gross margin (profit above baseline assumptions): modeled at $2.15 billion to $2.55 billion, down from $3.20 billion to $3.30 billion in 2026

Meanwhile, Constellation still did not disclose the exact prices Google or Amazon will pay, keeping its broad $20 to $50 per megawatt-hour premium estimate. Because grid capacity prices are already at their cap and new nuclear deals start years from now, near-term profit growth is slowing. What to watch: the first-time 2027 profit outlook next quarter, which will test whether lower enhanced margins cause earnings to drop next year.

🔴 𝐓𝐞𝐱𝐚𝐬 𝐏𝐨𝐰𝐞𝐫 𝐏𝐫𝐢𝐜𝐞𝐬 𝐅𝐞𝐥𝐥 𝐀𝐟𝐭𝐞𝐫 𝐁𝐮𝐲𝐢𝐧𝐠 𝐂𝐚𝐥𝐩𝐢𝐧𝐞
Purchasing Calpine gave Constellation a large fleet of natural gas power plants in Texas (the ERCOT grid). While power prices jumped in the Mid-Atlantic, third-quarter reference electricity prices in North Texas slipped 1.8% from a year ago to $34.41 per megawatt-hour.

In the company's modeling tables, the 2026 North Texas spark spread — the profit margin a gas plant earns after paying for fuel — stood at $12.82 per megawatt-hour as of September 30, well below its $21.00 baseline assumption. In addition, the natural gas, oil and hydro fleet recorded a 5.9% forced outage rate (the share of time plants were unexpectedly unavailable).

What to watch: North Texas forward spark spreads for 2027, currently $17.26 per megawatt-hour against a $22.00 baseline assumption. A reading that stays below the baseline would drag on gas fleet profits next year.

🔴 𝐑𝐢𝐬𝐤𝐬 𝐓𝐡𝐢𝐬 𝐐𝐮𝐚𝐫𝐭𝐞𝐫 𝐃𝐢𝐝 𝐍𝐨𝐭 𝐀𝐧𝐬𝐰𝐞𝐫
Several standing regulatory, contract and accounting risks received no final resolution in the third-quarter materials.

• Grid rules for large customers: Constellation noted that "Regulatory goals are clear, although rules are not final" in PJM; a final Federal Energy Regulatory Commission order will settle how data centers connect.
• Illinois state nuclear credits: volumes under the Illinois Carbon Mitigation Credit program drop from 53 million megawatt-hours in 2026 to 23 million in 2027 when the program expires in May 2027, shifting those plants to the federal tax credit floor.
• Calpine contract accounting drag: non-cash charges for amortizing acquired Calpine commodity contracts were $39 million ($0.11 per share) in Q3 after $149 million in Q2, and will continue across the contracts' multi-year life.
• Former Calpine owners' stock lock-up: the second tranche of 25 million shares unlocks on June 30, 2027.
• Crane nuclear restart: received no new milestone update this quarter ahead of its planned second-half 2027 return.

👓 𝐎𝐭𝐡𝐞𝐫 𝐓𝐡𝐞𝐦𝐞𝐬

𝐂𝐨𝐧𝐬𝐭𝐞𝐥𝐥𝐚𝐭𝐢𝐨𝐧 𝐁𝐮𝐲𝐬 𝐚 𝐍𝐞𝐰 𝐄𝐧𝐠𝐥𝐚𝐧𝐝 𝐆𝐚𝐬 𝐏𝐥𝐚𝐧𝐭 𝐟𝐨𝐫 $𝟕𝟏𝟓 𝐌𝐢𝐥𝐥𝐢𝐨𝐧
Constellation agreed to buy the Rhode Island State Energy Center from Shell Energy North America for $715 million. The natural gas plant has 609 megawatts of capacity and sells power into the competitive New England wholesale market. The deal price works out to about $1,174 per kilowatt, below the roughly $1,419 per kilowatt Constellation is receiving for selling its Brazos Valley gas plant in Texas, and requires regulatory approval.

— • — • —

💲 𝐎𝐭𝐡𝐞𝐫 𝐊𝐏𝐈𝐬

𝐓𝐨𝐭𝐚𝐥 𝐞𝐥𝐞𝐜𝐭𝐫𝐢𝐜𝐢𝐭𝐲 𝐬𝐮𝐩𝐩𝐥𝐲 𝐚𝐧𝐝 𝐬𝐚𝐥𝐞𝐬 𝐯𝐨𝐥𝐮𝐦𝐞 (𝟐𝟔𝐐𝟑): 𝟏𝟎𝟖,𝟔𝟕𝟒 𝐆𝐖𝐡  ⇗ accelerating
Total power supplied rose 53.8% from a year ago because the Calpine acquisition added 40,277 gigawatt-hours. By our math, power supplied by businesses Constellation owned a year ago fell 3.2% to 68,397 gigawatt-hours, as lower wholesale power purchases in other regions offset flat nuclear output.

𝐍𝐮𝐜𝐥𝐞𝐚𝐫 𝐟𝐥𝐞𝐞𝐭 𝐜𝐚𝐩𝐚𝐜𝐢𝐭𝐲 𝐟𝐚𝐜𝐭𝐨𝐫 (𝟐𝟔𝐐𝟑): 𝟗𝟕.𝟐%  ⇗ accelerating
Nuclear reliability rose from 96.8% a year ago and 93.0% last quarter, reaching 99.2% across the summer months. The power producer completed 20 planned refueling outage days, down from 23 a year ago, which kept its reactors running when summer power prices peaked.

𝐍𝐞𝐭 𝐢𝐧𝐜𝐨𝐦𝐞 𝐚𝐭𝐭𝐫𝐢𝐛𝐮𝐭𝐚𝐛𝐥𝐞 𝐭𝐨 𝐜𝐨𝐦𝐦𝐨𝐧 𝐬𝐡𝐚𝐫𝐞𝐡𝐨𝐥𝐝𝐞𝐫𝐬 (𝟐𝟔𝐐𝟑): $𝟏,𝟖𝟑𝟓 𝐦𝐢𝐥𝐥𝐢𝐨𝐧  ⇄ reversing
Reported profit nearly doubled from $930 million a year ago ($5.19 per share vs $2.97), reversing last quarter's 39% drop. Favorable paper gains on economic hedges ($127 million after tax) and a $108 million state tax adjustment lifted reported profit above the $1,792 million figure excluding one-offs.

— • — • —

🔮 𝐆𝐮𝐢𝐝𝐚𝐧𝐜𝐞

𝐅𝐘𝟐𝟔 𝐎𝐩𝐞𝐫𝐚𝐭𝐢𝐧𝐠 𝐞𝐚𝐫𝐧𝐢𝐧𝐠𝐬 𝐩𝐞𝐫 𝐬𝐡𝐚𝐫𝐞, 𝐞𝐱𝐜𝐥𝐮𝐝𝐢𝐧𝐠 𝐨𝐧𝐞-𝐨𝐟𝐟𝐬: $𝟏𝟐.𝟓𝟎–$𝟏𝟐.𝟖𝟎  ⇘ decelerating
🠅 raised from $11.50–$12.50
Raised. The middle of the range moved up $0.65 to $12.65 per share, representing 34.7% growth for the year. It is the second raise this year: +$0.50 in Q2 and +$0.65 in Q3. By our math, after earning $10.35 in the first nine months, the plan leaves $2.30 per share for Q4, unchanged from $2.30 in Q4 last year despite owning Calpine.

𝐅𝐘𝟐𝟔 𝐎𝐩𝐞𝐫𝐚𝐭𝐢𝐧𝐠 𝐚𝐧𝐝 𝐦𝐚𝐢𝐧𝐭𝐞𝐧𝐚𝐧𝐜𝐞 𝐜𝐨𝐬𝐭𝐬, 𝐞𝐱𝐜𝐥𝐮𝐝𝐢𝐧𝐠 𝐨𝐧𝐞-𝐨𝐟𝐟𝐬: $𝟕,𝟎𝟕𝟓 𝐦𝐢𝐥𝐥𝐢𝐨𝐧  ⇗ accelerating
🠅 raised from $7,025 million
Raised. Expected full-year operating and maintenance costs excluding one-offs increased by $50 million. Baseline plant operating costs stayed flat at $6,900 million, but the utility group added $50 million of employee bonus expenses (to $175 million in total) tied to beating its commercial trading targets. For 2027, total operating and maintenance costs are modeled flat at $7,075 million.

— • — • —

❓ 𝐊𝐞𝐲 𝐐𝐮𝐞𝐬𝐭𝐢𝐨𝐧𝐬

𝐖𝐡𝐲 𝐝𝐨𝐞𝐬 𝐭𝐡𝐞 𝐨𝐮𝐭𝐥𝐨𝐨𝐤 𝐩𝐨𝐢𝐧𝐭 𝐭𝐨 𝐟𝐥𝐚𝐭 𝐟𝐨𝐮𝐫𝐭𝐡-𝐪𝐮𝐚𝐫𝐭𝐞𝐫 𝐩𝐫𝐨𝐟𝐢𝐭?
By our math, the raised full-year outlook leaves $2.30 per share for Q4, matching last year's $2.30 before Constellation owned Calpine. Did the third quarter pull trading profits forward from the fourth quarter?

NFL Power Rankings heading into Week 10:

1) #49ers - the best most complete team in football, still. Will only get healthier with the return of Mike Evans. Purdy playing at an MVP level

2) #DaBears - GOOD BETTER BEST! Look I know the Bucs game was too close for comfort but I think a few things: the Bucs matchup well with the Bears and they can stop the run, which forced the Bears to throw more and Caleb got sloppy. Simmons makes a huge difference and the Bears still a complete team

3) #Jaguars - the additions at DT and S at the deadline show that this team is dead serious on winning, and they are so aware of the missing pieces needed. The most complete team in the AFC and no reason why they can’t come out of it. They just can’t beat themselves in the playoffs that’s what it comes down to

4) #Rams - again, record is overrated. Assuming Puka and Adams return this season, the Rams are a complete team who will only get better on defense, as Donald will get better each game and the return of Garrett just adds another dimension to their defense. I am not as concerned with the injury to Nacua since the Rams can beat most teams running the ball with two stud backs and playing good D. Look out 

5) #BillsMafia - I hate to put the Bills this high but I had no choice. We will learn a lot about their defense when they play some real teams down the stretch. Offense can beat you in different ways and their commitment to the run on MNF was impressive. But not a complete team.

6) #ChiefsKingdom - one would say they are concerned about KC when their run game gets shut down, but again people fail to realize how great Mahomes and Reid are. They have the benefit of the doubt regardless of stats because they turn it on when it matters most in the playoffs. Until that changes, as long as they are healthy and in the playoff mix, they won’t fall too far below 5.

But with a similar formula this team has made a Super Bowl, so Burrow has proven he can get it done. And as long as he is playing at an MVP level with those two WRs, they are a contender 

9) #Lions - we know the Lions offense is good. What is encouraging is that their defense has played better recently. They have the experience so that gives them the edge over the number 10 team

10) #GoPackGo - Jordan Love has been on a heater , with those two WRs playing incredible. Defense getting better and will get Parsons back. Only concern is the lack of run game.

2027: MORKA HIGHLIGHTS TINUBU, OBOREVWORI’S DEVELOPMENT GAINS AS IKA ARTISANS PLEDGE SUPPORT FOR APC

The National Publicity Secretary of the All Progressives Congress (APC), Barr. Felix Morka, CON, has highlighted the economic and infrastructural development efforts of President Bola Ahmed Tinubu and Delta State Governor, Rt. Hon. Sheriff Oborevwori, while pledging to facilitate access to government empowerment programmes for artisans in Ika South Local Government Area of Delta State.

Morka made the commitment on Wednesday, November 11, 2026, during an enlarged engagement with members of the Ika South Artisans Association in Agbor, Delta State, where he underscored the importance of artisans to economic growth, community development and the everyday functioning of society.

Describing artisans as indispensable contributors to national development, the APC spokesman noted that virtually every aspect of modern life, from housing and transportation to infrastructure and essential services, depended on the skills, creativity and services of artisans.

On the national economy, Morka defended the economic reforms of President Tinubu's administration, explaining that the country had inherited significant fiscal and economic challenges, including the burden of fuel subsidy payments and pressure on foreign exchange reserves.

He stated that the reforms had strengthened government revenues and expanded the fiscal capacity of federal, state and local governments to undertake development projects.

Citing increased federal allocations to Delta State, Morka highlighted the improved revenue position of the state and its potential to accelerate infrastructure delivery and improve the lives of citizens.

He also pointed to major federal infrastructure projects, including the Lagos-Calabar Coastal Highway, alongside ongoing road construction and bridge projects, as evidence of President Tinubu administration's commitment to national infrastructure renewal.

At the state level, he commended Governor Oborevwori for prioritising infrastructure development and executing projects aimed at improving connectivity and stimulating economic activities across Delta State.

Turning to the concerns of the artisans, Morka pledged to identify relevant federal and state government empowerment initiatives and facilitate direct engagement between the association's leadership and the heads of agencies responsible for implementing such programmes.

The engagement also featured discussions on the constitutional responsibilities of elected public officials and the respective roles of the President, governors, senators, members of the House of Representatives and members of State Houses of Assembly.

Morka urged the participants to make informed electoral choices ahead of the 2027 general elections, calling on them to support President Tinubu's re-election bid, Governor Oborevwori and other APC candidates.

He particularly appealed to women at the gathering to support greater female representation in elective offices, urging them to rally behind the APC candidate for Ika South Constituency, Hon. Cordelia Anyagwu, in her bid for election into the Delta State House of Assembly.

Other prominent APC leaders and stakeholders at the engagement included the Executive Chairman of Ika South Local Government Council, Hon. Engr. Jerry Ehiwarior; Dr. Donald Peterson; Hon. Emmanuel Osazuwa; Hon. Frank Izekor; and Hon. Cosmas Igbenije, alongside Hon. Cordelia Anyagwu.

In their response, participants expressed support for the APC and its candidates ahead of the 2027 elections, declaring their readiness to support the party across the five electoral positions: President, Governor, Senator, House of Representatives and State House of Assembly.

Morka thanked the leadership and members of the Ika South Artisans Association for their warm reception and active participation,assuring them of his commitment to ensuring that their concerns and aspirations receive appropriate attention
