text:
Japan’s Most Dangerous Military Constraint Is Time 
Japan’s most consequential defence vulnerability may not be the absolute size of its military forces, the sophistication of Chinese weapons or the willingness of the United States to honour its security commitments. It is the potential mismatch between the time required to authorise, organise and execute defensive preparations and the time available before military escalation makes those preparations prohibitively dangerous or operationally ineffective.

The principal findings are:

– The legal authority to prepare is not equivalent to political approval to act. Japan’s crisis-management architecture distinguishes between anticipated armed attack, imminent armed attack, an attack that has occurred and a survival-threatening situation involving an attack on a closely related country. These categories carry different legal and political consequences.

– The southwestern islands are a decisive geographic exposure. Yonaguni, Ishigaki and Miyako sit along the operational approaches to Taiwan and the passage between the East China Sea and the Philippine Sea. Their defence requires early movement of forces, access to facilities and coordination with civilian authorities.

– The threat environment is active rather than theoretical. On 14 October 2026, Japan documented the Chinese aircraft carrier Liaoning and three accompanying destroyers passing between Okinawa and Miyako into the Pacific. Aircraft operations were subsequently observed approximately 250 kilometres south of Ishigaki. mod.go.jp+1

– Access to Japanese territory is not automatically available to U.S. forces. Article II of the Japan–U.S. Status of Forces Agreement requires bilateral arrangements for designated facilities and areas, including temporary-use arrangements. Military urgency does not independently extinguish Japanese sovereignty or domestic legal requirements.

– Civilian evacuation and military mobilisation compete for time and infrastructure. Ports, airports, aircraft, ships and local administrative capacity must serve overlapping defence and population-protection requirements.

– Financial commitment does not automatically produce operational availability. Japan’s fiscal-year 2026 defence programme allocates ¥8.8093 trillion on an expenditure basis and ¥8.2607 trillion on a contract basis within its Defence Buildup Program. These measures are not interchangeable with deployed capability or crisis readiness. https://t.co/Zv5YqeblHJ

– The strategic priority is institutional preparation before a crisis, including legally validated contingency procedures, faster government coordination, realistic political decision exercises and tested arrangements for access, transport, logistics and civilian protection.

Principal judgment: Japan and the United States could possess sufficient aggregate military strength to contest a regional attack while still losing critical operational options through delayed decisions and incomplete implementation procedures. The decisive uncertainty is whether their existing administrative and alliance mechanisms can deliver lawful, politically sustainable and operationally timely decisions under genuine crisis pressure.

Japan’s Most Dangerous Military Constraint Is Time
Why Tokyo’s military transformation could be overtaken by the decisions required to make it operational

Japan is committing trillions of yen to strengthen its defence, yet its most consequential weakness may lie outside the weapons budget: the interval between recognising a threat and obtaining the authority, access and transport needed to respond. In October 2026, Chinese carrier operations south of Japan’s southwestern islands coincided with a Japan–United States defence agenda centred on air dispersal, facility access and a stronger regional presence. The contradiction is structural. Japan can purchase missiles and establish new commands faster than a crisis can necessarily be translated into lawful use of civilian infrastructure, coherent alliance decisions and the movement of people and equipment. Its constitutional safeguards are not the problem to be abolished; administrative assumptions that make legally available options unusable are the problem to be tested. For Tokyo and Washington, deterrence now depends on keeping those options open before a first strike.

The first island chain is becoming a timetable, not merely a map
Japan’s southwestern islands turn a Taiwan crisis into an immediate question of Japanese territorial security without making the two contingencies legally identical. Yonaguni lies approximately 110 kilometres from Taiwan; Ishigaki and Miyako form part of the island network linking surveillance, local defence, maritime passages and reinforcement. Japan has established Ground Self-Defense Force positions on Yonaguni, Miyako, Ishigaki and Amami Ōshima, with coastal surveillance, security, anti-ship and air-defence functions. Their military value depends not simply on where they stand, but on whether fuel, ammunition, communications, transport and supporting personnel can reach them when required.

The October 2026 passage of the Chinese aircraft carrier Liaoning and three destroyers between Okinawa and Miyako made the problem visible. Japan’s Joint Staff recorded the formation on 13 October, its passage toward the Pacific on 14 October, and approximately ten carrier-aircraft takeoffs and landings south of Ishigaki that day. These observations prove neither an imminent Chinese attack nor a planned Taiwan operation. They show that the maritime approaches needed for Japanese surveillance and allied movement are also accessible to major Chinese formations. In Japan’s 2026 defence assessment, Liaoning had undertaken 13 recorded Pacific deployments and Shandong nine by the end of May 2026. Geographical distance can no longer be assumed to provide sufficient administrative warning.

A ¥43 trillion programme cannot purchase permissions
Japan’s Defence Buildup Program envisages approximately ¥43 trillion over fiscal years 2023–2027, alongside distinct expenditure and contracting frameworks. For fiscal 2026, its expenditure-basis allocation is ¥8.8093 trillion, up ¥334.5 billion or 3.9% on the previous year; the contract-basis allocation is ¥8.2607 trillion, down ¥172.5 billion or 2.0%. Those are different accounting measures, not interchangeable indications of readiness. The same distinction applies to ammunition: the 2026 budget identifies approximately ¥907.5 billion when related allocations are included, against ¥255.3 billion under a narrower category. Adding them together would count overlapping expenditure twice.

The procurement transmission mechanism is slower than budget approval. A missile must be manufactured, accepted, stored, assigned to trained personnel and supported with maintenance and communications. Japan’s Ministry of Defense has acknowledged spare-parts shortages, equipment rendered unavailable by maintenance problems, and the use of parts from other equipment to restore selected systems to service. Fiscal 2026 sustainment and maintenance provision reaches approximately ¥2.124 trillion on the broader accounting basis. Across 283 Self-Defense Force locations, more than 20,000 buildings fall within the review of defence facilities for renovation and resilience. A contract does not harden a depot, replenish a stockpile or return an aircraft to service on the date it is signed. Defense of Japan 2026 — Sustainability and Resiliency.

The law permits preparation before it permits combat
Article 9 of Japan’s Constitution constrains the use of force, but it is not a general ban on every form of defensive readiness. The 2003 contingency framework distinguishes an anticipated armed attack from an armed attack situation, the latter including a clearly imminent danger of an attack on Japan. The 2014 Cabinet decision and 2015 Legislation for Peace and Security also established a narrowly defined survival-threatening situation involving an attack on a closely related country. Under the constitutional three conditions, force requires a qualifying armed attack and grave threat, the absence of other appropriate means, and the minimum necessary response. Recognising an imminent danger can support a statutory response without automatically satisfying all conditions for actual combat.

That legal differentiation is indispensable, but it creates demanding interfaces among the Cabinet, Prime Minister, Diet, ministries and military commanders. A Basic Response Policy must articulate the recognised circumstances and government response; defence-operation orders are subject to parliamentary approval in principle. In a Taiwan contingency, intelligence collection, the defence of Japanese territory, temporary American access and Japanese combat participation may rest on different authorities. Treating all four as the same decision would either overstate what the law allows or needlessly exclude preparations that it does permit. The practical deficiency to correct is not constitutional restraint but the absence of sufficiently rehearsed routes from lawful authority to administrative execution. Defense of Japan 2026 — Framework for Defence Operations.

American access is a treaty relationship, not a master key
The 1960 Japan–United States Security Treaty distinguishes the common-danger commitment of Article V from the facilities framework of Article VI. Under the Status of Forces Agreement, Article II(4)(b) allows agreed temporary American use of facilities and areas; Article XXV assigns implementation questions to a bilateral Joint Committee. Neither provision makes every municipal airport, commercial port or privately controlled site immediately available. Japan must possess or lawfully secure the rights required to provide access, while specified combat operations may raise separate prior-consultation questions. An American military requirement is not itself a Japanese authorisation.

The alliance is responding to the operational consequences. Japan established its Joint Operations Command on 24 March 2025, while United States Forces Japan began a phased transition toward a joint force headquarters. At their 28 October 2026 meeting, Defence Minister Shinjiro Koizumi and his American counterpart prioritised flexible air dispersal, broader facility access and a stronger southwestern presence. Keen Sword 27, held on 19–29 October 2026, involved approximately 57,000 personnel, including 12,000 Americans, and activities at civilian airports and ports. Yet exercise access does not guarantee crisis access, and command integration cannot transfer sovereign authority from one capital to another. The next measure of progress is approved, tested implementation rather than increasingly elaborate exercise scenarios. Japan–U.S. Defense Ministerial Meeting — 28 October 2026.

Evacuation and reinforcement draw on the same constrained network
Japan’s March 2026 planning for five Sakishima municipalities counted 112,337 registered residents as of 1 January 2025 and added approximately 10,000 visitors to arrive at a rounded planning population of 120,000. The government identified potential outward transport capacity of about 20,000 people per day—an indicative six-day calculation, not an assured wartime evacuation schedule. Ports, airfields, ships, aircraft, medical transfers and reception facilities must work together for that capacity to have practical meaning. The January 2026 evacuation exercise involved 94 organisations and 425 participants, compared with 31 organisations and 106 participants in fiscal 2022. Broader participation demonstrates institutional reach, not verified throughput under attack. Okinawa Remote-Island Evacuation Planning — Cabinet Secretariat — March 2026.

Reinforcement faces the same physical bottlenecks. Japan established a joint maritime transportation group in March 2025 and introduced four named transport vessels through March 2026; its private-sector programme envisages an eight-vessel framework. Those assets cannot be counted as eight continuously available emergency ships, still less as a guarantee that island ports can receive their loads while evacuating civilians. A vessel without a berth, a fuel reserve without distribution, or an airfield without authorised use is nominal capacity. The decision to move forces inward while moving civilians outward belongs to a government coordinating different legal responsibilities, not to a spreadsheet that assumes unlimited infrastructure.

The next 24 months will expose whether reform has produced executable choices
Through November 2028, the immediate test will be whether the final stages of the 2023–2027 Defence Buildup Program become measurable availability rather than additional appropriations. Japan and the United States must turn their October 2026 commitments on air dispersal and facility access into validated bilateral procedures, while the Joint Operations Command and its American counterpart demonstrate that military coordination works alongside civilian and Cabinet decision-making. The 2015 bilateral defence guidelines already provide a framework for cooperation; they do not grant automatic combat authority. European industrial participation, including Italy and the United Kingdom in the Global Combat Air Programme, and France’s April 2026 defence roadmap add strategic depth, but none can resolve the immediate Japanese access and mobilisation problem.

The cost of inaction would be concentrated before it appeared in a defence-budget table. Sakishima residents would face evacuation decisions taken with less transport capacity and greater uncertainty; Japanese and American units would face a narrower choice of usable facilities; commercial transport operators would absorb disrupted schedules and competing obligations; and taxpayers would finance equipment whose effective use still depended on missing procedures or support. China’s recorded activity around Taiwan—more than 3,700 military-aircraft observations and approximately 2,600 naval-vessel observations in 2025—shows why preserving warning time matters without proving that war is inevitable. The policy choice is not between speed and legality. It is whether Tokyo and Washington make lawful preparations executable before political leaders are forced to choose among options that have already expired.

STATE HOUSE PRESS RELEASE 

President Tinubu Focused, Supercharging State Coffers, Fast-Tracking Growth, Says VP Shettima 

...Leads APC Presidential Campaign Council in rapid-fire approach to securing President's re-election at Akure rally 

...Says Ondo's Federation Account receipts rose by over 22% in the first nine months of 2026 

The Vice President, Senator Kashim Shettima, has affirmed that President Bola Ahmed Tinubu's economic reforms are bolstering the fiscal strength of state governments, accelerating critical infrastructure development and expanding economic opportunities across Nigeria. 

According to him, the economic policies of the Tinubu administration have supercharged state-level revenues, unlocking vital investments in roads, agriculture, power, education and healthcare, with Ondo State recording a significant increase in revenue from the Federation Account. 

Speaking on Wednesday at the All Progressives Congress (APC) Presidential Campaign Rally in Akure, the Ondo State capital, Senator Shettima recalled that Ondo received over 22 per cent more from the Federation Account in the first nine months of 2026 than in the same period in 2025. 

Representing the President at the campaign rally, the VP told the mammoth crowd gathered at the Akure Township Stadium that the gains recorded so far demonstrate the importance of sustained reforms and cooperation between the Federal Government and subnational governments. 

"Our promise to prioritise the welfare of Ondo State has been demonstrated through the increased revenue accruing to Ondo State. This has come with President Tinubu's reforms. Even in the first nine months of this year, Ondo received over 22 per cent more from the Federation Account than it did in the same period last year," he stated. 

The Vice President commended Governor Lucky Orimisan Aiyedatiwa for deploying the additional resources towards development projects, noting that the administration's interventions are addressing longstanding infrastructure and economic challenges. 

On agriculture and rural development, he disclosed that the Federal Government, working with the state government and development partners, had constructed, rehabilitated and maintained more than 386 kilometres of rural roads to improve access to farms and markets. 

"We are aware that a cocoa farmer in Idanre knows how much of his earnings a bad road can swallow. We have worked with your governor and our partners to build, repair and maintain more than 386 kilometres of rural roads," he declared. 

VP Shettima also highlighted the Lagos–Calabar Coastal Highway, which he said had reached Ajegeri in Ilaje, the revalidation of the Port Ondo licence and the completion of 48 kilometres of concrete pavement on the Sagamu–Ore Road. 

In the power sector, he announced the completion and commissioning of the Ode-Erinje transmission line and substation, while noting that pipes had begun arriving for the Owena water supply project in Akure. 

The Vice President further listed the operationalisation of the Federal University of Technology, Akure (FUTA) Teaching Hospital, five TETFund projects at Rufus Giwa Polytechnic, Owo, and healthcare support through 203 public facilities under the Basic Health Care Provision Fund. 

He said the Nigerian Education Loan Fund (NELFUND), student hostel projects, MSME financing and grants are expanding opportunities for students, traders, artisans and small businesses across the state. 

On security, Senator Shettima reaffirmed the administration's commitment to strengthening security institutions and improving personnel welfare, citing the legislation providing statutory backing for the Police Training School in Oyin-Akoko. 

"We inherited a compromised security system, no doubt, and Ondo State paid a regrettable price. But we overcame all the attacks on us because we stood together and declared that never shall we let the enemies of the state triumph," he said. 

The Vice President thanked the people of Ondo State for their continued support, assuring them that President Tinubu's administration remained determined to consolidate its reforms and complete ongoing development projects. 

"Our economy is stable now. We have put the naysayers to shame. And the cause is not magic; it is your choice, your vote, your trust, your patience, your faith, and the leadership of His Excellency, President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, GCFR," he declared. 

"We will never take you for granted as we march together to the polls again to renew the mandate of our leader, His Excellency President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, and finish what we have begun," he said. 

Earlier, Ondo State Governor Lucky Aiyedatiwa vowed that the people of Ondo State would turn out en masse to vote for President Tinubu because the state is a progressive state, just as the President is a progressive. He also applauded the ongoing reforms the Tinubu administration has embarked on to revamp the nation's economy. 

Recalling that the people of Ondo State voted massively for the President in 2023, the governor said, "We voted for you because we believe in you, because we know what you can do, and because we know your track record as a former governor of Lagos State. Mr. President, you have not disappointed us at all. You have also done well here in Ondo State by giving us three ministers." 

Aiyedatiwa acknowledged that the reforms undertaken by President Tinubu have been effective and have brought prosperity to the nation, even as he promised that the people of Ondo "will all go to the mountains, to the hills, and everywhere to tell the people about" the President's re-election. 

On his part, the National Chairman of the APC, Professor Nentawe Goshwe Yilwatda, waxed rhetorical, saying that of the 18 presidential candidates lined up for the 2027 presidential poll, President Tinubu remains the most experienced, exposed and prepared among them, as well as the only person who can take Nigeria to the next level. 

"We are here because 18 candidates have been presented as presidential candidates by 18 political parties ahead of the January 16 presidential election. The question is: Among those 18 candidates, who has the wisdom of experience, wisdom of exposure, wisdom of preparation and wisdom of purpose? Who is the person that can take us to the next level? That is why today I am here to present a candidate who is fearless; a candidate who does not run from any problem," he added. 

Describing the Tinubu/Shettima ticket as the most competent, Yilwatda also characterised President Tinubu as the most prepared candidate, possessing all the leadership qualities Nigeria needs at this defining moment. 

Also speaking, the Chairman of the Progressive Governors' Forum (PGF) and Imo State Governor, Senator Hope Uzodimma, urged the people of Ondo State to go to the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) and collect all their Permanent Voter Cards (PVCs) still piled up at the commission's office in order to vote massively for the President in the January 16, 2027, presidential poll. 

"Going by the last count, we have 2.4 million registered voters in Ondo State. Out of 2.4 million voters, only 1.4 million have collected their PVCs. The question is, without your PVCs, how would you support President Bola Ahmed Tinubu? 

"I, therefore, want to urge you to go to the INEC office and collect all your PVCs that are lying there so that on January 16, 2027, you will be eligible to vote. I have seen the enthusiasm of all the leaders in those states in support of President Bola Ahmed Tinubu—an incredible goodwill I have seen," he stated, calling for unity among party leaders. 

For his part, the Director-General of the APC Presidential Campaign Council, Senator Abdulaziz Yari, highlighted President Tinubu's development strides in Ondo State and wished the President had brought similar infrastructure projects to his home state of Zamfara. 

"My state will grow and become like Ondo State. People of Ondo, on the 16th of January, you need to come out—youths, women, and the elderly—to ensure that Asiwaju wins. We are not looking for Asiwaju to win by a small margin. We are looking for Asiwaju to get millions of votes that will secure the presidency," the DG urged the people. 

The DG appreciated the leaders for all the mobilisation witnessed from the entrance into Akure to the venue of the campaign rally, urging them to work together to ensure maximum votes for President Tinubu.

CURRENTBLOCK DAILY WATCH | NOVEMBER 11, 2026

Wednesday;  Security Challenges, Institutional Adoption and the Expanding Digital Economy

What's Shaping the Decentralised World...

ACROSS PROTOCOL RECOVERS HIJACKED WEBSITE AFTER PHISHING ATTACK

Cross-chain bridge Across Protocol has regained control of its official domain, https://t.co/cgZFZYeI88, following a social engineering attack targeting its domain registrar, Namecheap.

The attackers briefly redirected users to a fraudulent website designed to compromise connected cryptocurrency wallets.

Across confirmed that its website has been restored and pledged to fully compensate affected users. Security researchers estimate that approximately $350,000 was stolen, although the protocol has not independently confirmed the final loss figure.

The incident highlights how vulnerabilities in domain management can threaten even established blockchain infrastructure.

INITIA HALTS NETWORK AFTER SECOND SECURITY EXPLOIT IN THREE WEEKS

Layer-1 blockchain Initia has suffered another security incident after attackers compromised infrastructure credentials and manipulated cross-chain transfer operations.

The team reported that approximately $3.27 million in assets were moved, with around $2.16 million remaining frozen on the halted network.

Initia says it is rebuilding affected infrastructure, strengthening access controls and working with security partners to recover assets.

The incident follows another exploit in October, raising further concerns about the security of its infrastructure.

COINBASE SECURES FEDERAL TRUST CHARTER APPROVAL FROM U.S. REGULATOR

Coinbase has received final approval from the US Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC) to establish Coinbase National Trust Company.

The approval allows the exchange to expand its digital-asset custody operations under a federal regulatory framework.

The development represents another step towards integrating crypto-native companies into established financial regulatory structures, particularly in institutional asset custody.

XRP LEDGER DEVELOPS QUANTUM-RESISTANT ACCOUNTS AHEAD OF 2028 SECURITY TARGET

The XRP Ledger Foundation has outlined a proposed approach to protect user accounts against future quantum-computing threats.

The design would allow account holders to add a quantum-resistant signing key and disable their existing cryptographic keys.

The proposed system uses the ML-DSA-44 signature standard, designed to withstand attacks from sufficiently powerful quantum computers.

The Foundation is targeting a broader transition by 2028, although development, testing and security audits remain outstanding.

PAXOS SAYS CORPORATE TREASURY TEAMS ARE DRIVING STABLECOIN ADOPTION

Stablecoin adoption is increasingly moving beyond cryptocurrency trading as corporate treasury departments explore faster and more efficient payment infrastructure.

Speaking during Singapore FinTech Festival 2026, Paxos Asia-Pacific head Khairi Azmi said businesses are increasingly considering stablecoins for managing cash flows and cross-border payments.

Industry data cited in the report puts business-to-business stablecoin payments at approximately $226 billion in 2025, representing a 733% increase from 2024.

The shift highlights the growing role of stablecoins in institutional financial operations.

STORM CHARLES FORCES WEB SUMMIT TO CANCEL ITS SECOND DAY IN LISBON

Web Summit 2026 has cancelled its Wednesday programme following an official recommendation from the Portuguese government over severe weather warnings associated with Storm Charles.

The decision was taken amid concerns about coastal flooding, strong winds and disruptions to public transportation.

Organisers say they intend to resume the conference on Thursday, November 12, subject to updated safety assessments.

The disruption marks an unusual interruption to one of the world's major technology gatherings.

AFRICA FOREX TRADING EXPO OPENS IN LAGOS, SPOTLIGHTING DIGITAL FINANCE

The second edition of Africa Forex Trading Expo opens today at Balmoral Convention Centre, Victoria Island, Lagos.

Running from November 11–12, the gathering brings together financial-market participants, fintech companies, traders, investors and technology professionals.

Its programme explores digital assets, blockchain, artificial intelligence in finance, payment infrastructure, financial regulation and cross-border opportunities across Africa.

The event provides another platform for conversations around the continent's evolving digital financial ecosystem.

CURRENTBLOCK WATCH

Today's developments reinforce the importance of stronger security, responsible innovation and the growing integration of blockchain into traditional finance.

From cross-chain vulnerabilities to institutional stablecoin adoption, the industry continues to evolve while confronting new challenges.

High Chief Government Ekpemupolo, popularly known as Tompolo and Grand Patron of the PBAT Door-to-Door Movement, has donated 25 campaign vehicles to support President Bola Ahmed Tinubu’s re-election bid in Cross River State ahead of the 2027 general elections.

The vehicles, along with other campaign materials, were distributed on Monday during the inauguration of the movement’s state structure in Calabar. 

The donation forms part of a larger deployment of 50 vehicles, 25 each to Cross River and Enugu States, aimed at strengthening grassroots mobilisation.

Represented by Chief Kestin Ebimorbowei Pondi, Managing Director of Tantita Security Services, Tompolo said the movement would complement the efforts of the All Progressives Congress (APC) by taking the administration’s policies and achievements directly to markets, motor parks, places of worship, polling units and communities across the state.

He said the logistics support from the PBAT Door-to-Door Movement had raised the state’s projected contribution from one million to 1.5 million votes, enabling deeper outreach into communities.

Governor Otu attributed the state’s strong support to developments recorded under the Tinubu administration, including the Lagos-Calabar Coastal Highway, increased federal allocations that have aided infrastructure projects and regular salary payments, and other interventions.

Cross River currently has approximately 1.93 million registered voters, according to Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) figures. 

The National Coordinator of the PBAT Door-to-Door Movement, Comrade Sunday Adekanbi Asuku, also urged Nigerians to back the President, citing initiatives such as the student loan scheme, local government financial autonomy and the establishment of the South-East Development Commission.

UD breaks ground on Biden Hall

Article by Amy Wolf | Photos by Evan Krape | November 09, 2026*

**New home for UD’s Biden School will advance public policy, civil discourse and community engagement**

The University of Delaware broke ground on Nov. 9 on Biden Hall, the future home of the Joseph R. Biden, Jr. School of Public Policy and Administration. The new building will provide space to prepare future leaders, advance research and foster civil discourse.

Named for former President Joe Biden, a UD alumnus, the approximately 30,000-square-foot facility will be located on the South Green between Morris Library and Robinson Hall. As the final planned building on UD’s iconic Green, Biden Hall will mark a significant milestone in the evolution of the University’s historic campus. The building is slated to open in fall 2029.

“In a time when civil discourse feels fragile, when the belief that people can talk to each other across differences feels, some days, like an act of faith, Biden Hall will be a place where students, faculty, researchers and the community will come together to do that work,” UD President Laura Carlson said.

Shovels in hand, UD breaks ground on the new Biden Hall, which is expected to open in fall 2029. Pictured from left to right: Gov. Matt Meyer, UD President Laura Carlson, Valerie Biden Owens, Jill Biden, former President Joe Biden, Biden School Dean Joseph Trainor, U.S. Senator Chris Coons and president of the Biden School Student Association Joe Oleksak.

At UD, Biden developed an understanding of how political engagement can drive meaningful change and empower individuals to help address challenges in their communities and the world.

“It’s the job of this University to help students make sense of the world around them — to prepare students as it prepared me to get engaged,” Biden said. “Biden Hall will be a place for students to answer for themselves and for this country: *Who are we? What do we stand for? What do we believe?* And maybe more importantly: *Who are we going to be?*”

A rendering of Biden Hall.

Biden Hall will serve as an interdisciplinary hub for the social sciences, bringing together scholars, practitioners, students and community partners to advance teaching, research and public engagement.

“Faculty, staff and students come to the Biden School because they believe government can work, that public policy can change lives and that public service is a noble profession,” said Joseph Trainor, dean of the Biden School. “There is no better name to affix to a building dedicated to that belief than Joseph R. Biden, Jr., a son of Delaware and a man who has devoted his entire life to bipartisan public service with integrity and an unshakable faith in the American people.”

At UD, Biden developed an understanding of how political engagement can drive meaningful change and empower individuals to help address challenges in their communities and the world.

The project is supported through philanthropy and state funding, reflecting a shared investment in the future of public service education at UD.

“Biden Hall is a testament to President Biden’s unwavering commitment to the people of Delaware,” said Gov. Matt Meyer. “As the new home of the University of Delaware’s Biden School, Biden Hall will help prepare our next generation of leaders to serve our nation with conviction and integrity."

### Preparing future leaders

Inside Biden Hall, students will have opportunities to apply classroom learning through policy labs, internships, research projects, leadership programs and community partnerships. Graduates will be prepared for careers in public service and leadership positions across government, nonprofit organizations, healthcare, education and the private sector.

text:
PROMPT
Build an impressive, fully playable 3D pixel American football game called FOURTH & GOAL.

Deliver one self-contained HTML file with its CSS, JavaScript, Three.js runtime, textures and sounds embedded. The final file must open locally without a server or network access. Use procedural code for every visual asset. No imported models, photographs, prerecorded footage or paid assets. The result should feel like a small collectible stadium brought to life, with a real match unfolding inside it.

ART DIRECTION
Create a detailed voxel stadium at dusk. Use a warm, slightly nostalgic sports broadcast aesthetic: deep forest green panels, ivory type, burnt orange and muted teal accents. The fictional teams are REDWOOD in orange and COASTAL in teal. Use pixelated rendering with deliberately limited internal resolution, crisp block geometry, warm directional lighting, ambient fill, readable shadows and gentle atmospheric fog. Keep the game sharp enough to see the players and ball. Avoid bloom that washes out the field.

The stadium should include striped green turf, correct American football yard markings, hash marks, yard numbers, colored end zones, a midfield emblem, yellow goalposts, orange pylons, stepped grandstands, thousands of individually colored block spectators, aisles, railings, stadium advertising, team benches, substitute players, referees, equipment boxes, floodlight towers, a press box and a large world-space scoreboard. Surround the stadium with a simple grounded miniature environment. Everything must feel intentionally placed and physically connected.

PLAYERS AND BALL
There must be exactly eleven active players per team. Give each player an articulated block character rig with a helmet, helmet stripe, face opening, facemask, shoulder pads, contrasting jersey, visible number, gloves, pants and cleats. Animate running through joint rotations, not by sliding a static mesh. Add poses for setting at the line, blocking, throwing, catching, carrying, juking, getting tackled and celebrating. Keep the characters readable from the stadium camera and convincing in the close chase view.

Use an actual three-dimensional brown football with a pointed oval silhouette and light laces. Snaps and passes must visibly move through space. A forward pass follows a high arc toward a moving receiver. The football stays with its carrier after a catch or handoff. Do not replace gameplay with a looping scripted animation.

GAME RULES
Implement a compact arcade match with clear, internally consistent rules. Each possession normally starts at its own twenty-yard line. Four downs are available to gain ten yards. Reaching the line to gain resets the down count. Four unsuccessful downs turn the ball over where the play ends. A touchdown scores seven points, including an automatic extra point. A safety scores two. The first team to at least twenty-one wins, with a visible result and a working new-match button. Kicks, penalties and complex NFL special cases are outside this arcade game's scope; explain that briefly in the help dialog.

Stop plays on tackles, sacks, an incomplete pass, stepping out of bounds, a touchdown or a safety. Players must stay in sensible formations between plays. Restore the line of scrimmage after an incomplete pass. Show the line of scrimmage and the first-down target on the field. Update the screen scoreboard and the physical stadium scoreboard from the same game state.

AI AND PLAYBOOK
The offense has a quarterback, five offensive linemen, a running back and four eligible receiving targets. The defense has rushers, linebackers, cornerbacks and a safety. Blockers engage defenders near the line and form a temporary pocket; defenders must eventually get through. Receivers run purposeful routes. Defenders cover routes, pursue the ball and tackle on real proximity. Allow defenders to intercept a pass and return it in the opposite direction. Pass accuracy should respond to pressure and target movement. Both completed and incomplete passes must be possible during normal autoplay.

Provide three selectable plays before the snap: Cross for short crossing routes, Verticals for deep routes, and Power Run for a handoff. Autoplay should run both sides immediately on page load. It chooses plays, snaps the ball, selects a receiver and continues each possession. Switching autoplay off gives the user control of the current offense. The player can move the ball carrier, choose a receiver to pass to and juke a defender. In manual mode, a carrier should wait when no movement key is held. Keep a short juke cooldown and make its effect visible.

CONTROLS
Space snaps the ball before the play and jukes while carrying it. WASD or arrow keys move the ball carrier. Keys 1 through 4 throw to numbered receivers, with matching clickable buttons and markers above the players. R toggles the last-play replay, C cycles cameras, and H hides or restores the interface. Include visible buttons for every important action, a help dialog, optional stadium sound and fullscreen. Touch layouts need usable movement controls and compact play/receiver buttons. Disabled buttons should accurately reflect which actions are currently possible.

CAMERAS AND REPLAY
Provide Stadium, TV and Chase cameras. Stadium presents the miniature arena; TV follows the action from an elevated sideline angle; Chase smoothly follows behind the ball carrier. Allow pointer dragging to orbit and the scroll wheel to zoom. Follow movement smoothly without sudden camera flips.

Record snapshots of the live players and ball. After a play, Replay should show that actual recorded play at half speed. Freeze the live match while replay runs, interpolate recorded transforms, clearly label the replay and return to the same live match state afterward. Do not simulate a different play and call it a replay.

PRESENTATION
Use a small branded masthead, a centered broadcast scoreboard, compact bottom playbook, receiver buttons and camera controls. Show possession, score, down, distance and field position. Event graphics should announce first downs, incomplete passes, interceptions, touchdowns and the final winner. Add small turf particles for tackles and restrained team-colored confetti for a touchdown. The interface must remain usable at desktop and phone sizes, with a clean way to hide it for recording.

Synthesize quiet crowd ambience, a whistle and simple game cues using Web Audio. Sound must start only after user interaction and have a reliable mute toggle. Do not autoplay sound without consent.

ENGINEERING AND VERIFICATION
Separate deterministic match simulation from rendering. Use delta time, bounded movement and finite coordinates. Batch static geometry and spectators to keep draw calls manageable, and reuse player rigs. Keep all gameplay real and interactive. Test a full automatic match, manual movement and passing, the running handoff, four-down turnovers, first downs, touchdowns, interceptions, safeties, replay pause/resume, camera switching, hiding/restoring the HUD, audio controls and a narrow mobile layout. Inspect the actual rendered scene and fix runtime errors or obvious visual defects before delivering the final HTML.

Commenting on the Bank's participation, Dele Faseemo, Group Executive, Corporate and Investment Banking at Sterling Bank, said:
 
“Climate change is already changing the way our cities function and how communities earn a living. Lagos has identified significant opportunities to invest in infrastructure that will support its long-term growth, while the situation in Aiyetoro shows what happens when vulnerable communities are unable to protect themselves against environmental threats. These are different challenges, but both require financing, credible projects and sustained collaboration. Our focus at COP31 is to work with the states and development partners to identify practical financing arrangements that can support implementation. The measure of progress will be what we are able to deliver beyond the conference.”
 
Sterling Bank’s participation builds on its HEART strategy, which prioritises investment in Health, Education, Agriculture, Renewable Energy and Transportation. Through the strategy, the Bank continues to support sectors central to Nigeria's economic development and climate transition, including clean energy adoption, sustainable agriculture and low-emission mobility.
 
This commitment was recently reinforced through a US$30 million senior credit facility signed with Proparco, the private-sector subsidiary of the Agence Française de Développement (AFD) Group, to expand financing for renewable energy projects and small and medium-sized enterprises across Nigeria's agricultural value chain. The arrangement reflects Sterling’s efforts to work with development finance partners to increase access to capital in sectors where financing can support both economic growth and environmental sustainability.
 
Beyond COP31, the Bank's engagement with OSOPADEC is expected to support continued dialogue on the Ilaje coastal-resilience agenda, including preparations for an international conference proposed for March 2027. The conference is intended to build on discussions in Antalya and advance potential partnerships and financing commitments for coastal interventions.

text:
Coromandel International Ltd Concall Summary (Q2 FY27, 12 November 2026) #COROMANDEL

🟡 Management Guidance: 
Management expects H2 FY27 to be significantly better than H1, supported by revised Rabi NBS subsidy rates, moderation in raw material prices, improved farm economics and a recovery in fertilizer consumption. The company expects fertilizer production, sales and consumption to improve during Rabi. Management indicated that NPK prices could see a 10% to 15% moderation in certain grades such as 20:20, depending on the final subsidy notification and the scope for MRP correction. The newly commissioned phosphoric acid and sulfuric acid plant at Kakinada is back to full-capacity operations, with backward integration spreads expected to improve in H2. Management considers a $300 to $350 spread a reasonable assumption. The new granulation facility is expected to be commissioned by February, with the target of operating close to full capacity next year. The retail network is targeted to increase from 1,300 stores to 2,000 over the next two years. Management expects the retail white-label brand to cross ₹100 crore in annual sales this year. One key crop protection molecule's expanded capacity is expected to come on stream by the end of November. The fluorination launch plant will be used to qualify products with customers before committing ₹200 crore to ₹300 crore towards a commercial facility, potentially 1 to 2 years later. Management expects to provide a further update on the Daksha defence order next quarter.

🟢 Green Alert: Consolidated Q2 revenue increased 6% YoY to ₹10,348 crore, while EBITDA declined 18% to ₹944 crore and PAT fell to ₹523 crore from ₹793 crore. H1 revenue grew 10% to ₹18,563 crore, but EBITDA declined 12% to ₹1,705 crore and PAT fell to ₹905 crore from ₹1,295 crore. The Kakinada phosphoric acid and sulfuric acid plant has resumed full-capacity operations following the sulfur subsidy announcement, improving the company's backward integration economics. Management expects the value gap from backward integration to benefit H2 performance. Crop protection revenue grew 22% in Q2, supported by exports, while Coromandel's standalone crop protection export revenue grew 44% and exports contributed more than 40% of segment revenue. New products contributed 36% of crop protection business during the year. Retail added 80 stores during Q2, taking the network to 1,300, with several recently opened stores reaching breakeven faster than expected. Specialty nutrients, organic fertilizers and biological products performed well, supported by increased farmer adoption and demand for differentiated products. The company launched 10 new products across nutrients and crop protection. The revised Rabi NBS rates and special sulfur subsidy have received cabinet approval. Subsidy collections were ₹4,478 crore during H1, and the company received another approximately ₹1,200 crore in October. Management also indicated that channel inventory is not significantly elevated, with industry inventory estimated at only 5% to 7% above last year's level.

🔴 Red Alert: Q2 was severely affected by deficient rainfall of around 20% to 30% across key markets, rupee depreciation, elevated raw material prices, weak agricultural consumption and unfavorable subsidy rates. Industry NPK production and consumption declined approximately 40% during the quarter. Coromandel's fertilizer primary sales declined 30% to 10 lakh tonnes, while production fell 15% to 7.7 lakh tonnes as management deliberately moderated supplies to protect working capital. H1 industry NPK sales declined to 60 lakh tonnes from 77 lakh tonnes, while DAP remained flat at 44 lakh tonnes. The widening price gap between DAP and NPK fertilizers caused farmers to shift towards DAP, hurting domestic complex fertilizer manufacturers. Consolidated EBITDA and PAT declined despite revenue growth, highlighting the impact of margin compression. NACL reported Q2 revenue of ₹374 crore, down 18%, and EBITDA of just ₹12 crore, due to high-cost inventory that could not be passed on to customers amid falling market prices. Management expects a recovery but acknowledged that crop protection portfolio improvements and new product registrations will take time, potentially 2 to 3 years. Restrictions on the sale of non-subsidy fertilizers in Uttar Pradesh, Bihar and Maharashtra have also affected business. The government's pilot fertilizer sales framework applies to all fertilizers and could restrict farmers' ability to purchase the required NPK quantities if implementation issues are not resolved. Battery-grade phosphoric acid development has been delayed for 2 to 3 quarters because management is prioritising the core fertilizer business. The proposed fluorination commercial plant requires customer validation and signed commitments before investment. The Daksha defence drone business is still awaiting progress on its earlier defence order, and no confirmed order timeline was provided.

🔵 Blue Alert: Coromandel is gradually diversifying beyond conventional subsidized fertilizers into crop protection, specialty nutrients, biologicals, retail, nano fertilizers, specialty chemicals and drones. Its retail network is becoming an important distribution advantage, allowing the company to sell organic fertilizers, water-soluble nutrients, biologicals and proprietary products directly to farmers. Management believes biologicals can deliver sustainable growth through neem-based biopesticides, microbials, plant extracts and organic fertilizers. These products have relatively strong entry barriers due to proprietary research, product registrations, branding and farmer engagement, although scaling volumes requires time. Specialty nutrients have historically delivered 20% to 25% volume growth, according to management, and the company is working to reduce dependence on imported Chinese raw materials through captive sourcing. In crop protection, Coromandel is leveraging NACL's spare manufacturing capacity, R&D capabilities and product portfolio to develop new-age chemistries and pursue CDMO opportunities. The proposed fluorination business could use hydrofluoroacetic acid generated from its phosphoric acid operations, providing a potential raw material advantage over competitors using the phosphor route. Management wants customer commitments before investing in this business. The company is also expanding its presence in nano DAP, with exports beginning and registrations being pursued in Latin America, the Middle East and Southeast Asia. Daksha is developing agricultural and defence drones, with two new agricultural drone variants introduced and demonstrations conducted for the Army in the Kargil region. The company has a 1,30,000 sq. ft. drone facility and is developing an indigenous vendor ecosystem.

🧠 Deep Insight: Coromandel's Q2 performance reflects a combination of industry-wide demand weakness and unfavorable fertilizer economics rather than simply a company-specific operational problem. The most important near-term variable is whether the revised NBS subsidy rates translate into lower NPK prices, improved farmer affordability and a recovery in consumption during Rabi. The company's deliberate reduction in production and primary sales has helped contain inventory and working capital risk, while the Kakinada backward integration facility provides an opportunity to improve margins as production scales up. However, the recovery should not be judged only by improved subsidy economics. Actual fertilizer volumes, NPK market share and the company's ability to maintain profitability after MRP corrections will be critical. Beyond fertilizers, retail, biologicals, specialty nutrients and crop protection exports are developing into meaningful diversification opportunities. NACL remains a weak point in the near term, although its manufacturing capacity and R&D capabilities could create longer-term synergies. The fluorination project is promising but remains at the customer-validation stage, while defence drones are still awaiting order conversion. The central investment thesis is that Coromandel is combining its established fertilizer and backward integration business with a growing retail-led specialty agriculture and crop protection platform. A recovery in fertilizer consumption could improve near-term earnings, while biologicals, specialty nutrients, exports and new chemistries offer longer-term growth opportunities. Key monitorables are Rabi fertilizer volumes, NPK market share, EBITDA per tonne, backward integration spreads, Kakinada utilisation, granulation plant commissioning, NACL margin recovery, retail store profitability, crop protection exports and customer commitments for the fluorination project.

My Adventures with Superman on the brink, DC Comics’ new boss, Nexon’s emergency mode and more | The Reef Daily

Superman in My Adventures with Superman. Image: Adult Swim

My Adventures with Superman could be the next DC show to go, and the newest Clownfish TV episode explains why the hosts think it’s done now that Peter Safran is out at DC Studios. The other new episodes cover what the DC shake-up could mean for DC Comics, the money trouble at ARC Raiders’ parent company Nexon and the threats aimed at the new Snape in HBO’s Harry Potter series. Below that, D/REZZED has a record Zelda launch in the UK, Godzilla’s big weekend and more, plus a few Shorts and the newest podcast episodes.

New Clownfish TV episodes

Is My Adventures with Superman canceled?

Not officially, but the hosts would bet on it. About a week ago, Safran told Collider the show’s future was “up in the air” and said its team is now making My Adventures with Green Lantern for DC. Now Safran and James Gunn are both out at DC Studios, and the hosts expect the new regime to wind down the projects the pair championed. They put Lars of the Stars, the Steven Universe spinoff still in the works for Amazon, on the same list.

Then there’s the money. The Cartoon Brew story the hosts read says Skydance is carrying $87 billion in debt after buying Warner Bros. Discovery and wants to save at least $6 billion a year within three years, with AI doing a lot of the work. The cuts include $2.2 billion from corporate operations and $1 billion from marketing. The hosts think animation will get made cheaper from here, and they see one odd upside: cheaper shows might mean a show like this one gets a shot it wouldn’t have gotten otherwise.

Will James Gunn’s exit change DC’s comic books?

The hosts think so, even if nothing has happened yet. Bleeding Cool’s Rich Johnston reports that nobody at DC Comics has been handed a voluntary layoff package, even as thousands of other Warner Bros. and Skydance workers were, and he suggests Absolute Batman’s sales helped keep the publisher safe. Johnston also reports that DC publisher Jim Lee felt frozen out by Gunn and Safran and welcomed the news that former Marvel executive Jeremy Latcham is taking over DC Studios.

Not everyone is happy about it. Comics journalist Heidi MacDonald wrote that the “Tom King Hollywood era” is coming to an end, and the hosts read a stack of upset reactions from comics fans and creators on Bluesky. Their prediction: Latcham, who they say wants superhero stories that play in middle America, will bring mandates with him, and DC Comics will feel them too.

Is ARC Raiders’ parent company in trouble?

By its own numbers, yes. Nexon, which owns ARC Raiders studio Embark, is in what a widely shared post on X called emergency mode: a restructure, a hiring freeze and more than 300 workers with no assigned project, some of them offered voluntary resignation. Nexon also confirmed it canceled six game projects.

That’s happening even though ARC Raiders has sold more than 17 million copies since it launched in October 2025, according to the Insider Gaming story the hosts read. Sales have slowed, though: it was at 16 million in May, and Nexon expects revenue to drop from last year. The hosts compare that with Marvel’s Wolverine at 2.4 million and call it proof that no studio is safe in what they’re calling video game crash 2.0.

Why is Harry Potter’s new Snape getting threats?

Paapa Essiedu says some of it is racism, and the hosts think plenty of it is about J.K. Rowling. Essiedu told the Sunday Times in March that he’d been told, “Quit or I’ll murder you.” Now HBO’s showrunner, Francesca Gardiner, has told Variety that “it’s appalling that anyone should be subjected to that kind of abuse.” Essiedu, who signed an open letter supporting trans rights earlier this year, told Vanity Fair he’s “not really here to speak about Jo’s politics or to be a mouthpiece for her.”

The hosts point to Bluesky, where searching his name turns up post after post attacking him for taking Rowling’s money. They expect the media to blame racist fans alone. The series premieres on Christmas Day, and the hosts say Alan Rickman left some big shoes to fill.

text:
Every year, on the National Day of the People's Republic of China, a giant portrait of Sun Yat-sen is displayed in Beijing's Tiananmen Square in his honor. Across the Taiwan Strait, he is also revered as the "Father of the Nation." His portraits hang in the governor's office in Taipei, and his image still appears on Taiwan's currency today.

Today marks the 160th anniversary of his birth. At a grand commemorative ceremony held in the Great Hall of the People in Beijing, Chinese President Xi said:
"The Chinese Communists are the staunchest supporters, the most loyal collaborators, and the most faithful successors of Dr. Sun Yat-sen's revolutionary cause."

Xi has made similar statements before, but these words still resonate powerfully with me today.

Who was Sun Yat-sen, and why does Xi speak of him in such terms? Why is he held in such high esteem on both sides of the Taiwan Strait? Who inherited Sun's political ideals? And who accomplished the historic mission that he himself was unable to complete?

Sun Yat-sen was born in Guangdong Province in southern China. The city where his native village is located has since been renamed in his honor.

At the age of 13, when Japan took over China's tributary state Ryukyus and transformed it into the Prefecture of Okinawa, with the help of his elder brother, Sun traveled to Hawaii, where he received his secondary education. Yes, he attended the very same school that Barack Obama would attend nearly a century later: Punahou School.

Sun went on to become one of the earliest students at the predecessor of the University of Hong Kong's medical school. He excelled academically and went on to practice medicine.

Had he continued down that path, he might well have become a highly respected doctor.

But Sun was confronted with more than just patients in need of treatment. He was also confronted with a nation in deep crisis.

In the 19th century, China was growing increasingly weak, suffering repeated aggression at the hands of western foreign powers, forced to cede territory and pay enormous indemnities.

Eventually, even Japan, which had once shared China's predicament, transformed itself into a rising power through sweeping reforms and began to turn its ambitions against China.

In 1879, Japan annexed the Ryukyu. Li Hongzhang (李鸿章), one of China's most powerful officials, offered little effective resistance.

By 1894, Japan had grown even more aggressive. It launched a surprise attack on China's naval forces, and as Li hesitated to commit his fleet to battle, Japan destroyed the whole fleet.

China was then forced to pay Japan a staggering 230 million taels of silver (abt 13 billion USD), and cede Taiwan.

That same year, Sun Yat-sen wrote to Li Hongzhang, proposing concrete measures to modernize China and enhance its national strength. But his proposals were ignored by the powerful, complacent and corrupted politician.

From that point on, Sun abandoned his hopes of reforming the Chinese empire from within. Instead, he devoted himself to overthrowing it and establishing a republic.

Later that year, in Hawaii, he founded the precursor to the Kuomintang.

After a series of failed revolutionary uprisings, the revolution finally triumphed in 1911.

The following year, China's last emperor abdicated, bringing more than two thousand years of imperial rule to an end. The Republic of China, Asia's earliest modern republic, was born.

Building a strong, modern nation was quite another. Sun and his fellow revolutionaries commanded only limited military forces. When the revolution erupted, much of northern China remained under the imperial control. Li Hongzhang was already died, while the dynasty's most powerful modern army was commanded by a deceitful minister named Yuan Shikai (袁世凯).

The revolutionaries had little assurance of victory if they attempted to unify the country by force. Eventually, the two sides reached a compromise: Yuan would secure the emperor's abdication, while Sun would step down as provisional president and allow Yuan to succeed him.

Yet the compromise brought China neither genuine democracy nor lasting unity.

Yuan was authoritarian, even audaciously restored the monarchy and crowned himself emperor in 1915.

After his death in 1916, China descended to endless fighting between warlords.

Time and again, Sun Yat-sen tried to organize military campaigns against Yuan and other warlords, but his efforts were repeatedly frustrated by his lack of military strength.

He also looked abroad for help. Sun once spent years living and studying in the United States, so he turned to Washington for support, even writing to the US president. I reviewed that original letter at Hoover a decade ago-both the White House and State Department refused to even acknowledge it. The letter was simply bluntly returned on the day of its arrival. 

The turning point came from an unexpected direction: the Soviet Union. It offered Sun financial, military and organizational assistance. It helped reorganize Sun's Kuomintang (KMT) into a more disciplined and effective political party and supported the establishment of the Whampoa Military Academy (黄埔军校), which trained a new generation of brilliant modern military officers loyal to the revolutionary cause.

As part of this cooperation, Sun paved the way for the united front between CPC and KMT. In January 1924, the Kuomintang held its First National Congress in Guangzhou (广州), formally establishing this new alliance. 

The alliance fueled the rapid growth of the CPC. When the CPC was founded in 1921, it had just over 50 members. By 1925, that number had grown to around 1,000. By 1927, it had surged to nearly 60,000.

In 1925, Sun Yat-sen died of illness in Beijing. He never lived to witness the military breakthrough his revolutionary movement was about to achieve. After a lengthy process, I was granted access to the bedroom where he spent his final days, a room not open to the general public, and almost none of my mentors has ever entered.

In 1926, the KMT and CPC jointly launched the Northern Expedition from southern China. Unlike Sun's earlier military campaigns, this time the revolutionary army swept through the country, winning one victory after another.

But then came a dramatic betrayal. Chiang Kai-shek (蒋介石), who portrayed himself as a disciple of Sun Yat-sen, suddenly launched a coup in 1927, purging and massacring Communist Party members and consolidating his control over the Kuomintang.

Chiang's actions drew condemnation from many, including Sun Yat-sen's widow, Soong Ching-ling (宋庆龄). Indeed, when the Communist Party defeated the Kuomintang on the Chinese mainland in 1949, Chiang fled to Taiwan with the remnants of his forces, taking with him some of the finest treasures of the Forbidden City and vast quantities of gold plundered by his regime.

Soong Ching-ling, however, chose to remain on the mainland. She went on to hold senior positions in the People's Republic of China, including that of vice president of the country.

By this point, you may already have formed your own judgment as to which party, the Communist Party or the Kuomintang, has the stronger claim to Sun Yat-sen's political legacy.

Xi's characterization of the Communist Party's relationship with Sun Yat-sen carries three layers of meaning:

1. The staunchest supporters: A shared revolutionary vision

Sun Yat-sen devoted his life to overthrowing imperial rule, resisting foreign oppression, securing national independence, and building a strong and prosperous China.

From its founding, the CPC embraced the struggle against imperialism and feudalism, national independence, and the liberation of the Chinese people as its historic mission. 

2. The most loyal collaborators: A shared revolutionary history

This characterization refers to the First United Front between the Kuomintang and the Communist Party, established in 1924.

Communists participated in the reorganization of the Kuomintang, helped establish the Whampoa, and played an important role in the subsequent Northern Expedition. The collaboration not only transformed the Kuomintang but also profoundly reshaped the course of the Chinese revolution.

Revisiting this history today serves not only to highlight the historical ties between Sun Yat-sen and the CPC, but also to remind us of something often forgotten: the two parties once shared a revolutionary cause, and through cooperation, they once changed the course of China's history.

3. The most faithful successors: Who fulfilled Sun Yat-sen's dream?

Of the three characterizations, this one carries the most profound political implications.

Sun's lifelong ambition was not merely to overthrow a dynasty and establish a republic. It was to lift China out of poverty, weakness, and division, free it from foreign domination, and transform it into an independent, united, prosperous, and powerful modern nation.

Sun Yat-sen died in 1925. China at the time was fragmented by warlords, bullied by foreign powers, and mired in poverty and weakness. The fate of the nation was still largely in the hands of others.

A century later, China has become the world's second-largest economy, possessing industrial, technological, and military capabilities that Sun could scarcely have imagined.

The CPC is making his vision happen.

He lost uprising after uprising.
Li Hongzhang would not read him.
Washington would not even open his letter.
Yuan Shikai betrayed him.
His own disciple betrayed him.

He died in Beijing in 1925 holding a map of a country that was not whole.

160 years after his birth, the China he dreamed of is almost a reality. 

Almost.

The same politicians and party leaders who have had the power to repeal these laws have repeatedly failed to do so. The Tennessee Firearms Association believes 2027 must be a year of results—not more promises, political excuses, or appeasement.

TFA has identified ten major legislative priorities for 2027, along with a renewed commitment to identifying opportunities for constitutional litigation, including federal civil-rights claims, when government refuses to respect constitutional limits. Our founding generation did not preserve liberty by surrendering to government authority or seeking favors from politicians. They confronted abuses of power with courage and determination. Read TFA's full agenda, examine the proposed reforms, and learn why elected officials must be held accountable for their actions—not their campaign promises or party affiliations.

GHK-Cu is one of the five peptides heading to an FDA advisory panel before February 2027. It is not on the current HHS enforcement-discretion list.

The HHS policy comment window closes Friday. The same week, the AMA called for the policy to be immediately rescinded and committed to pursuing enforcement at the state level.

This is what "access expanding faster than evidence" looks like in practice.

text:
Injustice is always painful. Sometimes life is unjust, & all we can do is control our response.

I hurt for this football team, & especially the seniors. Genuinely might be my favorite group of players I’ve ever coached. Selfless, hard working, humble, & fully bought in every day. All of them.

A group where the most talented guys, also have the highest character. A group where football was about more than just winning games & earning scholarships.

This group of young men has  been “all in”, all the time. Winter off season, spring ball, summer workouts, fall camp, football season. They worked everyday with great attitudes, leadership, & grit. I’ve enjoyed coaching them as much as any team I’ve ever been a part of.

I think most of all, I’ve been blessed to coach a group that are genuinely good people. Faithful young men who love Jesus & love each other. Young men I hope my sons can be like one day.

They put so much time & effort into a goal, & had that ripped away before they could finish what they started.

It’s an unfair outcome, one that will sting for a long time.

If you’ve never been a part of Liberty Christian, it’s hard to understand how special of a place it is. I say to most families that tour:

“Many schools have Jesus on the billboard, but he’s at the heart of everything we do here”

I hate that from the outside looking in, these accusations look legitimate. They’re not.

And that the reputation of a place so fiercely devoted to putting faith first, is being soiled when so many places that blatantly bend & break rules don’t see consequences.

But that is the world we live in. I’m proud to be a part of Liberty Christian. I’m proud that my children attend there. I’m blessed that my wife works there. This place has transformed my faith, & blessed my family in so many ways.

So to my players who are devastated right now:

Trust the story. God works good through all things, & He will work good through this. Football isn’t about rings, it’s about giving young men the opportunity to learn the value of chasing a common goal through grit, toughness & selfless hard work. It’s about preparing you for life. You learned those lessons & can walk away with your head held high that God used your time this season to prepare you for much greater things.

To our Liberty community:

Don’t grow weary in doing good. Our sinful nature urges us to fight fire with fire, & throw stones at those who wronged us. Use this as an opportunity to show how differently Jesus responds to enemies. Be a light. 

To those outside who see this as a black mark on Liberty:

Don’t believe everything you read and hear. Bitter people do ugly things. As someone who has been ingrained in Liberty Christian School for almost 10 years, it’s a special place. The administration, coaches, & teachers are some of the most incredible, faith-filled people I have ever been around. It’s a school committed to putting Jesus first. It’s a school committed to doing things the right way. God has used this place to transform many lives, including mine. I have faith he will continue to do that for years to come.

I hate this for our players and our community. But I am thankful for the journey all the same.

“And we know that in all things God works for the good of those who love him, who have been called according to his purpose.”
Romans 8:28 NIV

text:
Happy Birthday, Marines!

ON THIS DAY — NOVEMBER 10, 1775

BEFORE THERE WAS AN INDEPENDENT AMERICA, THERE WERE UNITED STATES MARINES!

🇺🇸 HAPPY 251ST BIRTHDAY TO THE UNITED STATES MARINE CORPS!

251 YEARS AGO TODAY, THE CONTINENTAL MARINES WERE BORN IN THE FIRES OF THE AMERICAN REVOLUTION.

Think about that for a moment.

America had not yet declared independence.

The Declaration of Independence had not been signed.

George Washington had not yet won the Revolutionary War.

The Constitution did not exist.

But on November 10, 1775, the Second Continental Congress made a decision that would become one of the most enduring traditions in American military history.

CONGRESS AUTHORIZED TWO BATTALIONS OF MARINES.

Their mission was to support America’s developing naval forces and serve wherever the Revolutionary cause required them.

They would fight aboard ships.

They would conduct operations ashore.

They would help defend a cause whose ultimate outcome remained uncertain.

These were the Continental Marines.

And their story began before the United States officially became an independent nation.

In March 1776, Marines participated in an expedition to Nassau in the Bahamas, helping capture military supplies desperately needed by American forces.

It was an early demonstration of the expeditionary capabilities that would become a defining characteristic of the Marine Corps.

The Revolutionary War eventually ended.

The Continental Marines were disbanded.

But the need for a permanent naval infantry force remained.

In 1798, Congress formally established the United States Marine Corps.

The traditions that began in 1775 continued.

And across the centuries, those traditions would be tested on battlefields throughout the world.

From the Barbary Wars to Belleau Wood.

From Guadalcanal to Iwo Jima.

From the frozen mountains surrounding the Chosin Reservoir to the jungles of Vietnam.

From the deserts of the Middle East to the mountains of Afghanistan.

Generations of Marines answered their nation’s call.

Some returned home.

Others made the ultimate sacrifice.

And countless families carried the burden of service alongside them.

THE MARINE CORPS HAS NEVER BEEN DEFINED SOLELY BY THE BATTLES IT HAS FOUGHT.

It is also defined by the character expected of those who earn the title Marine.

HONOR.

The commitment to integrity, responsibility, and doing what is right.

COURAGE.

The willingness to confront danger, hardship, and uncertainty.

COMMITMENT.

The determination to fulfill the mission and remain faithful to fellow Marines and country.

These are not simply words on a recruiting poster.

They are the values upon which generations of Marines have built their lives.

And they are reflected in two Latin words known throughout the world:

SEMPER FIDELIS.

ALWAYS FAITHFUL.

Faithful to duty.

Faithful to fellow Marines.

Faithful to the Constitution.

Faithful to the nation they have sworn to defend.

Today, as America celebrates its 250th anniversary, there is something especially remarkable about the Marine Corps birthday.

THE UNITED STATES MARINE CORPS TRACES ITS FOUNDING TO A DATE ONE YEAR BEFORE AMERICAN INDEPENDENCE.

Its origins belong to the generation that fought to establish our republic.

The generation that risked everything for the possibility of self-government.

The generation that believed liberty was worth defending.

And 251 years later, that responsibility continues.
