$MUX Q3 2026 earnings: McEwen's gold output falls 23%, and snow delays copper plans

Simultaneous operating problems at all three of McEwen's gold and silver mines wiped out the benefit of higher metal prices. Output fell 23% from a year ago, pushing the miner to a $37 million net loss even though its average selling price climbed 19%. The company replaced leadership at its Nevada mine in August and said production and costs recovered in October, so it kept its full-year targets intact.

• Total metal production: 𝟐𝟐,𝟖𝟓𝟐 𝐆𝐄𝐎𝐬 (-23% from a year ago)
• Revenue (100%-owned mines): $𝟒𝟑.𝟔𝐌 (-14% from a year ago)
• 100%-owned all-in sustaining cost: $𝟑,𝟔𝟎𝟔 / 𝐨𝐳 (+37% from a year ago)
• Full-year production and cost outlook: 𝐔𝐧𝐜𝐡𝐚𝐧𝐠𝐞𝐝 (middle of the range: 114,500 GEOs)

⚖️ 𝐕𝐞𝐫𝐝𝐢𝐜𝐭: 🔴 Bearish

The story got worse because mine setbacks drained cash and winter weather delayed the Los Azules copper project. Record Andes snowfall blocked the site road and pushed the copper project's final investment decision back six months to mid-2027, while by our math the unchanged 2026 cost targets at Fox and San José now require impossible fourth-quarter cost drops. On the positive side, $58 million in Argentine dividends and a $55 million property sale in Ontario rebuilt the cash cushion after quarter-end.

The question now is whether October's rebound at the Nevada and Ontario mines is the start of a steady recovery or just a brief bounce. If the new pit procedures hold, cash flow will recover to fund the 2027 mine builds; if grades slip again, McEwen will have to sell its Discovery Mining stock or raise capital. Fourth-quarter production and unit costs will tell.

Full article with charts - link in bio

🐂 𝐁𝐮𝐥𝐥 𝐂𝐚𝐬𝐞

🟢🟢 𝐀𝐬𝐬𝐞𝐭 𝐒𝐚𝐥𝐞𝐬 𝐚𝐧𝐝 𝐀𝐫𝐠𝐞𝐧𝐭𝐢𝐧𝐞 𝐃𝐢𝐯𝐢𝐝𝐞𝐧𝐝𝐬 𝐑𝐞𝐛𝐮𝐢𝐥𝐝 𝐂𝐚𝐬𝐡
McEwen is a gold and silver producer that wants to fund its mine builds without selling new stock. Its 49%-owned San José mine in Argentina has paid $58.3 million in cash dividends so far this year, beating the company's $40 million to $50 million full-year forecast.

The miner also raised cash by selling assets outside its main operations. In August, it sold a loan receivable from its McEwen Copper subsidiary for $13.6 million in cash. In October, it sold two unused properties in Timmins, Ontario to Discovery Mining for $5 million in cash and $50 million in Discovery Mining stock.

These inflows matter because operations burned cash in the third quarter, pulling cash and marketable securities down by $32.2 million to $59.5 million. The extra dividends and the $55 million Timmins sale give the group a fresh cushion to pay for its Canadian and Mexican mine construction.

What to watch: fourth-quarter cash and marketable securities, plus any timeline to sell the $50 million Discovery Mining stock. Converting those shares into cash would cover next year's construction budget without borrowing.

🟢 𝐎𝐜𝐭𝐨𝐛𝐞𝐫 𝐎𝐮𝐭𝐩𝐮𝐭 𝐑𝐞𝐛𝐨𝐮𝐧𝐝𝐬 𝐀𝐟𝐭𝐞𝐫 𝐍𝐞𝐯𝐚𝐝𝐚 𝐋𝐞𝐚𝐝𝐞𝐫𝐬𝐡𝐢𝐩 𝐂𝐡𝐚𝐧𝐠𝐞
Production at the Gold Bar mine in Nevada fell 24% from a year ago to 6,215 gold equivalent ounces (GEOs, which combine gold and silver into one measure). McEwen blamed "poor management oversight" and decided to "make changes to its leadership team in late August" while adding pit drilling and grade checks.

Because Gold Bar uses heap leaching — where rock sits on a pad for 45 to 60 days while solution dissolves the gold — the fixes only showed up in October. Daily output reached 108 ounces in October, up from 68 in the third quarter, while all-in sustaining costs (AISC, a measure of total mine operating and upkeep costs) dropped to $2,873 per ounce from $3,520.

One good month does not settle the concern, because Gold Bar has missed plans before, and by our math the mine still needs 11,559 ounces in the fourth quarter to hit the middle of its annual target. Still, October's pace of 3,353 ounces puts that fourth-quarter goal within reach if the pit holds its grade.

What to watch: full fourth-quarter production and unit costs at Gold Bar when annual results arrive. Hitting 10,000 ounces or more for the quarter would show the new pit procedures work beyond a single month.

🟢 𝐒𝐭𝐨𝐜𝐤 𝐌𝐢𝐧𝐞 𝐚𝐧𝐝 𝐄𝐥 𝐆𝐚𝐥𝐥𝐨 𝐀𝐝𝐯𝐚𝐧𝐜𝐞 𝐓𝐨𝐰𝐚𝐫𝐝 𝟐𝟎𝟐𝟕
McEwen plans to lift total output to between 250,000 and 300,000 GEOs a year by 2030 by opening new mines near its existing mills. At the Fox Complex in Ontario, the company spent $12.2 million on underground work at the new Stock Mine this quarter, keeping the build on schedule for December mining and commercial production in the first half of 2027.

In Mexico, crews started building the mill at the El Gallo mine, aiming for first gold in the fourth quarter of 2027 and 20,000 ounces a year. Because Stock will replace the expiring Froome mine with softer rock and lower royalties, and El Gallo needs little ongoing development, these two projects are the main bridge to lower costs next year.

What to watch: confirmation in the fourth-quarter report that underground mining at Stock started in December as scheduled. A timely start is needed for the Fox Complex to reach its 35,000-ounce target in 2027.

🐻 𝐁𝐞𝐚𝐫 𝐂𝐚𝐬𝐞

🔴🔴 𝐌𝐢𝐧𝐞 𝐏𝐫𝐨𝐛𝐥𝐞𝐦𝐬 𝐖𝐢𝐩𝐞 𝐎𝐮𝐭 𝐇𝐢𝐠𝐡𝐞𝐫 𝐆𝐨𝐥𝐝 𝐏𝐫𝐢𝐜𝐞𝐬
Higher gold and silver prices were supposed to generate cash to pay for McEwen's expansion, and the company's average selling price rose 19% from a year ago to $4,151 per ounce. Instead, simultaneous troubles at all three operating mines cut total production by 23% to 22,852 GEOs and drove revenue down 14% to $43.6 million.

• Gross margin: 9.2% of revenue, down 6.3 percentage points from 15.4% a year ago by our math
• Direct production costs: 73.2% of revenue, up 3.5 percentage points from a year ago
• Depreciation and depletion (wear and tear on mines): 16.2% of revenue, up 1.1 percentage points
• Net loss: $36.7 million, compared with a $0.5 million loss a year ago
• Adjusted EBITDA (operating cash profit excluding one-offs): negative $10.9 million, down from positive $11.8 million

At the Fox Complex, finishing all remaining underground development at the Froome mine added $780 per ounce to costs, while milling low-grade stockpiles added $150. Even stripping out that $930 per ounce by our math, Fox's all-in sustaining cost was $2,795 per ounce, still up 19% from a year ago. When a miner loses money with gold above $4,100, its self-funded growth plan has very little room for operating mistakes.

What to watch: fourth-quarter gross profit and Adjusted EBITDA from the wholly owned mines. If October's lower unit costs hold through December, Adjusted EBITDA will return to positive territory.

🔴🔴 𝐅𝐮𝐥𝐥-𝐘𝐞𝐚𝐫 𝐂𝐨𝐬𝐭 𝐓𝐚𝐫𝐠𝐞𝐭𝐬 𝐍𝐞𝐞𝐝 𝐈𝐦𝐩𝐨𝐬𝐬𝐢𝐛𝐥𝐞 𝐅𝐨𝐮𝐫𝐭𝐡-𝐐𝐮𝐚𝐫𝐭𝐞𝐫 𝐃𝐫𝐨𝐩𝐬
McEwen kept its full-year consolidated and mine-by-mine cost forecasts unchanged, saying October costs at the Fox Complex were back inside the annual target range at $2,618 per ounce. Keeping the full-year targets intact suggests the third-quarter cost jump will average out by December.

The nine-month numbers tell a different story. Through September, all-in sustaining costs averaged $3,107 per ounce at Fox across 17,212 ounces, and $2,946 at San José across 43,388 ounces. By our math, hitting the middle of the full-year cost outlook ($2,750 at Fox and $2,400 at San José) would require fourth-quarter AISC to drop to about $1,317 per ounce at Fox and $1,092 per ounce at San José.

Neither mine has approached those cost levels in recent years, and Fox's improved October figure of $2,618 is still double what the full-year math requires. In addition, the company warned that Argentine inflation and a strong peso will keep pressuring San José costs through year-end, making a full-year cost miss at both sites almost certain.

What to watch: full-year 2026 all-in sustaining costs per ounce when fourth-quarter results are published. A finish above $2,750 per ounce company-wide will confirm that the third-quarter overruns were too large to make up in three months.

🔴 𝐀𝐧𝐝𝐞𝐬 𝐒𝐧𝐨𝐰𝐟𝐚𝐥𝐥 𝐏𝐮𝐬𝐡𝐞𝐬 𝐋𝐨𝐬 𝐀𝐳𝐮𝐥𝐞𝐬 𝐃𝐞𝐜𝐢𝐬𝐢𝐨𝐧 𝐈𝐧𝐭𝐨 𝟐𝟎𝟐𝟕
McEwen owns 46.3% of McEwen Copper, which is developing the Los Azules copper project in Argentina, plus a 1.25% royalty on its future sales. In prior quarters, the company aimed to reach a Final Investment Decision (FID, the formal commitment to build the mine) by the end of 2026 and start construction in early 2027.

The project won permits this quarter for its 3,000-bed camp and for connecting to Argentina's national power grid, and expanded its loan facility to $240 million. However, the company said "Exceptional snowfall in the Andes, the heaviest in more than two decades, has delayed the reopening of the site access road" until early 2027.

Because crews cannot reach the mountain site, McEwen Copper now targets FID and full project financing in mid-2027, six months later than before. The company warned that "Site works will start later than planned, and the delay may affect the construction schedule", which narrows the time left to hit its 2030 copper production goal.

What to watch: the updated Los Azules project schedule once road crews open the site in early 2027. That schedule will show whether first copper cathode production can still happen in 2030.

👓 𝐎𝐭𝐡𝐞𝐫 𝐓𝐡𝐞𝐦𝐞𝐬

𝐖𝐞𝐚𝐭𝐡𝐞𝐫 𝐚𝐧𝐝 𝐀𝐫𝐠𝐞𝐧𝐭𝐢𝐧𝐞 𝐈𝐧𝐟𝐥𝐚𝐭𝐢𝐨𝐧 𝐇𝐢𝐭 𝐒𝐚𝐧 𝐉𝐨𝐬é
At the San José mine in southern Argentina, record regional snowfall soaked the ore with moisture. To prevent wet clay from blocking the processing plant, operators fed the mill harder sulphide rock with lower gold and silver grades, cutting McEwen's share of output by 21% to 11,786 GEOs. The company also stated that "Argentine inflation and the relative strength of the peso are expected to continue affecting unit costs through the remainder of 2026".

— • — • —

💲 𝐎𝐭𝐡𝐞𝐫 𝐊𝐏𝐈𝐬

𝐂𝐚𝐬𝐡 𝐚𝐧𝐝 𝐦𝐚𝐫𝐤𝐞𝐭𝐚𝐛𝐥𝐞 𝐬𝐞𝐜𝐮𝐫𝐢𝐭𝐢𝐞𝐬 (𝟐𝟔𝐐𝟑): $𝟓𝟗.𝟓 𝐦𝐢𝐥𝐥𝐢𝐨𝐧  ⇘ decelerating
Liquid holdings fell 35.1% from last quarter's $91.7 million, combining $49.1 million in cash and $10.4 million in marketable securities. Operating losses and mine development spending offset the $13.6 million loan sale, though the October Timmins property sale added $5 million in cash and $50 million in Discovery Mining shares after quarter-end.

𝐄𝐱𝐩𝐥𝐨𝐫𝐚𝐭𝐢𝐨𝐧 𝐢𝐧𝐯𝐞𝐬𝐭𝐦𝐞𝐧𝐭 (𝟐𝟔𝐐𝟑): $𝟏𝟏.𝟐 𝐦𝐢𝐥𝐥𝐢𝐨𝐧  ⇗ accelerating
Drilling spend rose 64.7% from $6.8 million a year ago and equalled 25.7% of third-quarter revenue. Nine-month exploration reached $28.0 million across Nevada, Ontario and Manitoba, topping the $25.7 million full-year budget the miner set in the second quarter and contributing to the wider quarterly net loss.

𝐂𝐨𝐦𝐦𝐨𝐧 𝐬𝐡𝐚𝐫𝐞𝐬 𝐨𝐮𝐭𝐬𝐭𝐚𝐧𝐝𝐢𝐧𝐠 (𝟐𝟔𝐐𝟑): 𝟔𝟏.𝟔 𝐦𝐢𝐥𝐥𝐢𝐨𝐧  ⇗ accelerating
Share count rose 13.9% from 54.1 million a year ago and is up from 59.7 million last quarter. The US and Canadian miner issued stock earlier this year to buy Canadian Gold Corp and Golden Lake Exploration, expanding its resource base while increasing the share count ahead of its planned production ramp.

— • — • —

🔮 𝐆𝐮𝐢𝐝𝐚𝐧𝐜𝐞

𝐅𝐘𝟐𝟔 𝐂𝐨𝐧𝐬𝐨𝐥𝐢𝐝𝐚𝐭𝐞𝐝 𝐏𝐫𝐨𝐝𝐮𝐜𝐭𝐢𝐨𝐧: 𝟏𝟎𝟗,𝟎𝟎𝟎–𝟏𝟐𝟎,𝟎𝟎𝟎 𝐆𝐄𝐎𝐬  ⇗ accelerating
🠆 unchanged from 109,000–120,000 GEOs
Unchanged. The full-year plan points to 114,500 gold equivalent ounces at the middle of the range, down 1.0% from 2025. By our math, reaching the middle of the range leaves 30,305 ounces for Q4, which requires a 32.6% jump from Q3's depressed output.

𝐅𝐘𝟐𝟔 𝐂𝐨𝐧𝐬𝐨𝐥𝐢𝐝𝐚𝐭𝐞𝐝 𝐂𝐚𝐬𝐡 𝐂𝐨𝐬𝐭𝐬 𝐩𝐞𝐫 𝐆𝐄𝐎: $𝟐,𝟐𝟎𝟎–$𝟐,𝟒𝟓𝟎  ⇘ decelerating
🠆 unchanged from $2,200–$2,450
Unchanged. The company kept the consolidated direct mining cost range it raised in Q2. After nine months, cash costs at the wholly owned mines averaged $2,579 per ounce and San José averaged $2,525, so both sit above the top end of the annual plan heading into the final quarter.

𝐅𝐘𝟐𝟔 𝐂𝐨𝐧𝐬𝐨𝐥𝐢𝐝𝐚𝐭𝐞𝐝 𝐀𝐈𝐒𝐂 𝐩𝐞𝐫 𝐆𝐄𝐎: $𝟐,𝟓𝟎𝟎–$𝟐,𝟕𝟓𝟎  ⇘ decelerating
🠆 unchanged from $2,500–$2,750
Unchanged. The middle of the range is $2,625 per ounce. Nine-month AISC stands at $3,035 per ounce for the wholly owned mines and $2,946 at San José, leaving the full-year target out of reach unless fourth-quarter upkeep costs fall far below October's reported rates.

𝐅𝐘𝟐𝟔 𝐆𝐨𝐥𝐝 𝐁𝐚𝐫 𝐏𝐫𝐨𝐝𝐮𝐜𝐭𝐢𝐨𝐧: 𝟑𝟎,𝟎𝟎𝟎–𝟑𝟑,𝟎𝟎𝟎 𝐆𝐄𝐎𝐬  ⇗ accelerating
🠆 unchanged from 30,000–33,000 GEOs
Unchanged. The Nevada mine's forecast was cut from 39,000–43,000 ounces in Q2 and held steady this quarter. By our math, the 31,500-ounce middle of the range leaves 11,559 ounces for Q4, nearly double Q3's 6,215 ounces; October's rebound to 3,353 ounces puts the bottom of the range within sight.

𝐅𝐘𝟐𝟔 𝐆𝐨𝐥𝐝 𝐁𝐚𝐫 𝐂𝐚𝐬𝐡 𝐂𝐨𝐬𝐭𝐬 𝐩𝐞𝐫 𝐆𝐄𝐎: $𝟐,𝟔𝟓𝟎–$𝟐,𝟗𝟓𝟎  ⇘ decelerating
🠆 unchanged from $2,650–$2,950
Unchanged. Nine-month cash costs at Gold Bar are $2,772 per ounce after Q3 reached $3,248. Because October cash costs fell back to $2,768 per ounce following the August pit changes, the mine is on track to finish inside this annual range.

𝐅𝐘𝟐𝟔 𝐆𝐨𝐥𝐝 𝐁𝐚𝐫 𝐀𝐈𝐒𝐂 𝐩𝐞𝐫 𝐆𝐄𝐎: $𝟐,𝟗𝟎𝟎–$𝟑,𝟐𝟎𝟎  ⇘ decelerating
🠆 unchanged from $2,900–$3,200
Unchanged. Nine-month AISC at Gold Bar sits at $2,975 per ounce. By our math, hitting the $3,050 middle of the range allows Q4 AISC of up to $3,179 per ounce, which looks achievable after October came in at $2,873.

𝐅𝐘𝟐𝟔 𝐅𝐨𝐱 𝐂𝐨𝐦𝐩𝐥𝐞𝐱 𝐏𝐫𝐨𝐝𝐮𝐜𝐭𝐢𝐨𝐧: 𝟐𝟎,𝟎𝟎𝟎–𝟐𝟑,𝟎𝟎𝟎 𝐆𝐄𝐎𝐬  ⇒ stable
🠆 unchanged from 20,000–23,000 GEOs
Unchanged. The Ontario complex kept the higher target it set in Q2. With 17,212 ounces produced in the first nine months, by our math the mine needs only 4,288 ounces in Q4 to reach the 21,500-ounce middle of the range, slightly below Q3's 4,427 ounces.

𝐅𝐘𝟐𝟔 𝐅𝐨𝐱 𝐂𝐨𝐦𝐩𝐥𝐞𝐱 𝐂𝐚𝐬𝐡 𝐂𝐨𝐬𝐭𝐬 𝐩𝐞𝐫 𝐆𝐄𝐎: $𝟐,𝟐𝟎𝟎–$𝟐,𝟒𝟎𝟎  ⇘ decelerating
🠆 unchanged from $2,200–$2,400
Unchanged. Nine-month cash costs at Fox are $2,349 per ounce after Q3 rose to $2,911 on low-grade stockpile processing. October's cash cost of $2,531 per ounce is still above the top of the annual range, making the full-year target tight.

𝐅𝐘𝟐𝟔 𝐅𝐨𝐱 𝐂𝐨𝐦𝐩𝐥𝐞𝐱 𝐀𝐈𝐒𝐂 𝐩𝐞𝐫 𝐆𝐄𝐎: $𝟐,𝟔𝟓𝟎–$𝟐,𝟖𝟓𝟎  ⇘ decelerating
🠆 unchanged from $2,650–$2,850
Unchanged. Nine-month AISC at Fox reached $3,107 per ounce because Q3 included all remaining Froome underground development. By our math, hitting the $2,750 middle of the range would require Q4 AISC of $1,317 per ounce, whereas October was $2,618.

𝐅𝐘𝟐𝟔 𝐒𝐚𝐧 𝐉𝐨𝐬é 𝐀𝐭𝐭𝐫𝐢𝐛𝐮𝐭𝐚𝐛𝐥𝐞 𝐏𝐫𝐨𝐝𝐮𝐜𝐭𝐢𝐨𝐧: 𝟓𝟗,𝟎𝟎𝟎–𝟔𝟒,𝟎𝟎𝟎 𝐆𝐄𝐎𝐬  ⇗ accelerating
🠆 unchanged from 59,000–64,000 GEOs
Unchanged. McEwen's 49% share of the Argentine mine has produced 43,388 ounces through September. By our math, reaching the 61,500-ounce middle of the range requires 18,112 ounces in Q4, a 53.7% rebound from Q3's snow-hit output as dry weather allows higher-grade clay ore back into the mill.

𝐅𝐘𝟐𝟔 𝐒𝐚𝐧 𝐉𝐨𝐬é 𝐂𝐚𝐬𝐡 𝐂𝐨𝐬𝐭𝐬 𝐩𝐞𝐫 𝐆𝐄𝐎: $𝟐,𝟎𝟎𝟎–$𝟐,𝟐𝟎𝟎  ⇘ decelerating
🠆 unchanged from $2,000–$2,200
Unchanged. Nine-month cash costs at San José are $2,525 per ounce after Q3 rose to $2,916. Because Argentine inflation and peso strength continue to lift local expenses, bringing the full-year average down into the $2,000–$2,200 band in a single quarter looks unrealistic.

𝐅𝐘𝟐𝟔 𝐒𝐚𝐧 𝐉𝐨𝐬é 𝐀𝐈𝐒𝐂 𝐩𝐞𝐫 𝐆𝐄𝐎: $𝟐,𝟑𝟎𝟎–$𝟐,𝟓𝟎𝟎  ⇘ decelerating
🠆 unchanged from $2,300–$2,500
Unchanged. Nine-month AISC is $2,946 per ounce after Q3 hit $3,414. By our math, reaching the $2,400 middle of the range would require Q4 AISC to fall to $1,092 per ounce across 18,112 ounces.

— • — • —

❓ 𝐊𝐞𝐲 𝐐𝐮𝐞𝐬𝐭𝐢𝐨𝐧𝐬

𝐖𝐡𝐲 𝐤𝐞𝐞𝐩 𝐟𝐮𝐥𝐥-𝐲𝐞𝐚𝐫 𝐜𝐨𝐬𝐭 𝐭𝐚𝐫𝐠𝐞𝐭𝐬 𝐭𝐡𝐚𝐭 𝐫𝐞𝐪𝐮𝐢𝐫𝐞 𝐢𝐦𝐩𝐨𝐬𝐬𝐢𝐛𝐥𝐞 𝐐𝟒 𝐝𝐫𝐨𝐩𝐬?
Nine-month AISC is $3,107 per ounce at Fox and $2,946 at San José. By our math, hitting the middle of the unchanged annual targets requires Q4 AISC of $1,317 at Fox and $1,092 at San José, far below October's reported levels.

𝐖𝐢𝐥𝐥 𝐭𝐡𝐞 𝐀𝐧𝐝𝐞𝐬 𝐬𝐧𝐨𝐰 𝐝𝐞𝐥𝐚𝐲 𝐩𝐮𝐬𝐡 𝐋𝐨𝐬 𝐀𝐳𝐮𝐥𝐞𝐬 𝐩𝐚𝐬𝐭 𝟐𝟎𝟑𝟎?
Road crews will not reach Los Azules until early 2027, pushing the Final Investment Decision to mid-2027 and delaying site works. Management has not yet said how much camp expansion will cost or whether first copper could slip into 2031.

𝐂𝐚𝐧 𝐌𝐜𝐄𝐰𝐞𝐧 𝐬𝐞𝐥𝐥 𝐢𝐭𝐬 $𝟓𝟎 𝐦𝐢𝐥𝐥𝐢𝐨𝐧 𝐢𝐧 𝐃𝐢𝐬𝐜𝐨𝐯𝐞𝐫𝐲 𝐌𝐢𝐧𝐢𝐧𝐠 𝐬𝐡𝐚𝐫𝐞𝐬?
The Timmins property sale brought in $5 million in cash and $50 million in Discovery Mining stock. With cash down to $49.1 million and 2027 construction approaching, investors need to know if those shares carry lock-up limits before they can fund capex.

𝐖𝐡𝐚𝐭 𝐢𝐬 𝐭𝐡𝐞 𝐧𝐞𝐰 𝐟𝐮𝐥𝐥-𝐲𝐞𝐚𝐫 𝐛𝐮𝐝𝐠𝐞𝐭 𝐟𝐨𝐫 𝐞𝐱𝐩𝐥𝐨𝐫𝐚𝐭𝐢𝐨𝐧 𝐬𝐩𝐞𝐧𝐝𝐢𝐧𝐠?
McEwen raised its 2026 exploration budget to $25.7 million in Q2, but nine-month spending has already reached $28.0 million after an $11.2 million third quarter. The release did not state how much more the company plans to spend in Q4.

$GHI Q3 2026 earnings: Greystone sells a Colorado property, but core lending still shrinks

Greystone Housing Impact Investors LP, an affordable-housing lender, closed its first apartment joint venture sale in five quarters while its core bond portfolio kept shrinking. Selling the Vantage at Loveland property in Colorado brought in $24 million and lifted distributable cash to $0.17 per unit, covering the $0.14 payout. Without the $2.5 million return from that sale, recurring distributable cash was about $0.06 per unit by our math. Chief executive Kenneth C. Rogozinski plans to put sale proceeds into tax-exempt housing bonds, yet the core bond and loan base fell 20% from a year ago.

• Revenue ex foreclosed properties: $𝟐𝟎.𝟎𝐌 (-5% from a year ago by our math)
• Distributable cash per unit (CAD): $𝟎.𝟏𝟕 ($0.06 excluding the Loveland sale by our math)
• Core bond and loan portfolio: $𝟖𝟗𝟖.𝟒𝐌 (-20% from a year ago)
• Quarterly distribution declared: $𝟎.𝟏𝟒 (Unchanged from Q2; down from $0.30 a year ago)

⚖️ 𝐕𝐞𝐫𝐝𝐢𝐜𝐭: ⚪ Neutral

The story is unchanged because one property exit did not stop the decline in recurring lending income. The Colorado sale and a new Nevada listing show that partners can exit buildings and recover principal, which eases the fear of deep book-value write-downs. The bad news: the partnership still put $5 million into remaining joint ventures, and a single borrower missed September payments on five housing bonds, leaving one bond still unpaid.

The question now is whether Greystone can sell enough apartment joint ventures and buy enough housing bonds to cover its $0.14 distribution from recurring interest. Either the new Nevada listing and rising cash balances quickly rebuild the bond portfolio, or slow sales and ongoing joint venture cash drains force another distribution cut. Fourth-quarter bond additions and the delinquent borrower details in the 10-Q filing will tell.

Full article with charts - link in bio

🐂 𝐁𝐮𝐥𝐥 𝐂𝐚𝐬𝐞

🟢 𝐅𝐢𝐫𝐬𝐭 𝐉𝐨𝐢𝐧𝐭 𝐕𝐞𝐧𝐭𝐮𝐫𝐞 𝐒𝐚𝐥𝐞 𝐢𝐧 𝐅𝐢𝐯𝐞 𝐐𝐮𝐚𝐫𝐭𝐞𝐫𝐬
Greystone Housing Impact Investors LP, an affordable-housing lender, wants to exit its equity stakes in market-rate apartment joint ventures and put that money into tax-exempt housing bonds. Before August, the partnership had not closed a property sale since May 2025, which left its money tied up in buildings generating accounting losses.

In August, the managing partner sold the Vantage at Loveland apartment property in Colorado for $23.6 million in gross proceeds. The sale returned Greystone's $21.1 million of invested equity and paid $2.5 million of preferred return income. In October, a partner listed a second property, Valage Senior Living Carson Valley in Nevada, for sale.

The Colorado exit proves the partnership can recover its full invested principal plus a return on a completed building. That lowers the risk of widespread write-downs across the remaining $137.5 million joint venture portfolio, even though one sale does not settle the timeline for the other ten properties.

What to watch: the sale price and closing date for Valage Senior Living Carson Valley. A second exit at or above carrying value would show that the joint venture portfolio can turn back into cash without damaging book value.

🟢 𝐋𝐨𝐰𝐞𝐫 𝐎𝐯𝐞𝐫𝐡𝐞𝐚𝐝 𝐚𝐧𝐝 𝐃𝐞𝐫𝐢𝐯𝐚𝐭𝐢𝐯𝐞 𝐆𝐚𝐢𝐧𝐬 𝐋𝐢𝐟𝐭𝐞𝐝 𝐏𝐫𝐨𝐟𝐢𝐭
Greystone returned to GAAP profitability this quarter, reporting net income of $3.2 million, or $0.09 per Beneficial Unit Certificate (BUC), its publicly traded partnership unit. That compares with a loss of $0.11 per unit last quarter and a loss of $0.01 per unit a year ago.

Two expense lines drove the swing. General and administrative overhead fell 26.3% from a year ago to $3.5 million, dropping 6.7 percentage points of revenue to 16.2%, partly because restricted unit compensation reversed by $167 thousand. At the same time, interest rate swaps produced $4.0 million in non-cash valuation gains, shifting the derivative line by 19.0 percentage points of revenue.

What to watch: general and administrative expenses in the fourth quarter. Holding overhead near $3.5 million without relying on compensation reversals would preserve cash while the lending portfolio rebuilds.

🐻 𝐁𝐞𝐚𝐫 𝐂𝐚𝐬𝐞

🔴🔴 𝐑𝐞𝐜𝐮𝐫𝐫𝐢𝐧𝐠 𝐂𝐚𝐬𝐡 𝐒𝐭𝐢𝐥𝐥 𝐌𝐢𝐬𝐬𝐞𝐝 𝐭𝐡𝐞 𝐃𝐢𝐬𝐭𝐫𝐢𝐛𝐮𝐭𝐢𝐨𝐧
Greystone evaluates its payout using Cash Available for Distribution (CAD), a measure that strips out non-cash items like depreciation and unrealized swap gains. For the third quarter, the partnership reported CAD of $3.8 million, or $0.17 per unit, which covered its $0.14 regular quarterly distribution for the first time this year.

• Reported CAD per unit: $0.17, down from $0.18 a year ago
• Vantage at Loveland preferred return included in CAD: $2.5 million, or about $0.11 per unit by our math
• CAD excluding the property sale: $1.3 million, or about $0.06 per unit by our math
• Nine-month CAD per unit: $0.40 against $0.42 in declared distributions

The headline coverage rests on a one-off property exit rather than recurring bond interest. Without the $2.5 million payout from the Colorado sale, investment income fell 18.6% from a year ago by our math, and recurring cash flow covered less than half of the $0.14 distribution.

What to watch: fourth-quarter CAD per unit when no joint venture sale closes. Another reading near $0.06 to $0.10 per unit would keep pressure on the board to trim the $0.14 payout again.

🔴🔴 𝐂𝐨𝐫𝐞 𝐋𝐞𝐧𝐝𝐢𝐧𝐠 𝐁𝐚𝐬𝐞 𝐒𝐡𝐫𝐚𝐧𝐤 𝐃𝐞𝐬𝐩𝐢𝐭𝐞 𝐏𝐫𝐨𝐩𝐞𝐫𝐭𝐲 𝐄𝐱𝐢𝐭
Chief executive Kenneth C. Rogozinski said the team is working to "identify traditional mortgage revenue bond investment opportunities where we can redeploy capital once the market rate multifamily exits occur". Mortgage revenue bonds (MRBs) and governmental issuer loans (GILs) are tax-exempt debt instruments that finance affordable housing and generate the partnership's core interest income.

Even with the Colorado sale returning $21.1 million of equity, the on-balance-sheet MRB and GIL portfolio shrank by $29.1 million from last quarter to $898.4 million, down 20.3% from a year ago by our math. Greystone advanced $39.2 million into bonds and loans, but it received $14.0 million in loan paydowns and sold $26.2 million of loans into its off-balance-sheet construction lending joint venture.

At the same time, the partnership sent another $5.2 million of equity into its market-rate joint ventures. Because new construction loans are routed off the balance sheet and existing joint ventures still absorb cash, the interest-earning asset base continues to contract, leaving less recurring income to pay unitholders.

What to watch: net additions to the MRB and GIL balance in the fourth quarter. Until bond purchases outpace redemptions and loan sales, core interest income cannot recover.

🔴 𝐎𝐧𝐞 𝐁𝐨𝐫𝐫𝐨𝐰𝐞𝐫 𝐌𝐢𝐬𝐬𝐞𝐝 𝐏𝐚𝐲𝐦𝐞𝐧𝐭𝐬 𝐨𝐧 𝐅𝐢𝐯𝐞 𝐁𝐨𝐧𝐝𝐬
Greystone has consistently stated that borrowers across its affordable-housing bond and loan portfolio were current on their contractual payments. That clean payment record broke at the end of the third quarter.

The company disclosed that all borrowers met their debt service obligations as of September 30 "except for five MRBs associated with a single borrower". Between the end of the quarter and November 9, the borrower paid on four of the five bonds, and management remains "in ongoing discussions with the borrower regarding the delayed payments".

Although Greystone recorded a small net credit loss recovery of $174 thousand this quarter, late payments across five bonds show strain among affordable-housing operators. What to watch: the identity, principal balance and occupancy of the delinquent borrower's properties in the quarterly 10-Q filing, which will show whether a forbearance or foreclosure is likely.

🔴 𝐑𝐢𝐬𝐤𝐬 𝐭𝐡𝐢𝐬 𝐪𝐮𝐚𝐫𝐭𝐞𝐫 𝐝𝐢𝐝𝐧'𝐭 𝐚𝐧𝐬𝐰𝐞𝐫
Five standing balance-sheet and credit concerns cannot be read from the earnings release or supplemental tables and await the quarterly 10-Q filing.

• South Carolina foreclosed properties: operating income and debt-service coverage ahead of the February and June 2027 recourse mortgage tests.
• Stabilized bond portfolio occupancy: physical occupancy across the core apartment properties, which sat at 85.8% last quarter.
• Affordable housing net interest spread: segment net interest income and average earning balances from the 10-Q management discussion.
• Debt maturities and credit lines: refinancing progress on credit lines maturing in June 2027 and swap collateral postings.
• Net book value per unit: the supplemental waterfall chart is an image without text values, leaving Q3 book value per unit unreadable until the 10-Q.

👓 𝐎𝐭𝐡𝐞𝐫 𝐓𝐡𝐞𝐦𝐞𝐬

𝐈𝐧𝐭𝐞𝐫𝐞𝐬𝐭 𝐑𝐚𝐭𝐞 𝐒𝐰𝐚𝐩𝐬 𝐂𝐮𝐬𝐡𝐢𝐨𝐧𝐞𝐝 𝐅𝐥𝐨𝐚𝐭𝐢𝐧𝐠 𝐁𝐨𝐫𝐫𝐨𝐰𝐢𝐧𝐠 𝐂𝐨𝐬𝐭𝐬
Greystone uses interest rate swaps to protect its floating-rate bond borrowings against interest rate swings, collecting $280 thousand in net cash receipts during the third quarter. Its sensitivity table shows that a 1 percentage point rise in the Secured Overnight Financing Rate (SOFR), a benchmark interest rate, would reduce annual net interest income by $1.06 million, or $0.046 per unit, while a 1 percentage point drop would add the same amount.

— • — • —

💲 𝐎𝐭𝐡𝐞𝐫 𝐊𝐏𝐈𝐬

𝐓𝐨𝐭𝐚𝐥 𝐚𝐬𝐬𝐞𝐭𝐬 (𝟐𝟔𝐐𝟑): $𝟏.𝟑𝟓 𝐛𝐢𝐥𝐥𝐢𝐨𝐧  ⇘ decelerating
Total assets shrank 3.0% from last quarter and 10.5% since the end of 2025, down to $1,345.3 million. Loan sales to the construction joint venture and the Colorado property exit reduced the balance sheet, while the leverage ratio — total debt divided by adjusted asset cost — held at 74%, unchanged from June and down from 75% at year-end.

𝐂𝐚𝐬𝐡 𝐚𝐧𝐝 𝐫𝐞𝐬𝐭𝐫𝐢𝐜𝐭𝐞𝐝 𝐜𝐚𝐬𝐡 (𝟐𝟔𝐐𝟑): $𝟓𝟒.𝟒 𝐦𝐢𝐥𝐥𝐢𝐨𝐧  ⇗ accelerating
Total cash rose 31.1% from last quarter by our math, combining $32.4 million of unrestricted cash and $22.0 million of restricted cash. Restricted cash — money held in trust accounts for bond purchases or collateral — more than doubled from $10.6 million in June as proceeds from the Loveland property sale and loan redemptions arrived awaiting redeployment.

𝐏𝐫𝐨𝐩𝐞𝐫𝐭𝐲 𝐥𝐨𝐚𝐧𝐬, 𝐧𝐞𝐭 (𝟐𝟔𝐐𝟑): $𝟑𝟗.𝟎 𝐦𝐢𝐥𝐥𝐢𝐨𝐧  ⇘ decelerating
Property loans — direct loans to apartment developers that sit alongside housing bonds — fell 25.6% from $52.5 million last quarter. Borrowers paid down $14.0 million of principal during the quarter, and the partnership sold additional property loans into its construction lending joint venture, reducing on-balance-sheet interest income.

— • — • —

❓ 𝐊𝐞𝐲 𝐐𝐮𝐞𝐬𝐭𝐢𝐨𝐧𝐬

𝐖𝐡𝐢𝐜𝐡 𝐛𝐨𝐫𝐫𝐨𝐰𝐞𝐫 𝐦𝐢𝐬𝐬𝐞𝐝 𝐩𝐚𝐲𝐦𝐞𝐧𝐭𝐬 𝐨𝐧 𝐟𝐢𝐯𝐞 𝐡𝐨𝐮𝐬𝐢𝐧𝐠 𝐛𝐨𝐧𝐝𝐬?
Five mortgage revenue bonds from one borrower were past due on September 30, and one remains unpaid. Investors need to know the total principal at risk, whether it is a Texas operator flagged last quarter, and whether a foreclosure is required.

𝐖𝐡𝐞𝐧 𝐰𝐢𝐥𝐥 𝐛𝐨𝐧𝐝 𝐩𝐮𝐫𝐜𝐡𝐚𝐬𝐞𝐬 𝐞𝐱𝐜𝐞𝐞𝐝 𝐥𝐨𝐚𝐧 𝐫𝐞𝐝𝐞𝐦𝐩𝐭𝐢𝐨𝐧𝐬 𝐚𝐧𝐝 𝐬𝐚𝐥𝐞𝐬?
The partnership received $21.1 million of equity from the Loveland sale, yet its core bond and loan portfolio still shrank by $29.1 million. Management has not said how much of its $54.4 million cash balance is committed to new tax-exempt bonds.

𝐖𝐢𝐥𝐥 𝐭𝐡𝐞 𝐛𝐨𝐚𝐫𝐝 𝐤𝐞𝐞𝐩 𝐭𝐡𝐞 $𝟎.𝟏𝟒 𝐝𝐢𝐬𝐭𝐫𝐢𝐛𝐮𝐭𝐢𝐨𝐧 𝐰𝐢𝐭𝐡𝐨𝐮𝐭 𝐬𝐚𝐥𝐞𝐬?
Excluding the $2.5 million preferred return from the Loveland exit, recurring distributable cash was about $0.06 per unit by our math. If Valage Senior Living does not close in the fourth quarter, recurring cash will again fall short of the payout.

𝐖𝐡𝐚𝐭 𝐚𝐫𝐞 𝐭𝐡𝐞 𝐨𝐜𝐜𝐮𝐩𝐚𝐧𝐜𝐲 𝐚𝐧𝐝 𝐬𝐩𝐫𝐞𝐚𝐝 𝐧𝐮𝐦𝐛𝐞𝐫𝐬 𝐢𝐧 𝐭𝐡𝐞 𝟏𝟎-𝐐?
The earnings release omits the affordable housing segment's net interest spread, stabilized apartment occupancy, and the South Carolina properties' debt-service coverage ahead of their February 2027 loan test. Those disclosures in the 10-Q will show how the core portfolio performed.

Project Jupiter represents a major investment in New Mexico’s future, with more than $13 billion in projected economic impact, an estimated 7,000 jobs during construction, including more than 1,230 New Mexican workers and 1,800 union workers to date, and 1,500 long-term jobs once operational. The project includes a fully funded $50 million investment in Doña Ana County water infrastructure. Its closed-loop cooling and fuel cell systems will use zero potable water and, on average, less water annually than nine U.S. households consume. Oracle has also committed to 100% carbon-free energy matching by 2031.

We look forward to working with the incoming administration to deliver these benefits for all New Mexicans.

text:
From @NM_SSA :
"November 2026 | New Mexico Shooting Sports Association
A New Governor, a New Legislature, and the Future of the Second Amendment in New Mexico

With the election of Deb Haaland as New Mexico's next governor, firearm owners, gun dealers, shooting ranges, firearm instructors, and Second Amendment organizations are looking ahead to what could happen when her administration takes office in January 2027.

The question now is not simply who occupies the Governor's Office, but what legislation could be introduced, what policies Haaland intends to pursue, and how those decisions could affect law-abiding New Mexicans.

1. The Return of Senate Bill 17 — Restrictions on Semiautomatic Firearms

One of the clearest indications of Haaland's firearms priorities comes from her own campaign.

On May 20, 2026, Haaland announced her support for passing the Stop Illegal Gun Trade Act, which would impose additional requirements on firearms dealers and restrict certain categories of firearms.

A version of this legislation, Senate Bill 17, passed the New Mexico Senate in February 2026 but failed to become law.

The 2026 legislation included restrictions affecting:

AR-15-style and other gas-operated semiautomatic firearms capable of accepting detachable magazines, subject to specified exceptions.

Detachable magazines holding more than 10 rounds.

Certain .50-caliber rifles and ammunition.

Firearms dealer security, inventory, employee training, reporting, and inspection requirements.

Dealer participation in transfers of firearms and magazines covered by the proposed restrictions.

These provisions were part of the unsuccessful 2026 legislation. They are not currently law under SB17.

Because Haaland expressly supported the legislation during her campaign, a similar proposal is an important possibility for the 2027 legislative session. The language of any new bill will determine exactly which firearms, transactions, and businesses it would affect.

2. Greater Oversight of Firearms Dealers and Businesses

New Mexico firearms dealers, Federal Firearms Licensees (FFLs), and other industry businesses could face new compliance requirements if legislation modeled on SB17 advances.

The 2026 proposal included enhanced recordkeeping, inventory controls, security measures, employee training, reporting, and state inspections.

Supporters maintain that these requirements could help prevent firearm theft and illegal trafficking. Firearms-industry representatives have raised concerns about compliance costs, regulatory complexity, and the effect on smaller businesses, particularly in rural communities.

The practical consequences would depend on the final legislation, including exemptions, implementation deadlines, and enforcement procedures.

3. A New Office of Gun Violence Prevention

Haaland has also proposed establishing an Office of Gun Violence Prevention and appointing a dedicated Gun Violence Prevention Coordinator.

According to her campaign, these officials would work with the New Mexico Department of Public Safety and other organizations on violence-prevention programs, illegal firearms, and related public safety initiatives.

Key questions include what authority the new office would have, how it would be funded, and whether it would help develop future firearms regulations.

Creating such an office would not, by itself, establish new firearms prohibitions. Its powers would depend on the legal authority and resources provided.

4. New Mexico's Seven-Day Firearms Waiting Period

New Mexico's seven-day waiting period remains a significant issue for firearm purchasers and dealers.

The law was enacted in 2024 under Governor Michelle Lujan Grisham and has been challenged in federal court.

On August 27, 2026, the United States District Court for the District of New Mexico issued an order preventing enforcement against the two named plaintiffs. According to the New Mexico Department of Public Safety, the waiting period remains applicable to other purchasers.

Haaland's administration will inherit this law and the legal issues surrounding it.

Its ultimate future depends on additional judicial proceedings, potential legislative changes, and any subsequent court rulings.

5. The 2027 Legislature Will Be a Major Factor

Haaland will enter office with Democrats controlling both chambers of the New Mexico Legislature.

Following the November election, Democrats hold a reported 47–23 majority in the House and a 26–16 majority in the Senate.

These numbers matter because proposed firearms restrictions will proceed through legislative committees and floor votes before reaching the governor.

However, party control does not guarantee passage. SB17 failed in 2026 despite Democratic majorities, demonstrating that individual legislators and committee decisions can determine the outcome of controversial legislation.

The next 60-day legislative session begins January 19, 2027, and concludes March 20, 2027.

6. What About Concealed Carry and Other Firearms Laws?

New Mexico's concealed carry licensing system, firearm sales regulations, and other existing laws will remain in place unless modified through lawful legislative or administrative action or affected by court decisions.

There is no basis at this time to state that Haaland has announced a specific proposal to eliminate concealed carry licenses or prohibit concealed carry statewide.

However, gun owners and instructors will have reason to review any new legislation involving permit requirements, prohibited locations, training standards, licensing procedures, or firearms transfers.

Any such proposal should be evaluated on its actual language, not speculation.

7. Constitutional Challenges Could Play an Important Role

Future restrictions involving semiautomatic rifles, ammunition magazines, and firearm transactions could face challenges under the Second Amendment.

Federal courts continue to examine firearms laws in light of the United States Supreme Court's decisions in District of Columbia v. Heller, McDonald v. Chicago, and New York State Rifle & Pistol Association v. Bruen.

Whether a particular New Mexico law survives constitutional review will depend on its language, the relevant legal standards, and how courts apply those standards.

New firearms legislation could therefore generate both legislative debate and additional litigation.

What Happens Next?

As New Mexico prepares for a new administration, the most important developments to watch will be the actual legislation introduced in 2027, Haaland's proposed budget and executive appointments, and the positions taken by legislative committees.

Haaland has expressed a commitment to reducing gun violence through additional firearms regulation and public safety programs.

The questions for New Mexico firearm owners and businesses will be how those proposals are written, how they are enforced, and whether they comply with constitutional protections.

The 2027 legislative session could become an important period for New Mexico firearms policy, particularly because a new governor who has already endorsed SB17-style legislation will be taking office.

NMSSA Will Continue Monitoring Developments"

U.S. National Politics Update 2: A Democratic blue wave in the midterm elections has temporarily offset a projected decline in Black representation within the U.S. House of Representatives. According to an NPR analysis, the incoming Congress is set to include 60 Black House members, including nonvoting delegates, down from 63 in the current body. This figure remains just one away from the record loss of four Black representatives that occurred after the 1876 election.

The decline stems from a combination of factors, including high-level redistricting battles and standard political churn such as retirements. However, elevated Black voter turnout, particularly in the South, fueled Democratic victories that mitigated these losses. This dynamic was evident in Alabama, where Rep. Shomari Figures won reelection despite his district being redrawn by Republican state leaders to be more GOP-leaning following a Supreme Court ruling that weakened Voting Rights Act protections.

Advocates and experts warn that redistricting after the 2030 census continues to pose a threat to Black representation. The Supreme Court's decision in Louisiana v. Callais, released weeks before the midterms, allowed Alabama's legislature to redraw districts in a way that previously offered zero chance for Black-preferred candidates to win. While Figures' victory was attributed to remarkable turnout, experts caution that relying on such waves is not sustainable if voting rights are further diluted over time.

Redistricting changes also impacted Texas and Florida, where new maps undid some Black-represented districts. Conversely, Democrats flipped districts in North Carolina represented by incoming Black House Democrats Cyril Jefferson and LaKesha Womack. Additionally, Democratic socialist Reps.-elect Melat Kiros in Colorado and Donavan McKinney in Michigan are adding to the tally.

Beyond the House, Black representation in the Senate has reached a historic high of seven members. This includes Scott Colom, who is set to become the first Black senator from Mississippi since Reconstruction, and Juliana Stratton as Illinois Lt. Gov. While some politicians declare a generational shift, redistricting experts advise caution, noting that the full impact of recent Supreme Court decisions on state legislative maps may not be felt until 2028 or 2030.

House Republicans have elected Rep. Jim Jordan (R-Ohio) as House minority leader, and Senate Republicans picked Sen. John Thune (R-S.D.) as Senate minority leader for the next Congress starting in January.

Jordan, who defeated House Majority Leader Steve Scalise (R-La.) in Tuesday's vote, will face opposition from Democrats who have pledged to investigate the Trump administration, and will be tasked with taking back the House in 2028.

The tally was 106–73 in favor of Jordan, House GOP staff told reporters, including one from The Epoch Times.

Jordan is currently chairman of the House Judiciary Committee. He was first elected to Congress in 2006 from Ohio’s 4th Congressional District.

The election of Jordan, a staunch conservative, follows the GOP’s loss of dozens of seats in the midterms as the Democrats are on track to have as many as 260 seats come Jan. 3, 2027, when the new Congress will be sworn in.

House Speaker Mike Johnson (R-La.), who also serves as leader of the House GOP conference, elected not to run for minority leader following the midterm losses.

In a Dear Colleague letter, Jordan portrayed himself as a fighter for the House GOP and touted his experience in Congress facing the Democrats.

He criticized House Republicans for not having “a clear plan to survive the hour or the day in front of us. That will not cut it against an emboldened and energetic Democrat majority.”

“I know what it will take to lead our Conference in the minority, to stay unified, and to coordinate and calibrate our response to the Democrats’ tactics,” Jordan added. “We need a Leadership team that is active and engaged, forward-thinking and straight-shooting.”

Jordan is a founding member of the House Freedom Caucus, a conservative wing of the House GOP, and served as its first chairman. 

Under his watch, the Freedom Caucus pressured former Rep. John Boehner (R-Ohio) to step down as House speaker in 2015.

Jordan opposed Kevin McCarthy to succeed Boehner, but supported McCarthy's speakership bid in January 2023. McCarthy became speaker after 15 rounds of voting—only to be stripped of the gavel the following October after a motion to vacate.

Jordan ran for speaker but lost an internal House GOP vote to Scalise, who was unsuccessful in gathering enough Republicans to vote for him to be in the position, which is second in line to the presidency. Johnson threw his hat into the ring and went on to become speaker.

Following Jordan's election as minority leader, House Republicans praised him on X.

"Jim is a fighter and a convicted conservative. He’s the original congressional brawler and is exactly what our Conference needs to lead us back to the majority," Rep. Brandon Gill (R-Texas) posted.

"He is a strong conservative who will fight for this country and hold Washington accountable," said Rep. Ron Estes (R-Kan.).

Democrats criticized the House GOP for picking Jordan.

Rep. Don Beyer (D-Va.) reposted one of his posts from 2023 during the House speakership race to succeed McCarthy. Beyer criticized Jordan for not answering a subpoena from the House select committee investigating the Jan. 6, 2021, attack on the U.S. Capitol.

The Jewish Democratic Council of America also posted opposition on X: "Jim Jordan, a Trump ally who voted to overturn the 2020 election results, represents everything Americans voted against last week. 

The GOP continues to miss the message and show just how out of step they are with the people they claim to represent."

In addition to Jordan, Rep. Tom Emmer (R-Minn.) was elected House minority whip. He is currently the House majority whip.

Rep. Lisa McClain (R-Mich.) won reelection as House GOP conference chair.

CHAPTER 13 – VERY HARD QUESTIONS TO MAINSTREAM MEDIA AND THE VERY QUIET REST OF THE WORLD: WHY IS GENOCIDE TREATED LIKE NORMAL NEWS?

This is the chapter that asks questions many people want answered, but which are often missing from mainstream headlines.
Mainstream media frequently gives us headlines without enough explanation. We hear: "Clashes in Gaza," "Israel responds," "Hamas says," and "Death toll rises."
It can sound like a weather report, a football score or just another ordinary news story.
But this is about human lives.
So here are very hard questions for mainstream media – #CNN, #Fox, #BBC , The New York Times – and for the very quiet rest of the world, which watches the suffering in Gaza as though it were normal.

 HARD QUESTIONS TO MAINSTREAM MEDIA – THE BISHOPS WHO BLESS THE WAR

CNN, Fox, BBC and The New York Times, you say you are journalists. You say you are independent, impartial and committed to the truth.
So answer these questions.
1.Why do you sometimes describe a Palestinian child through the language of security and militancy, while an Israeli child is immediately presented as a child with a name, a face and a story?
2.Why does one child get a name, a face and a personal story, while the other becomes part of a number – "60,000 dead" – with no name, no face and no story?
3.Why do you often say, "Israel says," "Israel claims" and "Israel defends itself," while using words such as "Hamas claims" or "Hamas says"? Why are statements from Gaza's Health Ministry sometimes treated with immediate suspicion, while official Israeli statements receive a different level of scrutiny?
Is that balanced journalism, or is it a double standard?
4.Why have images and accounts of the October 7 attack received extensive coverage, while the destruction in Gaza has not always received the same sustained attention, with the same names, faces and personal stories?
Why does one attack become a detailed documentary, while another is reduced to a headline saying, "Death toll rises"?
5.Why do subjects such as Gaza Marine gas, the Hannibal Directive, Qatar's financial support for Hamas and the allegations of delayed military response not always receive the detailed investigation they deserve?
6.Why do headlines sometimes use words such as "clashes," "tensions" and "conflict," as though two equally equipped armies are fighting, when the military capabilities of the two sides are vastly different?
7.Why have some journalists faced professional consequences for expressing pro-Palestinian views, while others have been praised for expressing support for Israel? And how many Palestinian journalists have been killed in Gaza, over 200 according to organisations such as the Committee to Protect Journalists?
8.If a journalist is killed in Ukraine, the world demands an investigation. If a journalist is killed in Gaza, why does the story sometimes disappear so quickly?
9.Why do you use the word "genocide" when discussing events in places such as Rwanda and Bosnia, yet hesitate to use it when discussing Gaza?
South Africa brought a case against Israel at the International Court of Justice in 2024. The Court found that the rights claimed by Palestinians under the Genocide Convention were plausible and ordered provisional measures. That was not a final ruling that genocide had occurred.
10. So why not explain the legal process clearly, rather than avoiding the subject altogether?
Mainstream media, in this chess analogy, you are the Bishops. You influence how the public sees the board. But when you fail to ask difficult questions, you risk becoming Bishops who bless the war, protect the King and the Rook, and forget the Pawn.

 QUESTIONS TO THE VERY QUIET REST OF THE WORLD – WHY DO YOU WATCH AS IF THIS IS NORMAL?

Rest of the world – Africa, Asia, Latin America, the Arab world, the Muslim world and the Christian world – you are also part of this story.
So answer these questions.
1.The Arab world: Egypt, Jordan, Saudi Arabia, the UAE and Qatar, you share history, language, geography and political interests with Palestine. You have oil, money and powerful armies.
.Why do you watch Gaza suffer while your response is often limited to sending tents, rice and prayers? Why do you continue trading and maintaining relations with Israel while Palestinian civilians are being killed?
Is your oil more important than Palestinian blood?

2. #Africa : You know colonialism. You know apartheid. You know what it means to be treated as a Pawn on somebody else's board.
#SouthAfrica  Africa took #Israel  to the International Court of Justice. But what about the rest of Africa ?
Why do you vote one way at the #UnitedNations  in Support of Palestine but maintain economic and political relationships with USA & Israel that appear to contradict those positions?
Are your loans, trade agreements and military relationships more important than Palestinian lives?

3. #Asia: China, India and Indonesia, you represent billions of people and have enormous economic and diplomatic influence.
Why do you sometimes say, "We are neutral," when civilians are dying?
How can you remain neutral when children are being killed? Does neutrality, in such circumstances, risk becoming silence in favour of the stronger side?

4.Latin America: #Brazil , Colombia and Chile have taken strong positions on Palestine. Some countries have cut or downgraded relations with Israel.
But what about the others? Why are some governments still quiet?

5.And to the rest of the unbothered world:
You watch #TikTok.  #Instagram &  see  babies in Gaza die on a live video. You scroll, say, "Sad," press like and go to sleep.
How can you sleep when a baby dies on your phone, as though it were just another news update?
How did mass death become normal? How did thousands of lives become a headline saying, "Death toll rises," while people continue drinking their coffee?
If a child in Paris dies, the world demands answers. If a child in Newyork dies, the world also deserves to hear the story. If a Palestinian child in Gaza dies, why should the response be reduced to, "Clashes in Gaza"?
Why is Palestinian blood treated as though it matters less?
The rest of the world, you are not quiet because you do not know. You know.
Perhaps some governments are quiet because they fear the King. They fear America may cut aid, loans or diplomatic support. They fear being accused of antisemitism. They fear political and economic consequences.
So they remain quiet, while the Pawns continue to die.
But one day, the Pawn may become Queen.
And one day, the Pawn may ask you: "Where were you when I was dying?"
What will you answer?

CHAPTER 14 – : EUROPE AND AUSTRALIA IN 2025–2026 – WAS RECOGNISING PALESTINE A LAST-DITCH ATTEMPT TO SAVE FACE AFTER STAYING SILENT WHILE GAZA WAS BEING DESTROYED?ANOTHER #WWE GEOPOLITICAL THEATRE EPISODE?

After years of war, tens of thousands of reported deaths and enormous destruction in Gaza, several Western governments announced that they recognised Palestine as a state.
In September 2025, the #United Kingdom, #France , #Canada  and #Australia  announced recognition. Other #European  countries also took steps towards recognition during this period.
The headlines called it historic, brave and moral. Politicians stood before cameras and spoke about peace, the Two-State Solution and the children of Gaza.
And ordinary people on TikTok, Instagram and X asked one simple  question:
"WHERE WERE YOU FOR THE LAST TWO YEARS?"

Where were you in October 2023, when the bombing of Gaza began? Where were you in November 2023, as hospitals and civilian infrastructure came under attack? Where were you in 2024, when Rafah was attacked and the humanitarian crisis deepened?
Critics argue that Western governments continued selling or licensing weapons, maintaining diplomatic support and trading with Israel while repeatedly calling for restraint.
#France , you say you support human rights. But your government's handling of pro-Palestinian demonstrations in 2023 and 2024 faced criticism, including over restrictions and arrests.
Now, in 2025, you recognise Palestine.
Is that a change of conscience, or is it public relations?

#TheUK, you issued the Balfour Declaration in 1917 and ended your Mandate in Palestine in 1948. You have maintained a close relationship with Israel for decades and have faced criticism over your diplomatic and military support.
Now you recognise Palestine.
Is that justice, or an attempt to wash your hands after the blood has dried?

#Australia , you are far from Gaza but politically close to America. You supported America in wars in Iraq and Afghanistan and maintained defence and diplomatic relationships with Israel.
Your government also faced pressure from students, voters and protesters who demanded a stronger response to the destruction in Gaza.
Now you recognise Palestine.
Is that moral courage, or an attempt to save face after your own citizens began asking why their government remained silent?

#EUROPE & Australia,Was recognising Palestine in 2025–2026 a genuine act of justice, or was it a last-ditch attempt to save face after remaining silent for so long while Gaza was being destroyed?
Because if it was justice, why did it take so long?
-Why did it take tens of thousands of reported deaths? ---Why did it take years of destruction broadcast to the world?
-Why did Spain, Ireland and Norway recognise Palestine in 2024, while other governments waited until 2025?
Was that leadership, or was it following after the crowd had already left?
And if recognition was partly about saving face, what does it mean to recognise a state whose territory remains fragmented, whose people face severe restrictions, and whose infrastructure has been devastated?
You recognise Palestine on paper while Palestinians continue to struggle for land, water, freedom and security on the ground.
Is that recognition, or is it a certificate issued while the patient is still fighting for survival?
You say, "We recognise Palestine to save the Two-State Solution."
But the Two-State Solution faces enormous obstacles. Settlement expansion in the West Bank, the status of East Jerusalem and the destruction in Gaza have made the prospect of two viable states increasingly difficult.
You cannot save a Two-State Solution simply by recognising a state while doing nothing to address the conditions that threaten its existence.
That is like recognising a man after watching him drown, then saying, "We recognised him. We are good people."
The masses see it. The masses are not stupid.
They ask: Did you recognise Palestine because you believe in Palestinian rights, or because you fear how history will judge your silence?
Perhaps, in 20 years, when children ask, "Where were you when Gaza was destroyed?" some governments will point to their recognition of Palestine and say, "We were on the right side."
But what did you do when it mattered?
Europe and Australia, if you really want justice, recognition alone is not enough.
Recognition without meaningful action is political theatre (#wwe). Recognition without addressing arms transfers is theatre. Recognition without holding those responsible for serious violations of international law accountable is theatre.
Recognition must also be accompanied by serious efforts to protect Palestinian rights, end unlawful settlement activity, support reconstruction and ensure that Palestinians have a say in the future of their own natural resources, including Gaza Marine.
So answer this:
1.Will you review or stop arms transfers where there is a clear risk that weapons could be used to commit serious violations of international humanitarian law?
2.Will you take action against violent settlers? Will you use your influence to help end the occupation and support the rebuilding of Gaza? Will you support accountability for serious crimes, regardless of who commits them?
Or will you simply recognise Palestine on paper, take a photograph, post it on Instagram and return to silence?
The Pawns in Gaza, the Pawns in the West Bank, the Pawns in #Lagos, London and Sydney are watching.
And they know the difference between justice and saving face.
Justice speaks even when it is dangerous. Saving face speaks when it is safe.
In 2023, it was politically difficult in some places to say, "Free Palestine."
In 2025, it became politically possible for more Western governments to say, "We recognise Palestine."
That is the difference.
That is the story The Chess Board wants to examine.

WHO BENEFITS? WHO PAYS?

If you are a Palestinian child in Gaza, you do not care about Gaza Marine or Leviathan. You care about bread, water and school.
If you are an Israeli child in Tel Aviv, you do not care about Chevron or Exxon. You care about safety, school and not having to run to a bunker.
If you are an American child in Ohio, you do not care about West Asia. You care about the price of petrol, rent and school.
All children are Pawns. All are at risk of being sacrificed for the King.
We care about Palestinian people, Israeli people and American people. They all want peace, bread, education and a safe place to call home.
What we oppose is a system that divides Palestinians into Fatah and Hamas, allows rival political interests to deepen that division, and leaves ordinary people paying the price.
We question the financial arrangements involving Qatar, the blockade and restrictions affecting the Palestinian Authority, the Hannibal Directive, allegations of delayed military response on October 7, and the use of the October 7 attack to justify a devastating military campaign in Gaza.
We also question the wider struggle over Gaza Marine gas and the control of energy resources across West Asia.
These are difficult questions about power, responsibility and accountability. They deserve evidence-based investigation, not automatic assumptions.
We support only one side: the helpless victims – children in Gaza,  in Be'eri, and mothers in the West Bank – who never chose to become pieces in this geopolitical chess game.

#DISCLAIMER
This is an educational, political and historical analysis presented through a chess analogy on publicly available 7 verified records

Today in Dutse, we had the distinct honor of welcoming our leader, President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, GCFR (@officialABAT), alongside Vice President Kashim Shettima @officialSKSM (GCON), to Jigawa State, for the APC 2027 presidential campaign rally.

Seeing the mammoth crowd of party faithful and citizens that filled the campaign ground was deeply humbling.  Joined by the APC National Chairman Professor Nentawe Yilwatda (@nentawe1), Speaker of the House of Representatives Rt Hon. Abbas Tajudeen, GCON (@Speaker_Abbas), Deputy Senate President Senator Barau Jibrin GCON (@barauijibrin), and Governors from across the north, sent an unmistakable message: Jigawa remains firmly anchored in the Renewed Hope agenda.

What made today truly special for us, however, was what we did before the rallies began.

We brought Mr. President face-to-face with our commitment to human capital development and food security. He commissioned the Renewed Hope Technical Services Centre and the Bola Ahmed Tinubu Multipurpose Skills Acquisition Centre—two institutions designed to equip our vibrant youth with market-ready, future-proof skills.

Even more exciting was the official rollout of the Jigawa State Farm Mechanisation Service Company’s fleet. Agriculture is the livelihood of our state, and today we backed that with serious hardware: 400 Tractors & Implements, 150 Multipurpose Planters, 150 Rice Seeders, 80 Boom Sprayers, and 60 Combine Harvesters

We are moving Jigawa away from rudimentary, manual labour toward industrialized, agriculture that guarantees prosperity for our farmers.

My profound gratitude goes to Mr President, our distinguished guests, and, most importantly, the wonderful people of Jigawa who came out in their hundreds of thousands. 

We will continue to build, empower, and deliver, In Sha Allah.

text:
STATE HOUSE PRESS RELEASE 

President Tinubu's Massive Security, Infrastructure Boom Igniting South-East Economy — VP Shettima 

...Seeks renewed mandate for President, says democracy is a debt of honour repayable through service 

...Receives traditional title, Aka Ekpuchi Ọnwa, as state pledges 80% of votes for President's re-election 

The Vice President, Senator Kashim Shettima, has said the administration of President Bola Ahmed Tinubu is engineering a seismic economic and security shift in the South-East through aggressive capital injections into transport, green energy, agriculture, housing and human capital development. 

He said the Federal Government's interventions in Ebonyi State and the wider South-East are designed to improve regional connectivity, strengthen food security, expand economic opportunities and address longstanding development challenges that have constrained the region's economic potential. 

Speaking on Monday during the All Progressives Congress (APC) presidential campaign rally in Abakaliki, Ebonyi State, Senator Shettima said the Tinubu administration had demonstrated its commitment to the state through major infrastructure projects, federal appointments and policies aimed at improving the welfare of citizens. 

"This campaign has been a season of triumph. We have triumphed over the falsehoods of our opponents. We have triumphed over those who mistook the limits of their imagination for the limits of our reach. We have never turned our backs on you. We have answered your support with projects and His Excellency, President Bola Ahmed Tinubu has honoured Ebonyi through distinguished appointments and projects across the state," he said. 

The Vice President maintained that the administration's development programmes reflect its determination to honour the confidence reposed in it by Nigerians, stressing that public office imposes an obligation to deliver measurable improvements in people's lives. 

"If any state can speak with confidence about the dividends of democracy, it is Ebonyi. You have stood by us. You have assured us that a mandate is a debt of honour, repayable only through service. Yet democracy demands the humility of asking again. We have returned to seek the renewal of your mandate, to serve you, to defend you, and to stand by you," he said. 

Highlighting ongoing infrastructure investments, VP Shettima identified the Calabar–Ebonyi–Benue–Kogi–Nasarawa–Abuja Superhighway, which forms part of the administration's Trans-Saharan highway vision, as a major project intended to strengthen trade and economic integration between the South-East, North-Central and other parts of the country. 

He also listed the Ndibe Bridge, designed to improve connectivity between Ebonyi and Cross River states, as well as ongoing work on the Enugu–Abakaliki–Ogoja Expressway and the Okposi–Ohaozara–Ukawu–Cross River road. 

"Where shall we begin the account of our work? Shall we begin with the Calabar–Ebonyi–Benue–Kogi–Nasarawa–Abuja Superhighway, part of our Trans-Saharan highway vision? Or with the Ndibe Bridge, which will link Ebonyi with Cross River? We are advancing work on the Enugu–Abakaliki–Ogoja Expressway and the Okposi–Ohaozara–Ukawu–Cross River road. Again, I ask: where shall we begin?" he stated. 

The Vice President explained that the road projects would improve the movement of agricultural produce, manufactured goods and other commodities while reducing the logistical barriers facing businesses and communities across the region. 

Turning to agriculture, VP Shettima described Ebonyi as an important contributor to Nigeria's food security, particularly through rice and cassava production, noting that the administration is supporting farmers with fertiliser distribution, interest-free FarmerMoni assistance and other agricultural development programmes. 

He said investments in rural roads are equally important to agricultural productivity, as improved access to markets would help farmers reduce losses, increase earnings and expand production. 

The Vice President further disclosed that thousands of beneficiaries in Ebonyi State had received grants under the Presidential Conditional Grant Scheme, while federal employment and digital skills initiatives were creating opportunities for young people to acquire relevant skills and establish sustainable livelihoods. 

On security, Senator Shettima said President Tinubu's administration had intensified efforts to restore stability across the South-East, stressing that lasting economic development depends on the safety of communities, businesses and critical infrastructure. 

He identified the establishment and commencement of operations at the Nigerian Army Recruits Training Depot at Amasiri–Edda in Ebonyi State as one of the Federal Government's security interventions in the region. 

"The security of the South-East has changed since President Bola Ahmed Tinubu became Commander-in-Chief over three years ago. We have worked to restore order, and we will keep working," he assured. 

The Vice President also noted the establishment of the South East Development Commission, the launch of the South-East Vision 2050 and the approval of the South East Investment Company as major institutional initiatives intended to accelerate regional development, attract investment and create sustainable economic opportunities. 

He said these interventions recognise the relationship between security, economic inclusion and long-term stability, adding that the Federal Government remains committed to addressing the structural challenges affecting the South-East. 

Commending Ebonyi State Governor, Francis Ogbonna Nwifuru, the Vice President said improved federal revenue allocations have strengthened the capacity of state governments to invest in infrastructure and essential public services. 

He praised Governor Nwifuru for deploying the state's increased resources towards development projects, describing his administration's efforts as a demonstration of responsible stewardship. 

VP Shettima urged the people of Ebonyi State to renew their support for President Tinubu and the APC in the 2027 general elections, maintaining that the administration had established the foundation for further economic progress and national development. 

He thanked the people of Ebonyi State for their continued support and urged them to stand by President Tinubu, Governor Nwifuru and the APC in the forthcoming elections. 

In their separate remarks at the rally, Ebonyi State Governor, Francis Ogbonna Nwifuru; former APC National Chairman, Senator Adams Oshiomhole; and Minister of Works, Senator David Umahi, commended President Tinubu's economic reforms and infrastructure investments, urging the people of the state to renew their support for the administration in the 2027 general elections. 

Governor Nwifuru reaffirmed the state's support for President Tinubu, saying Ebonyi had benefited significantly from the administration's economic reforms and special interventions in road infrastructure. 

"Under President Tinubu, the poor roads in our state and zone are now better. We now enjoy special road interventions," he said. 

The governor, however, appealed to the Federal Government to support the provision of a 330kV electricity transmission line to improve power supply across Ebonyi State. 

Stressing the importance of reliable electricity to industrial development and economic growth, he assured President Tinubu that the state would deliver 80 percent of its votes to him in the 2027 presidential election. 

Also speaking, the Minister of Works, Senator Umahi, described the massive turnout at the rally as a demonstration of Ebonyi State's support for the APC and President Tinubu. 

He thanked the President for what he described as unprecedented federal investments in road infrastructure across the state, involving hundreds of kilometres of highways and billions of naira in funding. 

Senator Umahi further urged the people of Ebonyi State to sustain their support for the Tinubu–Shettima administration, expressing confidence that the state would deliver 1.3 million votes to the President in the forthcoming election. 

Earlier, on arrival in Abakaliki, the Vice President paid a courtesy visit to His Royal Highness, Eze Fidelis Nwonumara, Eze Nnodo II of Amagu Autonomous Community in Abakaliki and Chairman of the Izzi/Nnodo Traditional Rulers Council, where he was conferred with the traditional chieftaincy title, Aka Ekpuchi Ọnwa, meaning "A Hand Cannot Cover the Moon." 

The title, drawn from an Igbo proverb, symbolises the enduring power of truth, integrity and greatness, conveying the belief that genuine merit and distinguished service cannot be concealed or diminished. 

The conferment celebrated the Vice President's public service and the longstanding bonds of friendship between the people of Northern Nigeria and the South-East. 

Expressing gratitude to the monarch and the traditional rulers, VP Shettima described the honour as a personal responsibility to deepen his relationship with Ebonyi State and strengthen national unity. 

He recalled the historic ties of trade, friendship and shared community life between the North and the South-East, noting that Nigeria's diversity remains one of its greatest strengths. 

"I have travelled from the far North-East to the South-East, yet I stand here among brothers and sisters. Our ancestors understood that friendship could cross rivers, mountains and kingdoms. They knew that a stranger who is received with love soon becomes a member of the household. This is the Nigeria we must preserve," he stated.

Stanley Nkwocha
Senior Special Assistant to the President on Media & Communications
(Office of the Vice President)
November 9, 2026
